title: 13.11 The non-pluripolar products
text:
The proofs of the standard results recalled in this section can be found in [ BEGZ10 ] . Let $X$ be a complex manifold. Definition 13.11.1 . 1A52175C3D64 Let $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. We set \[  O_ k \coloneqq \bigcap _{j=1}^ p \{ \varphi _ j>-k\} ,\quad k\in \mathbb {N}.  \] We say that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined if for each connected open subset $U\subseteq X$, any smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $U$, and each compact subset $K\subseteq U$, we have 826BE13A141D 13.11.2 \begin{equation}  \sup _{k\geq 0} \int _{K\cap O_ k}\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ j\lor (-k))\right)\right|_ U\wedge \omega ^{\dim U-p}<\infty . \end{equation} In this case, we define the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ by 63B22DDAC51C 13.11.3 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{O_ k}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p=\mathds {1}_{O_ k}\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \varphi _ j\lor (-k)\right) \end{equation} on $\bigcup _{k\geq 0} O_ k$ and extend it by zero to $X$. As recalled in section 5.15 , an $\mathcal{F}$-open subset means an open subset with respect to the plurifine topology. Proposition 13.11.4 . 9E81D36B1290 Let $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. 4C9D393253D0 The product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is local with respect to the plurifine topology in the following sense: Let $O\subseteq X$ be an $\mathcal{F}$-open subset and $\psi _1,\ldots ,\psi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. Assume that \[  \varphi _ j|_{O}=\psi _ j|_{O},\quad j=1,\ldots ,p,  \] and that \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\textup{ and } \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j  \] are both well-defined, then C3F3FF3F504B 13.11.5 \begin{equation}  \left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j\right)\right|_{O}. \end{equation} If furthermore $O$ is open in the usual topology, then the product \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{O}  \] on $O$ is well-defined and 7E91D53462AC 13.11.6 \begin{equation}  \left. \left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{O}. \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{U}$ be an open covering of $X$. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined if and only if each product \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{U},\quad U\in \mathcal{U}.  \] 13DFC0FA2988 The current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ and the fact that it is well-defined depend only on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$, not on the choice of the $\varphi _ j$'s nor on the ordering of the $\varphi _ j$'s. 1353BEBCB3BB When $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in L^{\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$, the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined and is equal to the Bedford–Taylor product. More generally, if $q\leq p$, and we only assume that $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ q\in L^{\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$, and that the non-pluripolar product $T\coloneqq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _{q+1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined, then the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is also well-defined, and is equal to the Bedford–Taylor product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ q\wedge T$ as in 13.10.2 . F4627B44F775 Assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ puts no mass on pluripolar sets. 90ED277A28AD Assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined. Then $\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ is a closed positive $(p,p)$-current on $X$. 1 87188EAC5CDB The product is multilinear: Let $\psi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$, $a,b>0$ then A1F77BA03A26 13.11.7 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\varphi _1+b\psi _1)\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j =a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j + b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \end{equation} in the sense that the left-hand side is well-defined if and only if both terms on the right-hand side are well-defined, and the equality holds in that case. 1. ↩ This current is in fact strongly positive, as shown in [ Xiabdiv2 ] . Proof. For bounded potentials, Bedford--Taylor plurifine locality identifies their products on every plurifine open set on which the potentials agree. Apply it to the bounded truncations $\max\{\varphi_j,-k\}$ and $\max\{\psi_j,-k\}$, on the intersection of $O$ with the finite-level loci of all the potentials. The truncated products agree there. Let $k\to\infty$ in the increasing restriction measures defining the non-pluripolar product. The omitted pole sets have zero mass by construction, so equality holds on all of $O$. This limiting argument, including invariance under changes of local potentials, is established in the local calculus of non-pluripolar products . In view of 3 , we do not need to specify whether our product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is the Bedford–Taylor product or the non-pluripolar product when the $\varphi _ i$'s are all locally bounded. Example 13.11.8 . 00950EDCBA2C Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$, then 9F35F663186D 13.11.9 \begin{equation}  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi . \end{equation} Here $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1$ on the left-hand side denotes the non-pluripolar product, while $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ on the right-hand side denotes the usual derivative in the sense of current. The problem is local, so we may assume that $X=\Delta ^ n$, the unit polydisk in $\mathbb {C}^ n$. Take $f\in C^{\infty }_ c(\Delta ^ n)$ with $f\geq 0$. We need to show that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _{\Delta ^ n} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-k\} }f\,  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\bigl (\varphi \lor (-k)\bigr )\wedge \omega ^{n-1}=\int _{\Delta ^ n} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }f\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \omega ^{n-1},  \] where $\omega $ is the standard Kähler form on $\mathbb {C}^ n$. By the dominated convergence theorem, this reduces immediately to the $1$-dimensional case: \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _{\Delta ^1} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-k\} }f\,  \Delta \bigl (\varphi \lor (-k)\bigr )=\int _{\Delta ^1} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }f\, \Delta \varphi ,  \] for any subharmonic function $\varphi $ on the unit disk $\Delta ^1$, which is a special case of [ Proposition 3.3 , EK24 ] . Definition 13.11.10 . 05C17B17762F Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. We say that $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ is well-defined if there exists an open covering $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ such that on each $U\in \mathcal{U}$, we can find $\varphi _ j^ U\in \mathrm{PSH}(U)$ ($j=1,\ldots ,p$) such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j^ U=T_ j,\quad j=1,\ldots ,p  \] and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ U\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p^ U$ is well-defined. In this case, we define the non-pluripolar product $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ as the closed positive $(p,p)$-current on $X$ defined by 3FE189D717D7 13.11.11 \begin{equation}  \left(T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\right)|_ U=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ U\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p^ U,\quad U\in \mathcal{U}. \end{equation} The product $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ is independent of the choices we made thanks to proposition 13.11.4 1 and 2 . proposition 13.11.4 can be formulated in terms of currents without any difficulty. Remark 13.11.12 . 76807540FC41 Similar to 13.10.2 , there is also an extension of the non-pluripolar theory allowing us to define \[  T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\cap T  \] for any closed positive current $T$. This is the relative non-pluripolar product defined above. Unlike the relative Bedford–Taylor products, the relative non-pluripolar products present some pathological behaviors. For example, they are not linear in general. Remark 13.11.13 . 873B08B81AC9 Another possible generalization of the non-pluripolar products is motivated by proposition 13.11.4 1 . One could begin by defining a generalized notion of plurisubharmonic functions on $\mathcal{F}$-open sets, called $\mathcal{F}$-plurisubharmonic functions and define their non-pluripolar products. See [ EKFW11 , EKW14 ] . Proposition 13.11.14 . FB457F67F566 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ is well-defined. Proof. Write $T_j=\theta_j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm c}\varphi_j$ by the global potential lemma, and fix a Kähler form $\omega$. Choose $C$ so large that every $\tau_j=\theta_j+C\omega$ is semipositive. The compact mass estimate proves
\[\int_X\langle T_1\wedge\cdots\wedge T_p\rangle\wedge\omega^{n-p}\leq\int_X\tau_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\tau_p\wedge\omega^{n-p}<\infty.\]
Thus the increasing restricted truncation measures have locally finite coefficient measures. The construction therefore defines a current everywhere; closedness of the truncation limit and the local-calculus theorem show that it is independent of the chosen potentials and patches between charts. Compactness and the Kähler form are used in the displayed uniform mass bound. This proposition explains why we usually work in the setting of compact Kähler manifolds. Corollary 13.11.15 . AE7DB6D35BE9 Let $X$ and $Z$ be connected compact Kähler manifolds of dimensions $n$ and $m$, respectively, and let $p_1\colon X\times Z\to X$ and $p_2\colon X\times Z\to Z$ be the projections. Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $\gamma $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $Z$. Put \[  Y=X\times Z,\qquad \Theta =p_1^*\theta +p_2^*\gamma ,\qquad \Phi =p_1^*\phi .  \] Suppose that $W\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\Theta )$ and $\Phi -C\leq W\leq \Phi +C$ for some $C>0$. Set \[  T=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}W,\qquad S=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi ,  \] and write $W_ z(x)=W(x,z)$. Then $W_ z\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for every $z\in Z$. For $0\leq j\leq n$ and every smooth real $(m,m)$-form $\eta $ on $Z$, 091EC34E5A75 13.11.16 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned} & \int _ Y(W-\Phi )p_2^*\eta \wedge T^ j\wedge S^{n-j}\\ & \qquad =\int _ Z\left(\int _ X(W_ z-\phi )\,  \theta _{W_ z}^ j\wedge \theta _\phi ^{n-j}\right)\eta (z), \end{aligned} \end{equation} and 8D9958903619 13.11.17 \begin{equation}  \int _ Y p_2^*\eta \wedge T^ n =\int _ Z\left(\int _ X\theta _{W_ z}^ n\right)\eta (z). \end{equation} Proof. By linearity, it suffices to consider $\eta \geq 0$. All the non-pluripolar products that occur below are well-defined by proposition 13.11.14 . We work on a relatively compact product chart $Q\times D\subseteq X\times Z$ and let $a$ and $b$ be smooth local potentials of $p_1^*\theta $ and $p_2^*\gamma $. After subtracting constants, put $w=W+a+b\leq 0$ and $f=\Phi +a+b\leq 0$. For $k\geq 1$, set \[  \begin{aligned}  w_ k& =w\lor (-k),&  f_ k& =f\lor (-k),\\  O_ k& =\{ w>-k\} \cap \{ f>-k\} ,&  \mu _{j,k}& =\mathds {1}_{O_ k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ k)^ j\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ k)^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] For $z\in D$, write $w_ z(x)=w(x,z)$ and $f_ z(x)=f(x,z)$, and set \[  \mu _{j,k,z} =\mathds {1}_{\{ w_ z>-k\} \cap \{ f_ z>-k\} } \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x(w_ z\lor (-k))\bigr )^ j\wedge \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x(f_ z\lor (-k))\bigr )^{n-j}.  \] Apply 13.10.5 with $u_1=\cdots =u_ j=w_ k$, $u_{j+1}=\cdots =u_ n=f_ k$, and \[  h=\rho G\mathds {1}_{O_ k},\qquad \rho \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty }_ c(Q\times D),\quad \rho \geq 0,  \] where $G$ is any bounded non-negative Borel function. This gives 32D177AC1071 13.11.18 \begin{equation}  \int _{Q\times D}\rho G\, p_2^*\eta \wedge \mu _{j,k} =\int _ D\left(\int _ Q\rho _ zG_ z\, \mu _{j,k,z}\right)\eta (z). \end{equation} By plurifine locality, $\mu _{j,k}$ increases to the local expression of $T^ j\wedge S^{n-j}$, while, for every $z\in D$, $\mu _{j,k,z}$ increases to the local expression of $\theta _{W_ z}^ j\wedge \theta _\phi ^{n-j}$. Taking $G=\delta +C\geq 0$ in ( 13.11.18 ), applying monotone convergence, subtracting the corresponding constant-weight identity, and summing over a non-negative partition of unity proves ( 13.11.16 ). The same argument with constant weight and degree $n$ proves ( 13.11.17 ). $\square$

title: Definition 13.11.1
text: Definition 13.11.1 . 1A52175C3D64 Let $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. We set \[  O_ k \coloneqq \bigcap _{j=1}^ p \{ \varphi _ j>-k\} ,\quad k\in \mathbb {N}.  \] We say that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined if for each connected open subset $U\subseteq X$, any smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $U$, and each compact subset $K\subseteq U$, we have 826BE13A141D 13.11.2 \begin{equation}  \sup _{k\geq 0} \int _{K\cap O_ k}\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ j\lor (-k))\right)\right|_ U\wedge \omega ^{\dim U-p}<\infty . \end{equation} In this case, we define the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ by 63B22DDAC51C 13.11.3 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{O_ k}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p=\mathds {1}_{O_ k}\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \varphi _ j\lor (-k)\right) \end{equation} on $\bigcup _{k\geq 0} O_ k$ and extend it by zero to $X$.

title: Equation 13.11.2
text: 826BE13A141D 13.11.2 \begin{equation}  \sup _{k\geq 0} \int _{K\cap O_ k}\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ j\lor (-k))\right)\right|_ U\wedge \omega ^{\dim U-p}<\infty . \end{equation}

title: Equation 13.11.3
text: 63B22DDAC51C 13.11.3 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{O_ k}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p=\mathds {1}_{O_ k}\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \varphi _ j\lor (-k)\right) \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.11.4
text: Proposition 13.11.4 . 9E81D36B1290 Let $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. 4C9D393253D0 The product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is local with respect to the plurifine topology in the following sense: Let $O\subseteq X$ be an $\mathcal{F}$-open subset and $\psi _1,\ldots ,\psi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. Assume that \[  \varphi _ j|_{O}=\psi _ j|_{O},\quad j=1,\ldots ,p,  \] and that \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\textup{ and } \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j  \] are both well-defined, then C3F3FF3F504B 13.11.5 \begin{equation}  \left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j\right)\right|_{O}. \end{equation} If furthermore $O$ is open in the usual topology, then the product \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{O}  \] on $O$ is well-defined and 7E91D53462AC 13.11.6 \begin{equation}  \left. \left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{O}. \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{U}$ be an open covering of $X$. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined if and only if each product \[  \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{U},\quad U\in \mathcal{U}.  \] 13DFC0FA2988 The current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ and the fact that it is well-defined depend only on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$, not on the choice of the $\varphi _ j$'s nor on the ordering of the $\varphi _ j$'s. 1353BEBCB3BB When $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in L^{\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$, the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined and is equal to the Bedford–Taylor product. More generally, if $q\leq p$, and we only assume that $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ q\in L^{\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$, and that the non-pluripolar product $T\coloneqq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _{q+1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined, then the non-pluripolar product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is also well-defined, and is equal to the Bedford–Taylor product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ q\wedge T$ as in 13.10.2 . F4627B44F775 Assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ puts no mass on pluripolar sets. 90ED277A28AD Assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p$ is well-defined. Then $\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ is a closed positive $(p,p)$-current on $X$. 1 87188EAC5CDB The product is multilinear: Let $\psi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$, $a,b>0$ then A1F77BA03A26 13.11.7 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\varphi _1+b\psi _1)\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j =a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j + b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \end{equation} in the sense that the left-hand side is well-defined if and only if both terms on the right-hand side are well-defined, and the equality holds in that case. 1. ↩ This current is in fact strongly positive, as shown in [ Xiabdiv2 ] . Proof. For bounded potentials, Bedford--Taylor plurifine locality identifies their products on every plurifine open set on which the potentials agree. Apply it to the bounded truncations $\max\{\varphi_j,-k\}$ and $\max\{\psi_j,-k\}$, on the intersection of $O$ with the finite-level loci of all the potentials. The truncated products agree there. Let $k\to\infty$ in the increasing restriction measures defining the non-pluripolar product. The omitted pole sets have zero mass by construction, so equality holds on all of $O$. This limiting argument, including invariance under changes of local potentials, is established in the local calculus of non-pluripolar products .

title: Equation 13.11.5
text: C3F3FF3F504B 13.11.5 \begin{equation}  \left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\left.\left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j\right)\right|_{O}. \end{equation}

title: Equation 13.11.6
text: 7E91D53462AC 13.11.6 \begin{equation}  \left. \left(\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)\right|_{O}=\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_{O}. \end{equation}

title: Equation 13.11.7
text: A1F77BA03A26 13.11.7 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\varphi _1+b\psi _1)\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j =a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j + b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1\wedge \bigwedge _{j=2}^ p \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \end{equation}

title: Example 13.11.8
text: Example 13.11.8 . 00950EDCBA2C Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$, then 9F35F663186D 13.11.9 \begin{equation}  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi . \end{equation} Here $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1$ on the left-hand side denotes the non-pluripolar product, while $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ on the right-hand side denotes the usual derivative in the sense of current. The problem is local, so we may assume that $X=\Delta ^ n$, the unit polydisk in $\mathbb {C}^ n$. Take $f\in C^{\infty }_ c(\Delta ^ n)$ with $f\geq 0$. We need to show that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _{\Delta ^ n} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-k\} }f\,  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\bigl (\varphi \lor (-k)\bigr )\wedge \omega ^{n-1}=\int _{\Delta ^ n} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }f\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \omega ^{n-1},  \] where $\omega $ is the standard Kähler form on $\mathbb {C}^ n$. By the dominated convergence theorem, this reduces immediately to the $1$-dimensional case: \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _{\Delta ^1} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-k\} }f\,  \Delta \bigl (\varphi \lor (-k)\bigr )=\int _{\Delta ^1} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }f\, \Delta \varphi ,  \] for any subharmonic function $\varphi $ on the unit disk $\Delta ^1$, which is a special case of [ Proposition 3.3 , EK24 ] .

title: Equation 13.11.9
text: 9F35F663186D 13.11.9 \begin{equation}  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >-\infty \} }\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi . \end{equation}

title: Definition 13.11.10
text: Definition 13.11.10 . 05C17B17762F Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. We say that $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ is well-defined if there exists an open covering $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ such that on each $U\in \mathcal{U}$, we can find $\varphi _ j^ U\in \mathrm{PSH}(U)$ ($j=1,\ldots ,p$) such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j^ U=T_ j,\quad j=1,\ldots ,p  \] and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ U\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p^ U$ is well-defined. In this case, we define the non-pluripolar product $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ as the closed positive $(p,p)$-current on $X$ defined by 3FE189D717D7 13.11.11 \begin{equation}  \left(T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\right)|_ U=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ U\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p^ U,\quad U\in \mathcal{U}. \end{equation}

title: Equation 13.11.11
text: 3FE189D717D7 13.11.11 \begin{equation}  \left(T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\right)|_ U=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ U\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p^ U,\quad U\in \mathcal{U}. \end{equation}

title: Remark 13.11.12
text: Remark 13.11.12 . 76807540FC41 Similar to 13.10.2 , there is also an extension of the non-pluripolar theory allowing us to define \[  T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\cap T  \] for any closed positive current $T$. This is the relative non-pluripolar product defined above. Unlike the relative Bedford–Taylor products, the relative non-pluripolar products present some pathological behaviors. For example, they are not linear in general.

title: Remark 13.11.13
text: Remark 13.11.13 . 873B08B81AC9 Another possible generalization of the non-pluripolar products is motivated by proposition 13.11.4 1 . One could begin by defining a generalized notion of plurisubharmonic functions on $\mathcal{F}$-open sets, called $\mathcal{F}$-plurisubharmonic functions and define their non-pluripolar products. See [ EKFW11 , EKW14 ] .

title: Proposition 13.11.14
text:
Proposition 13.11.14 . FB457F67F566 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then $T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p$ is well-defined. Proof. Write $T_j=\theta_j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm c}\varphi_j$ by the global potential lemma, and fix a Kähler form $\omega$. Choose $C$ so large that every $\tau_j=\theta_j+C\omega$ is semipositive. title: Corollary 13.11.15
text: Corollary 13.11.15 . AE7DB6D35BE9 Let $X$ and $Z$ be connected compact Kähler manifolds of dimensions $n$ and $m$, respectively, and let $p_1\colon X\times Z\to X$ and $p_2\colon X\times Z\to Z$ be the projections. Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $\gamma $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $Z$. Put \[  Y=X\times Z,\qquad \Theta =p_1^*\theta +p_2^*\gamma ,\qquad \Phi =p_1^*\phi .  \] Suppose that $W\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\Theta )$ and $\Phi -C\leq W\leq \Phi +C$ for some $C>0$. Set \[  T=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}W,\qquad S=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi ,  \] and write $W_ z(x)=W(x,z)$. Then $W_ z\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for every $z\in Z$. For $0\leq j\leq n$ and every smooth real $(m,m)$-form $\eta $ on $Z$, 091EC34E5A75 13.11.16 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned} & \int _ Y(W-\Phi )p_2^*\eta \wedge T^ j\wedge S^{n-j}\\ & \qquad =\int _ Z\left(\int _ X(W_ z-\phi )\,  \theta _{W_ z}^ j\wedge \theta _\phi ^{n-j}\right)\eta (z), \end{aligned} \end{equation} and 8D9958903619 13.11.17 \begin{equation}  \int _ Y p_2^*\eta \wedge T^ n =\int _ Z\left(\int _ X\theta _{W_ z}^ n\right)\eta (z). \end{equation} Proof. For $k\geq 1$, set \[  \begin{aligned}  w_ k& =w\lor (-k),&  f_ k& =f\lor (-k),\\  O_ k& =\{ w>-k\} \cap \{ f>-k\} ,&  \mu _{j,k}& =\mathds {1}_{O_ k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ k)^ j\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ k)^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] For $z\in D$, write $w_ z(x)=w(x,z)$ and $f_ z(x)=f(x,z)$, and set \[  \mu _{j,k,z} =\mathds {1}_{\{ w_ z>-k\} \cap \{ f_ z>-k\} } \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x(w_ z\lor (-k))\bigr )^ j\wedge \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x(f_ z\lor (-k))\bigr )^{n-j}.  \] Apply 13.10.5 with $u_1=\cdots =u_ j=w_ k$, $u_{j+1}=\cdots =u_ n=f_ k$, and \[  h=\rho G\mathds {1}_{O_ k},\qquad \rho \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty }_ c(Q\times D),\quad \rho \geq 0,  \] where $G$ is any bounded non-negative Borel function. title: 13.12 Quasi-continuous functions
text:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Definition 13.12.1 . C96BE5099B6A Let $A\subseteq X$ be a Borel subset. The $\theta $-capacity $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)$ of $A$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \int _ A\theta _{\varphi }^ n : \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),V_{\theta }-1\leq \varphi \leq V_{\theta } \right\} .  \] Here $V_{\theta }$ is defined in ( 13.13.7 ) below. As we will recall below, the non-pluripolar product $\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ is well-defined. 


The capacity is not very sensitive to the choice of $\theta $: Theorem 13.12.2 . C5C10F2AB708 Let $\theta '$ be another closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Then there are continuous functions $f,g\colon [0,\infty )\rightarrow [0,\infty )$, with $f(0)=g(0)=0$, such that for any Borel subset $E\subseteq X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(E)\leq f\left( \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta '}(E)\right),\quad \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta '}(E)\leq g\left( \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(E)\right).  \] Proof. Use the comparison with Kähler capacity with the reference potentials defining $\operatorname{Cap}_\theta$ and $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}$. It gives continuous nondecreasing functions $F,G,F',G'$, all zero at zero, with
\[\operatorname{Cap}_\theta\leq F\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\omega,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_\omega\leq G\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\theta,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}\leq F'\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\omega,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_\omega\leq G'\circ\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}.\]
The reference potentials have positive mass because the classes are big. Set $f=F\circ G'$ and $g=F'\circ G$. Composing the respective inequalities proves the two assertions for every Borel set. The compositions are continuous and vanish at zero, as required. A more general result is proved in [ Lu21 ] . Similar comparison results hold between $\theta $-capacity and the classical Bedford–Taylor capacity, see [ Section 9.2 , GZ17 ] for the proof. As a consequence, we can freely apply the results in [ Section 4.2 , GZ17 ] , even though capacity has a different meaning there. Definition 13.12.3 . BA13EE505D9B Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. A function $f\colon U\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous if it is Borel measurable and for any $\epsilon >0$, there is an open subset $G\subseteq U$ such that E9A5229B982B $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(G)\leq \epsilon $; EC64A29E7BCB $f|_{U\setminus G}$ is real-valued and continuous. Thanks to theorem 13.12.2 , the notion of quasi-continuous functions is independent of the choice of $\theta $. Note that if $f,g\colon U\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ are two Borel measurable functions equal quasi-everywhere (see definition 5.47.2 ), then $f$ is quasi-continuous if and only if $g$ is. Theorem 13.12.4 . 9F9E57CC1422 Let $A\subseteq X$ be a Borel set. Then the following are equivalent: 9860890C10B2 $A$ is pluripolar; 0031AD934DC8 $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)=0$. Proof. By capacity comparison , zero $\theta$-capacity is equivalent to zero Kähler capacity. The comparison with coordinate-ball capacities makes this equivalent to zero local Bedford--Taylor capacity in every member of a finite coordinate cover. The local zero-capacity theorem identifies these zero sets with the pluripolar sets. This proves both implications. For a Borel set, one may first apply the local statement to compact subsets and then use the capacitability and zero-capacity characterization proved with that theorem; a mere measure-zero argument would not suffice. See [ Theorem 4.40 , GZ17 ] for the proof. Example 13.12.5 . 472C675FCEA8 A quasi-plurisubharmonic function on an open subset $U\subseteq X$ is always quasi-continuous. See [ Theorem 4.20 , GZ17 ] for the proof. More generally, if $\varphi ,\psi $ are two quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $U$, then the following function \[  f(x)\coloneqq \begin{cases}  \varphi (x)-\psi (x),& \textup{if }(\varphi \lor \psi )(x)\neq -\infty ;\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise} \end{cases}  \] is quasi-continuous. 2 2. ↩ In the literature, people usually say carelessly that $\varphi -\psi $ is quasi-continuous. Definition 13.12.6 . F7490AE48EAC Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. Let $(f_ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net of Borel measurable functions $f_ i\colon U\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$, and $f\colon U\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a Borel measurable function. We say $(f_ i)_{i\in I}$ converges to $f$ in capacity if for any $\delta >0$, we have \[  \lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }\Bigl ( \{ f_ i>f+\delta \}  \Bigr )=0,\quad \lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }\Bigl ( \{ f_ i<f-\delta \}  \Bigr )=0{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000011932}{3}}.  \] We sometimes write $f_ i\xrightarrow {\mathrm{C}} f$. 3. ↩ It is very tempting to write $\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }\left( \{ |f_ i-f|>\delta \}  \right)=0$. But the set where $f_ i-f$ is not defined is not a pluripolar set in general. Hence this abuse of notation is not acceptable. Note that $f$ is not uniquely determined by the net $(f_ i)_{i\in I}$. Thanks to theorem 13.12.2 , the notion of convergence in capacity is independent of the choice of $\theta $. Proposition 13.12.7 . D56D6D4A5E94 Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(U,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(U,\theta )$. Assume one of the following conditions holds: 11DA1A704FF9 $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is decreasing and $\varphi $ is the limit of the net; C18393916362 $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is increasing and converges almost everywhere to $\varphi $. Then $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ converges to $\varphi $ in capacity. See [ Proposition 4.25 , GZ17 ] for the proof. The reference concerns only the sequence case, but the proof works for nets as well. Theorem 13.12.8 . 272876B00528 Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. Let $(\chi _ i\colon U\rightarrow [0,\infty ))_ i$ be a sequence of quasi-continuous functions. Assume that the sequence is uniformly bounded and converges in capacity to $\chi \colon U\rightarrow [0,\infty )$. For each $j=1,\ldots ,p$, let $(\varphi _ j^ i)_ i$ be uniformly bounded sequences in $\mathrm{PSH}(U,\theta _ j)$ converging in capacity to bounded $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(U,\theta _ j)$. Then \[  \chi _ i\, \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \theta _{j,\varphi _ j^ i}\rightharpoonup \chi \, \bigwedge _{j=1}^ p \theta _{j,\varphi _ j}  \] weakly as currents on $U$. See [ Theorem 4.26 , GZ17 ] 1 . 1. ↩ In the displayed formula in the statement of [ Theorem 4.26 , GZ17 ] , $1\leq j\leq p$ should be $1\leq i\leq p$ on both sides.

title: Definition 13.12.1
text: Definition 13.12.1 . C96BE5099B6A Let $A\subseteq X$ be a Borel subset. The $\theta $-capacity $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)$ of $A$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \int _ A\theta _{\varphi }^ n : \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),V_{\theta }-1\leq \varphi \leq V_{\theta } \right\} .  \]

title: Theorem 13.12.2
text:
Theorem 13.12.2 . C5C10F2AB708 Let $\theta '$ be another closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Then there are continuous functions $f,g\colon [0,\infty )\rightarrow [0,\infty )$, with $f(0)=g(0)=0$, such that for any Borel subset $E\subseteq X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(E)\leq f\left( \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta '}(E)\right),\quad \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta '}(E)\leq g\left( \operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(E)\right).  \] Proof. Use the comparison with Kähler capacity with the reference potentials defining $\operatorname{Cap}_\theta$ and $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}$. It gives continuous nondecreasing functions $F,G,F',G'$, all zero at zero, with
\[\operatorname{Cap}_\theta\leq F\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\omega,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_\omega\leq G\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\theta,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}\leq F'\circ\operatorname{Cap}_\omega,\quad\operatorname{Cap}_\omega\leq G'\circ\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta'}.\]
The reference potentials have positive mass because the classes are big. Set $f=F\circ G'$ and $g=F'\circ G$. Composing the respective inequalities proves the two assertions for every Borel set. The compositions are continuous and vanish at zero, as required.

title: Definition 13.12.3
text: Definition 13.12.3 . BA13EE505D9B Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. A function $f\colon U\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous if it is Borel measurable and for any $\epsilon >0$, there is an open subset $G\subseteq U$ such that E9A5229B982B $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(G)\leq \epsilon $; EC64A29E7BCB $f|_{U\setminus G}$ is real-valued and continuous.

title: Theorem 13.12.4
text: Theorem 13.12.4 . 9F9E57CC1422 Let $A\subseteq X$ be a Borel set. Then the following are equivalent: 9860890C10B2 $A$ is pluripolar; 0031AD934DC8 $\operatorname{Cap}_{\theta }(A)=0$. Proof. By capacity comparison , zero $\theta$-capacity is equivalent to zero Kähler capacity. The comparison with coordinate-ball capacities makes this equivalent to zero local Bedford--Taylor capacity in every member of a finite coordinate cover. The local zero-capacity theorem identifies these zero sets with the pluripolar sets. This proves both implications. For a Borel set, one may first apply the local statement to compact subsets and then use the capacitability and zero-capacity characterization proved with that theorem; a mere measure-zero argument would not suffice.

title: 13.13 Properties of non-pluripolar products
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta ,	heta _1,\ldots ,	heta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. We write 44C4E200865B 13.13.1  egin{equation}  \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}=\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \int _ X	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0 ight\} . \end{equation} The non-pluripolar product $	heta _{\varphi }^ n$ is well-defined thanks to proposition 13.11.14 . Remark 13.13.2 . 218A02F6B9E0 Suppose that $X$ is a connected complex manifold of dimension $0$, namely, $X$ is a single point. In this case, by definition, the non-pluripolar product $	heta _{\varphi }^ n$ is given by the current of integration at the unique point. So $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}=\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cong \mathbb {R}$ in this case and $\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=1$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Recall the following basic result: Proposition 13.13.3 . C0B519026258 Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is non-empty. Then the cohomology class $\{ 	heta \} $ is big. See [ Proposition 1.22 , BEGZ10 ] . 


We recall a few basic facts about the non-pluripolar masses. Proposition 13.13.4 . 365687A6A087 Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ and $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \int _ Y (\pi ^*T_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\pi ^*T_ n)=\int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n.  \] Similarly, if $S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $Y$, then \[  \int _ Y S_1\wedge \cdots \wedge S_ n=\int _ X \left(\pi _*S_1ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\pi _*S_ night).  \] Here $\pi ^*T_ i$ is defined as follows: Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta _ i$ on $X$ and $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$, then $\pi ^*T_ i=\pi ^*	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi _ i$. The pull-back $\pi ^*T_ i$ is clearly independent of the choices of $	heta _ i$ and $\varphi _ i$. Proof. The assertions follow from proposition 13.11.4 1 on the Zariski open set where $\pi $ is an isomorphism. The exceptional locus is pluripolar, and the relevant non-pluripolar products put no mass on pluripolar sets by proposition 13.11.4 4 . $\square$ Theorem 13.13.5 . 7F7BE8292E76 Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then the map \[  [0,1] 
i t\mapsto \log \int _ X 	heta _{t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0}^ n  \] is concave. More generally, given closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$, we have \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \int _ X T_ i^ n ight)^{1/n}.  \] See [ DDNL19log ] for the proof. Remark 13.13.6 . 22841C35D44B Here and in the sequel, when we write expressions like $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi $ for $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we will follow the convention that when $t=0$, the value is $\psi $ and when $t=1$, the value is $\varphi $. We shall write 6F52E700CD98 13.13.7  egin{equation}  V_{	heta }=\sup \left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\varphi \leq 0 ight\} . \end{equation} Note that the upper semicontinuous regularization $V_{	heta }^*$ of $V_{	heta }$ is itself a candidate of ( 13.13.7 ) if $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )
eq \varnothing $ as follows from proposition 5.14.2 , therefore, $V_{	heta }=V_{	heta }^*\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ if $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )
eq \varnothing $. The function $V_{	heta }$ should be regarded as a canonical representative of the least singular potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. We recall the following result: Lemma 13.13.8 . F77E450F00FD Suppose that $\{ 	heta \} $ is big. The potential $V_{	heta }$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$. Recall that $\operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$ is the non-Kähler locus introduced in definition 5.19.9 . Proof. By definition of $\operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$, it suffices to show that if $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ has analytic singularities and $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then $V_{	heta }$ is locally bounded outside $\{ \varphi =-\infty \} $. After replacing $\varphi $ by $\varphi -\sup _ X\varphi $, the function $\varphi $ is a candidate in ( 13.13.7 ); hence $V_{	heta }\geq \varphi $ and $V_{	heta }\leq 0$. Since $\varphi $ is locally bounded outside its pole set, so is $V_{	heta }$. $\square$ The non-pluripolar product has a lower semicontinuity property. Theorem 13.13.9 (Semicontinuity theorem) . B3DC3180FF35 Let $\varphi _ j, \varphi _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$, $j=1,\ldots ,n$). Let $\chi _ k,\chi $ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$) be non-negative uniformly bounded quasi-continuous functions on $X$ such that $(\chi _ k)_ k$ converges to $\chi $ in capacity. Assume that for any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, as $k	o \infty $, either $\varphi _ j^ k$ decreases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ or increases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ almost everywhere. Then 8EB996A1BAE1 13.13.10  egin{equation}  \varliminf _{k	o \infty }\int _ X\chi _ k \, 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \geq \int _ X \chi \, 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} If in addition, \[  \lim _{k	o \infty }\int _ X	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} =\int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n},  \] then \[  \chi _ k \, 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}ightharpoonup \chi \, 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}  \] weakly as measures 3 . In particular, the limit in ( 13.13.10 ) exists and equality holds in ( 13.13.10 ). 3. ↩ Recall that the weak convergence of Radon measures is stronger than the weak convergence as currents in general. When the Radon measures have uniformly bounded total variation, they are equivalent. See [ Theorem 2.6 , DDNLsurv ] for the proof. 


The non-pluripolar mass is a monotone quantity with respect to the singularity type. Theorem 13.13.11 (Monotonicity theorem) . 0E5F6133B048 Let $\varphi _ j,\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ j \succeq \psi _ j$ 4 for every $j$, then \[  \int _{X} 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n} \geq \int _{X} 	heta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In particular, if $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\varphi \succeq \psi $, then \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass increases as the potentials become less singular. 4. ↩ See definition 16.7.1 for the notation. See [ Theorem 1.1 , DDNL18mono ] . We will prove a vast extension of this theorem in proposition 16.8.22 . By this theorem, the non-pluripolar mass $\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n$ can be used as a rough measure of the singularities of $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. In section 16.2 , we shall refine this measure by defining the notion of $P$-envelope. As a corollary, we obtain that Corollary 13.13.12 . 37623491DEDC Fix a directed set $I$. For each $j=1,\ldots ,n$, take an increasing net $(\varphi _ j^ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$, uniformly bounded from above. Set \[  \varphi _ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j^ i,\quad j=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then 18A95DBDA47A 13.13.13  egin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} = \int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} In particular, if the nets are indeed sequences, we have \[  	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} ightharpoonup 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] Proof. The final assertion follows from ( 13.13.13 ) together with theorem 13.13.9 . It remains to establish ( 13.13.13 ). We may assume that $I$ is infinite as there is nothing to prove otherwise. Thanks to theorem 13.13.11 , we already know the $\leq $ inequality in ( 13.13.13 ). We prove the reverse inequality. When $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets, the reverse inequality follows from theorem 13.13.9 . In general, by Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 , we can find a countable infinite subset $R\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{r\in R}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ r_ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ i_ j  \] for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We fix a bijection $R\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, we will then denote elements $\varphi _ j^ r$ ($r\in R$) by $\varphi _ j^1,\varphi _ j^2,\dots $. We shall write \[  \psi _ j^ a=\varphi _ j^1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ j^ a  \] for each $a\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For every $a$ we may choose $i_ a\in I$ dominating the finitely many indices corresponding to $\varphi _ j^1,\ldots ,\varphi _ j^ a$ for all $j$. It then follows from the monotonicity theorem that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i}\geq \lim _{a	o \infty }\int _ X 	heta _{1,\psi _1^ a}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\psi _ n^ a}.  \] From the special case mentioned above, we know that the right-hand side is exactly the right-hand side of ( 13.13.13 ), so we conclude. $\square$ We prove an interesting inequality about the Monge–Ampère measure of the maximum of two potentials. Lemma 13.13.14 . F56651914DE1 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then 37A13FA36078 13.13.15  egin{equation}  	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, if $\varphi \leq \psi $, then \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] At a first sight, ( 13.13.15 ) might seem trivial, and it is if we replace $\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} $ by $\{ \varphi >\psi \} $. The difficulty really lies on understanding the contact set $\{ \varphi =\psi \} $. Proof. For each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we set \[  \psi _ k=\psi \lor (V_{	heta }-k),\quad \varphi _ k=\varphi \lor (V_{	heta }-k).  \] For each $t>0$ and each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[   egin{split}  	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\geq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\  =& \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality follows from the plurifine locality of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 1 . We observe that for any $t>0$, $\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)\sim \psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k$. Therefore, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 guarantees that \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n=\int _ X	heta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n.  \] As $t	o 0+$, \[  	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ nightharpoonup 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n  \] by theorem 13.13.9 . Letting $t	o 0+$, we conclude that \[  	heta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k\leq \varphi _ k\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n.  \] In particular, multiplying both sides by $\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{	heta }-k\} }$ and applying proposition 13.11.4 1 again, we find that \[   egin{split}  \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{	heta }-k\} }\, 	heta _{\psi \lor \varphi }^ n\geq & \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{	heta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi \leq \varphi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n \ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{	heta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi >\varphi \} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n. \end{split}  \] Letting $k	o \infty $, we conclude ( 13.13.15 ). $\square$ Corollary 13.13.16 . 7CB7A3C51640 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ so that $\varphi _ i	o \varphi $ in $L^1$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\leq 0$ for all $i\in I$. Then D30B25375476 13.13.17  egin{equation}  \varlimsup _{i\in I} \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }	heta _{\varphi _ i}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi =0\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Observe that $\varphi \leq 0$ by proposition 5.17.3 . Step 1 . We first assume that $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ is a sequence. For each $k>0$, let \[  \psi _ k=\operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq k}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j.  \] Then $(\psi _ k)_{k}$ is a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with limit $\varphi $, see corollary 5.14.8 for example. Thanks to 13.13.14 , for each $k>0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Multiplying both sides with $\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }$, we find that \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Take $b,C>0$. For each $k>0$, we have \[   egin{split}  \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } 	heta _{\psi _ k}^ n\ =\int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\psi _ k}\, 	heta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality part follows from proposition 13.11.4 1 . Letting $k	o \infty $ with the help of theorem 13.13.9 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }\int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\varphi }\, 	heta _{\varphi \lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n.  \] Letting $b	o \infty $ and then $C	o \infty $, we conclude ( 13.13.17 ). Thanks to ( 13.13.41 ), for each $a'>\epsilon ^{-1}$, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n>\left( rac{a'-\epsilon ^{-1}}{a'}ight)^ n\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Letting $a'	o \infty $, we conclude that \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] On the other hand, since $\eta \preceq \psi $, using the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 we find that \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n\leq \int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Hence, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, 1 holds as well. $\square$ Next we prove a domination principle. Theorem 13.13.43 (Domination principle) . B798B54E6F2E Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Assume that 92DC05470A2E 13.13.44  egin{equation}  \exists \phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\quad 	extup{s.t.} \quad \varphi \preceq \phi , \quad \psi \preceq \phi ,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n, \end{equation} and 99773FAEB14E 13.13.45  egin{equation}  \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \geq \psi $. Proof. Take the common less singular potential $\phi$ in the hypotheses as the reference potential. The inequalities $\varphi\preceq\phi$, $\psi\preceq\phi$ and the two mass equalities say exactly that $\varphi,\psi\in\mathcal E(X,	heta,\phi)$. The reference mass is positive, because it equals the positive mass of $\varphi$. The second hypothesis says that the Monge--Ampère measure of $\varphi$ vanishes on $\{\varphi<\psi\}$. The relative full-mass domination principle therefore gives $\varphi\geq\psi$. This identifies every hypothesis of the earlier proof; in particular the common full-mass reference cannot be dropped. Remark 13.13.46 . B80857C56A45 Using the terminologies to be introduced in section 16.1 , we can reformulate a special case of theorem 13.13.43 as follows: Suppose that $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is a model potential and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Assume that ( 13.13.45 ) holds then $\varphi \geq \psi $. Equivalently, using the terminologies of section 16.7 , the assumption ( 13.13.44 ) can be reformulated as $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. Proof. Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n.  \] We may replace $\psi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. Without loss of generality, we may also assume that $\psi \leq 0$. Now fix $a>1$. We define \[  \eta _ a\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr ).  \] Note that $\eta _ a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ by corollary 13.13.42 and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Furthermore, $\eta _ a\leq P_{	heta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\varphi )=\varphi $. Define \[  \gamma _ a\coloneqq a^{-1}\eta _ a+(1-a^{-1})\psi ,\quad D_ a\coloneqq \{ \gamma _ a=\varphi \} .  \] Then $\gamma _ a\leq \varphi $ with equality on $D_ a$. Therefore, \[   egin{aligned}  a^{-n}\, 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n\leq &  a^{-n}\, 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n& \  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} a^{-n}\, 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n &  	extup{ by theorem \href{../../tag/A60C61FA5696/}{13.13.24}}\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} 	heta _{\gamma _ a}^ n & \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} 	heta _{\varphi }^ n &  	extup{ by \href{../../tag/F56651914DE1/}{13.13.14}}\  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n &  	extup{ by (\href{../../tag/99773FAEB14E/}{13.13.45})}. \end{aligned}  \] Note that on $D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} $, we have $\eta _ a=\varphi $. We deduce that \[  	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\,  	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n \leq 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,  \] where the inequality follows from 13.13.14 . But the two ends have the same mass, and hence \[  	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\eta _ a}\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\varphi }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0.  \] Note that $\eta _ a$ is decreasing in $a$. The above equation shows that \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{a>1} \eta _ a
ot\equiv -\infty .  \] On the other hand, if $x\in X$ is such that $\varphi (x)<\psi (x)$, we then have \[  \eta _ a(x)\leq a\varphi (x)-(a-1)\psi (x)= \psi (x)+a\Bigl ( \varphi (x)-\psi (x) \Bigr ).  \] Letting $a	o \infty $, we find that $\eta (x)=-\infty $. Therefore, $\{ \varphi 
eq \psi \} $ is pluripolar, and hence empty by proposition 5.14.6 . Our assertion follows. $\square$ Lemma 13.13.47 . 3AA4A74713F0 For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that B1CBA0B9F2D3 $	heta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current, and 9583FAA82351 $\psi \leq \varphi $. In particular, there is an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ converging almost everywhere to $\varphi $ such that $	heta _{\varphi _ i}$ is a Kähler current for all $i\geq 1$. Proof. Using 13.13.30 , we can find $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that \[  \epsilon V_{	heta }+(1-\epsilon )\gamma \leq \varphi .  \] We observe that the cohomology class $\{ 	heta \} $ is big as a consequence of proposition 13.13.3 . Therefore, we can take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $	heta _{\eta }$ is a Kähler current and $\eta \leq 0$. Since $\eta \leq V_{	heta }$, we may take \[  \psi \coloneqq \epsilon \eta +(1-\epsilon )\gamma .  \] Then $\psi $ clearly satisfies 1 and 2 . For the latter claim, it suffices to take \[  \varphi _ i=\left(1-(i+1)^{-1}ight)\varphi +(i+1)^{-1}\psi  \] for each $i>0$. $\square$ Lemma 13.13.48 . 72A62384B9EC Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$ with $	heta \in c_1(L)$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then there exists $k_0>0$ such that for each $k\geq k_0$, we have \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)
eq 0.  \] Proof. By 13.13.47 , there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $	heta _{\psi }$ a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. Since $\mathcal{I}(k\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$, it suffices to prove the assertion with $\psi $ in place of $\varphi $. In this case, the result follows from Hörmander's $L^2$-estimate ( [ Hor66 ] ), see [ Theorem 13.21 , Dem12 ] . $\square$ In the remainder of this section, we sharpen theorem 13.13.24 for $C^{1,\overline{1}}$ barrier functions. Theorem 13.13.49 (Tosatti, Chu–Zhou) . FE0721C3DE01 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with a Kähler form $\omega $ and let $f\in C^{1,1}(X)$. Then \[  P_\omega (f)\in C^{1,1}(X),  \] and there is a constant $C=C(X,\omega ,\| f\| _{C^{1,1}})$ such that \[  \| P_\omega (f)\| _{C^{1,1}}\leq C.  \] This is the main result of [ Tos18 , CZ19 ] . The proof of this theorem relies on some PDE techniques far beyond the scope of the current book. Weaker results were due to [ Ber09 , Ber19 ] . Proposition 13.13.50 (Darvas–Rubinstein) . 4BEA034735FD Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. This is [ Theorem 2.5 , DR16 ] . The original proof relies unfortunately on [ BD12 ] , which can be replaced by theorem 13.13.49 . Lemma 13.13.51 . 9453F71CEE8F Assume that $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$ and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then the functions $f_1$, $f_2$ and $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$ coincide up to second order at almost every point of the contact set $\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\} $. In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)=f_1=f_2ight\} }\, \omega _{f_1}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)=f_1=f_2ight\} }\, \omega _{f_2}^ n.  \] We also have for $j\in \{ 1,2\} $, 93FB8527BF9B 13.13.52  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_{P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)} = &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)=f_1ight\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)=f_2ight\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} \ & - \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2ight\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}\  \geq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight)=f_ jight\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here $\omega _{f_ i}\coloneqq \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i\in L^ n(X)$, since $f_ i\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Therefore, $\omega _{f_ i}^ n$ makes sense as an absolutely continuous Radon measure. Proof. Set $\varphi \coloneqq P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$. Since $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \in C^0(X)$, we have $\varphi \leq \min \{ f_1,f_2\} $. By proposition 13.13.50 , $\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. As $f_1,f_2,\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, the measures $\omega ^ n_{f_1}$, $\omega ^ n_{f_2}$ and $\omega ^ n_\varphi $ are all absolutely continuous. Step 1 : We show that at almost every contact point, $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two. For $i\in \{ 1,2,3\} $ set \[  \Psi _1\coloneqq \varphi -f_1,\quad \Psi _2\coloneqq \varphi -f_2,\quad \Psi _3\coloneqq f_1-f_2.  \] Each $\Psi _ i$ lies in $C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. We claim that for $i=1,2,3$, we have 12862DAB63AB 13.13.53  egin{equation}  \Psi _ i	extup{ vanishes to second order at almost every point of }\{ \Psi _ i=0\} . \end{equation} To prove this, write $\{ \Psi _ i=0\} $ as the disjoint union $A_ i\sqcup B_ i\sqcup C_ i\sqcup D_ i$ of the following four sets: $A_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i
eq 0\} $; $B_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ 	extup{the classical real Hessian of }\Psi _ i	extup{ does not exist}\} $; $C_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ 	extup{the classical real Hessian exists and is non-zero}\} $; $D_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ 	extup{the classical real Hessian exists and equals zero}\} $. It suffices to prove $A_ i$, $B_ i$, $C_ i$ are Lebesgue null sets. The set $A_ i$ is a $C^1$ real hypersurface in $X$, hence has Lebesgue measure zero. Since $\Psi _ i\in W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the classical pointwise real Hessian of $\Psi _ i$ exists almost everywhere, so $B_ i$ is Lebesgue null. Finally $C_ i$ is Lebesgue null by Stampacchia's lemma. This proves ( 13.13.53 ). Specialising ( 13.13.53 ) to $\Psi _1,\Psi _2$, the functions $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two at almost every point of the contact set $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $. Consequently $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i$ have the same matrix of coefficients almost everywhere on $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $, and therefore so do their $n$-fold wedge powers: A9866D01984D 13.13.54  egin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ i},\qquad i\in \{ 1,2\} . \end{equation} The analogous statement applied to $\Psi _3$ gives 6FB38BF4B16C 13.13.55  egin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} = \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2}. \end{equation} Step 2 . The barrier $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} $ is continuous, hence quasi-continuous, so theorem 13.13.24 yields 77FFDFF752EB 13.13.56  egin{equation}  \int _{X\setminus \left(\{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\} ight)}\omega ^ n_\varphi = \int _{\left\{ \varphi <\min \{ f_1,f_2\} ight\} }\omega ^ n_\varphi =0. \end{equation} Set $V_1\coloneqq \{ f_1<f_2\} $ and $V_2\coloneqq \{ f_1>f_2\} $, both open. We may decompose \[  \{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\}  =  igl (V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\}  igr ) \sqcup  igl (V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\}  igr ) \sqcup \{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} .  \] This combined with ( 13.13.56 ) and ( 13.13.54 ) yields \[   egin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_\varphi ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi \  ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned}  \] On the other hand, \[  \mathds {1}_{V_ j\cap \{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} - \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}.  \] Therefore, \[  \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} } \,  igl (\omega ^ n_{f_ j}-\omega ^ n_{f_1}-\omega ^ n_{f_2} igr ).  \] Together with ( 13.13.55 ) we obtain ( 13.13.52 ). $\square$ Theorem 13.13.57 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . 6245F87DD88E Let $	heta _1,\dots ,	heta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing pseudo-effective cohomology classes. For each $i=1,\dots ,n$, let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ and $f_ i\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ be functions with $\varphi _ i\leq f_ i$. Then F5A7BEAB8003 13.13.58  egin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{ igcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n} = \mathds {1}_{ igcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  	heta _{1,f_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,f_ n}. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $	heta _1=\cdots =	heta _ n$, $\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n$ and $f_1=\cdots =f_ n$. Assume for the moment that this special case is known. Let us handle the general case. For $\lambda =(\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n)\in (\mathbb {R}_{>0})^ n$, we set \[  	heta _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j	heta _ j,\quad \varphi _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j\varphi _ j,\quad f_\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j f_ j.  \] Then $\varphi _\lambda \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _\lambda )$, $f_\lambda \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, $\varphi _\lambda \leq f_\lambda $, and \[   igcap _{j=1}^ n\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} \subseteq \{ \varphi _\lambda =f_\lambda \} .  \] So \[  \mathds {1}_{ igcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(	heta _\lambda )^ n_{\varphi _\lambda } = \mathds {1}_{ igcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(	heta _\lambda )^ n_{f_\lambda }.  \] Both sides are polynomials in $\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n$; comparing the coefficient of $\lambda _1\cdots \lambda _ n$ gives ( 13.13.58 ). From now on, we assume \[  	heta =	heta _1=\dots =	heta _ n,\quad \varphi =\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ),  \] and \[  f=f_1=\cdots =f_ n\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)  \] with \[  \varphi \leq f.  \] We wish to prove that 1FE4032CE3EE 13.13.59  egin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =fight\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =fight\} }\, 	heta _{f}^ n. \end{equation} Step 2 . We first handle the special case where $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Step 2.1 . We assume that $	heta $ is a Kähler form, denoted by $\omega $ for clarity. Pick a decreasing sequence $(\phi _ j)_ j$ in $C^{\infty }(X)$ 7 with pointwise limit $\varphi $ and set \[  \psi _ j\coloneqq P_{\omega }\left(\min \{ \phi _ j,f\} ight).  \] Then $\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, and \[  \varphi \leq \psi _ j\leq \min \{ \phi _ j,f\}  \leq f,  \] and hence $\psi _ j\searrow \varphi $. Applying 13.13.51 with $f_1=\phi _ j$ and $f_2=f$ gives 88AC8C43CD82 13.13.60  egin{equation}  \omega ^ n_{\psi _ j}\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ j=f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f \geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f. \end{equation} Fix $C>0$ with $\min _ X f>-C$ and $\epsilon >0$. Let \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq  rac{(\psi _ j+C)\lor 0}{\left((\psi _ j+C)\lor 0 ight)+\epsilon },\qquad h^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq  rac{(\varphi +C)\lor 0}{\left((\varphi +C)\lor 0ight)+\epsilon }.  \] These functions are both quasi-continuous with values in $[0,1]$. Observe that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }$ converges in capacity to $h^{C,\epsilon }$ as $j	o \infty $. Now fix $g\in C^0(X)$, $g\geq 0$. Note that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \psi _ j\leq -C\} $ and $h^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \varphi \leq -C\} $. Using locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 1 , we have \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n=h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n,\quad h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n=h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n.  \] Therefore, \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq &  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n & \  =&  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n & \  =&  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n &  	extup{by theorem \href{../../tag/272876B00528/}{13.12.8}}\  =& \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n & \  \geq &  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} } h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n &  	extup{by }(\href{../../tag/88AC8C43CD82/}{13.13.60})\  =&  \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the last equality follows from the dominated convergence theorem. By our choice of $C$, we have $h^{C,\epsilon }>0$ on $\{ \varphi =f\} $, and hence when $\epsilon 	o 0+$, $h^{C,\epsilon }	o 1$ everywhere on this set. Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, we find \[  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g \, \omega _{f}^ n  \] by the dominated convergence theorem. By the Riesz representation theorem, we conclude that \[  \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega _{f}^ n.  \] Then by 13.13.14 , the reverse inequality also holds, and ( 13.13.59 ) follows in this case. Step 2.2 . We no longer assume that $	heta $ is a Kähler form. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta +\omega $ is a Kähler form and $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega )$. Fix $g\in C^0(X)$ and consider, for $t\geq 0$, \[  Q(t)\coloneqq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (	heta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n - \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (	heta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ n.  \] By multilinearity of the non-pluripolar product, $Q$ is a polynomial in $t$. Step 2.1 applied to $	heta +t\omega $ for $t>1$ gives $Q(t)\equiv 0$ for $t>1$, hence $Q\equiv 0$, and in particular $Q(0)=0$. Since $g$ is arbitrary, ( 13.13.59 ) holds. Step 3 . We handle the general case. We no longer assume that $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta +\omega $ is a Kähler form. Then \[  \varphi \leq P_{	heta +\omega }(f)\leq f.  \] By 13.13.51 applied to $f_1=f_2=f$, we find that $f$ and $P_{	heta +\omega }(f)$ agree to the second order on the contact set $\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f \} $, so \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f ight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta +\omega }(f)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f ight\} }\, 	heta _{f}^ n.{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000018446}{8}} \] However, Step 2 implies that \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=\varphi ight\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=\varphi ight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta +\omega }(f)}^ n.  \] Combining these results, we conclude ( 13.13.59 ). $\square$ 7. ↩ The functions $\phi _ j$ are not required to be $\omega $-psh. 8. ↩ This expression looks slightly unusual, as $P_{	heta +\omega }(f)$ is not $	heta $-psh in general, but it does make sense. Corollary 13.13.61 . 77CAD5891555 Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )
eq \varnothing $. For any $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, we have \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ V_{	heta }=0\} }\, 	heta ^ n.  \] Proof. From theorem 13.13.57 , we find \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] By the concentration property theorem 13.13.24 , our assertion follows. $\square$ Theorem 13.13.62 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . 700E44C7083B Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then \[  P_	heta (f)\in C^{1,\overline{1}} igl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} ) igr ).  \] In particular, $V_{	heta }\in C^{1,\overline{1}} igl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} ) igr )$. We refer to [ DNT23 ] for the proof.
