title: Remark 13.13.2
text: Remark 13.13.2 . 218A02F6B9E0 Suppose that $X$ is a connected complex manifold of dimension $0$, namely, $X$ is a single point. In this case, by definition, the non-pluripolar product $\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ is given by the current of integration at the unique point. So $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}=\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cong \mathbb {R}$ in this case and $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=1$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$.

title: Proposition 13.13.3
text: Proposition 13.13.3 . C0B519026258 Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is non-empty. Then the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $ is big.

title: Proposition 13.13.4
text: Proposition 13.13.4 . 365687A6A087 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ and $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \int _ Y (\pi ^*T_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\pi ^*T_ n)=\int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n.  \] Similarly, if $S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $Y$, then \[  \int _ Y S_1\wedge \cdots \wedge S_ n=\int _ X \left(\pi _*S_1\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\pi _*S_ n\right).  \] Proof. The assertions follow from proposition 13.11.4 1 on the Zariski open set where $\pi $ is an isomorphism. The exceptional locus is pluripolar, and the relevant non-pluripolar products put no mass on pluripolar sets by proposition 13.11.4 4 . $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.5
text: Theorem 13.13.5 . 7F7BE8292E76 Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the map \[  [0,1] \ni t\mapsto \log \int _ X \theta _{t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0}^ n  \] is concave. More generally, given closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$, we have \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \int _ X T_ i^ n \right)^{1/n}.  \]

title: Remark 13.13.6
text: Remark 13.13.6 . 22841C35D44B Here and in the sequel, when we write expressions like $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi $ for $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we will follow the convention that when $t=0$, the value is $\psi $ and when $t=1$, the value is $\varphi $.

title: Equation 13.13.7
text: 6F52E700CD98 13.13.7 \begin{equation}  V_{\theta }=\sup \left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ):\varphi \leq 0 \right\} . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.13.8
text: Lemma 13.13.8 . F77E450F00FD Suppose that $\{ \theta \} $ is big. The potential $V_{\theta }$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Proof. By definition of $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$, it suffices to show that if $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ has analytic singularities and $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then $V_{\theta }$ is locally bounded outside $\{ \varphi =-\infty \} $. After replacing $\varphi $ by $\varphi -\sup _ X\varphi $, the function $\varphi $ is a candidate in ( 13.13.7 ); hence $V_{\theta }\geq \varphi $ and $V_{\theta }\leq 0$. Since $\varphi $ is locally bounded outside its pole set, so is $V_{\theta }$. $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.9 (Semicontinuity theorem)
text: Theorem 13.13.9 (Semicontinuity theorem) . B3DC3180FF35 Let $\varphi _ j, \varphi _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$, $j=1,\ldots ,n$). Let $\chi _ k,\chi $ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$) be non-negative uniformly bounded quasi-continuous functions on $X$ such that $(\chi _ k)_ k$ converges to $\chi $ in capacity. Assume that for any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, as $k\to \infty $, either $\varphi _ j^ k$ decreases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ or increases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ almost everywhere. Then 8EB996A1BAE1 13.13.10 \begin{equation}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \geq \int _ X \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} If in addition, \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} =\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n},  \] then \[  \chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\rightharpoonup \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}  \] weakly as measures 3 . In particular, the limit in ( 13.13.10 ) exists and equality holds in ( 13.13.10 ). 3. ↩ Recall that the weak convergence of Radon measures is stronger than the weak convergence as currents in general. When the Radon measures have uniformly bounded total variation, they are equivalent.

title: Equation 13.13.10
text: 8EB996A1BAE1 13.13.10 \begin{equation}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \geq \int _ X \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 13.13.11 (Monotonicity theorem)
text: Theorem 13.13.11 (Monotonicity theorem) . 0E5F6133B048 Let $\varphi _ j,\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ j \succeq \psi _ j$ 4 for every $j$, then \[  \int _{X} \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n} \geq \int _{X} \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In particular, if $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\varphi \succeq \psi $, then \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass increases as the potentials become less singular. 4. ↩ See definition 16.7.1 for the notation.

title: Corollary 13.13.12
text: Corollary 13.13.12 . 37623491DEDC Fix a directed set $I$. For each $j=1,\ldots ,n$, take an increasing net $(\varphi _ j^ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$, uniformly bounded from above. Set \[  \varphi _ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j^ i,\quad j=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then 18A95DBDA47A 13.13.13 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} = \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} In particular, if the nets are indeed sequences, we have \[  \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} \rightharpoonup \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] Proof. The final assertion follows from ( 13.13.13 ) together with theorem 13.13.9 . It remains to establish ( 13.13.13 ). We may assume that $I$ is infinite as there is nothing to prove otherwise. Thanks to theorem 13.13.11 , we already know the $\leq $ inequality in ( 13.13.13 ). We prove the reverse inequality. When $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets, the reverse inequality follows from theorem 13.13.9 . In general, by Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 , we can find a countable infinite subset $R\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{r\in R}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ r_ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ i_ j  \] for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We fix a bijection $R\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, we will then denote elements $\varphi _ j^ r$ ($r\in R$) by $\varphi _ j^1,\varphi _ j^2,\dots $. We shall write \[  \psi _ j^ a=\varphi _ j^1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ j^ a  \] for each $a\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For every $a$ we may choose $i_ a\in I$ dominating the finitely many indices corresponding to $\varphi _ j^1,\ldots ,\varphi _ j^ a$ for all $j$. It then follows from the monotonicity theorem that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i}\geq \lim _{a\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{1,\psi _1^ a}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n^ a}.  \] From the special case mentioned above, we know that the right-hand side is exactly the right-hand side of ( 13.13.13 ), so we conclude. $\square$

title: Equation 13.13.13
text: 18A95DBDA47A 13.13.13 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} = \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.13.14
text: Lemma 13.13.14 . F56651914DE1 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 37A13FA36078 13.13.15 \begin{equation}  \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, if $\varphi \leq \psi $, then \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. For each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we set \[  \psi _ k=\psi \lor (V_{\theta }-k),\quad \varphi _ k=\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-k).  \] For each $t>0$ and each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\geq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\\  =& \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality follows from the plurifine locality of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 1 . We observe that for any $t>0$, $\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)\sim \psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k$. Therefore, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 guarantees that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n.  \] As $t\to 0+$, \[  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n  \] by theorem 13.13.9 . Letting $t\to 0+$, we conclude that \[  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k\leq \varphi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n.  \] In particular, multiplying both sides by $\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} }$ and applying proposition 13.11.4 1 again, we find that \[  \begin{split}  \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} }\, \theta _{\psi \lor \varphi }^ n\geq & \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi \leq \varphi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n \\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi >\varphi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{split}  \] Letting $k\to \infty $, we conclude ( 13.13.15 ). $\square$

title: Equation 13.13.15
text: 37A13FA36078 13.13.15 \begin{equation}  \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 13.13.16
text: Corollary 13.13.16 . 7CB7A3C51640 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ so that $\varphi _ i\to \varphi $ in $L^1$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\leq 0$ for all $i\in I$. Then D30B25375476 13.13.17 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{i\in I} \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi =0\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Observe that $\varphi \leq 0$ by proposition 5.17.3 . Step 1 . We first assume that $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ is a sequence. For each $k>0$, let \[  \psi _ k=\operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq k}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j.  \] Then $(\psi _ k)_{k}$ is a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with limit $\varphi $, see corollary 5.14.8 for example. Thanks to 13.13.14 , for each $k>0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Multiplying both sides with $\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }$, we find that \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Take $b,C>0$. For each $k>0$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n\\ =\int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\psi _ k}\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality part follows from proposition 13.11.4 1 . Letting $k\to \infty $ with the help of theorem 13.13.9 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\varphi }\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n.  \] Letting $b\to \infty $ and then $C\to \infty $, we conclude ( 13.13.17 ). Step 2 . We now handle the general net case. Fix a volume form on $X$, so that we can talk about the $L^1$-norm on $X$ in the sequel. Suppose that ( 13.13.17 ) fails. Then there is $\delta >0$ such that, for every $i_0\in I$, one can find $i\geq i_0$ satisfying \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n>\int _{\{ \varphi =0\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n+\delta .  \] Since $\varphi _ i\to \varphi $ in $L^1$, for every $k>0$ there is $a_ k\in I$ such that \[  \| \varphi _ i-\varphi \| _{L^1}<k^{-1},\quad i\geq a_ k.  \] We can then recursively choose an increasing sequence $(i_ k)_{k>0}$ in $I$ with $i_ k\geq a_ k$ and \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _{i_ k}=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _{i_ k}}^ n>\int _{\{ \varphi =0\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n+\delta .  \] This sequence converges to $\varphi $ in $L^1$, contradicting Step 1. $\square$

title: Equation 13.13.17
text: D30B25375476 13.13.17 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{i\in I} \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi =0\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Definition 13.13.18
text: Definition 13.13.18 . 434FC63292E2 Given a function $f\colon X\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$, we define $P_{\theta }(f)$ as follows: B0CB5D62EE36 13.13.19 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \varphi \leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere} \right\} {}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000013831}{5}}. \end{equation} 5. ↩ For an $\mathcal F$-upper semicontinuous obstacle (in particular, for an upper semicontinuous obstacle), the almost-everywhere and pointwise formulations of the envelope agree, by 5.15.20 and Proposition 5.15.18 .

title: Equation 13.13.19
text: B0CB5D62EE36 13.13.19 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \varphi \leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere} \right\} {}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000013831}{5}}. \end{equation} 5. ↩ For an $\mathcal F$-upper semicontinuous obstacle (in particular, for an upper semicontinuous obstacle), the almost-everywhere and pointwise formulations of the envelope agree, by 5.15.20 and Proposition 5.15.18 .

title: Equation 13.13.20
text: 5F5458A60B41 13.13.20 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }(f)\leq f\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.13.21
text: Lemma 13.13.21 . 2904B26253E2 Fix a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\colon X\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a lower semicontinuous function. Assume that $P_{\theta }(f)\not\equiv \infty $. Then $P_{\theta }(f)$ is locally bounded outside $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Set $U\coloneqq \{ P_{\theta }(f)<f\} \setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$, then 0D2A1EE39CF8 13.13.22 \begin{equation}  \Bigl (\theta |_ U+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }(f)|_ U\Bigr )^ n=0. \end{equation} Proof. First observe that $V_{\theta }+\inf _ X f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 13.13.19 ). So \[  P_{\theta }(f)\geq V_{\theta }+\inf _ X f,  \] and in particular $P_{\theta }(f)\not\equiv -\infty $. In particular, $P_{\theta }(f)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. It is therefore bounded from above. By 13.13.8 , it is locally bounded away from $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Now fix $x\in U$, and $\epsilon >0$ so that \[  P_{\theta }(f)(x)<f(x)-\epsilon .  \] Take holomorphic balls $B\Subset B'\Subset U$ containing $x$. After shrinking $B$, we can guarantee that BB745DB26624 13.13.23 \begin{equation}  \left.P_{\theta }(f)\right|_{B}<f(x)-\epsilon ,\quad f|_ B> f(x)-\epsilon . \end{equation} Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be the balayage of $P_{\theta }(f)$ on $B$, as constructed in proposition 5.17.9 . By the domination principle proposition 5.14.22 , we find that \[  \varphi |_{B}\leq f(x)-\epsilon <f|_{B}.  \] Since $\varphi =P_{\theta }(f)$ outside $B$, we conclude that \[  \varphi \leq f\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] From this it follows that $\varphi \leq P_{\theta }(f)$, and hence equality holds. But then ( 13.13.22 ) holds automatically on $B$ since $\varphi $ is constructed by balayage. Since $x$ and $B$ are arbitrary, we conclude ( 13.13.22 ). $\square$

title: Equation 13.13.22
text: 0D2A1EE39CF8 13.13.22 \begin{equation}  \Bigl (\theta |_ U+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }(f)|_ U\Bigr )^ n=0. \end{equation}

title: Equation 13.13.23
text: BB745DB26624 13.13.23 \begin{equation}  \left.P_{\theta }(f)\right|_{B}<f(x)-\epsilon ,\quad f|_ B> f(x)-\epsilon . \end{equation}

title: Theorem 13.13.24
text:
Theorem 13.13.24 . A60C61FA5696 Let $f\colon Xightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a quasi-continuous function. Assume that $P_{	heta }(f)
ot\equiv \pm \infty $. Then $P_{	heta }(f)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and 426FF7E9832C 13.13.25  egin{equation}  \int _{\{ P_{	heta }(f)<f\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $f$ is bounded. Step 1.1 . Reduce to the case where $f\leq 0$. Take $C\in \mathbb {R}$ so that $P_{	heta }(f)\leq C$. Then \[  P_{	heta }(f)=P_{	heta }\Bigl ( \min \{ f,C\}  \Bigr ).  \] Thus we can replace $f$ by $\min \{ f,C\} $. Replacing $f$ by $f-\sup _ X f$, we reduce easily to the case where $f\leq 0$. Step 1.2 . Reduce to the case where $f$ is bounded. Assume that in this case, the theorem is known. We prove ( 13.13.25 ) for $f\leq 0$. For each $j>0$, we have 1F8BEEBD94D3 13.13.26  egin{equation}  \int _{\{ P_{	heta }(f_ j)<f_ j\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)}^ n=0, \end{equation} where $f_ j=f\lor (-j)$. Now fix $C>0$ and two open sets $G'\Subset G\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$. Fix a smooth function $\chi \colon Xightarrow [0,1]$ so that $\chi |_{G'}\equiv 1$ and $\chi $ is supported in $G$. Define \[  U_ C\coloneqq G \cap \left\{ P_{	heta }(f)>V_{	heta }-C ight\} ,\quad U'_ C\coloneqq G' \cap \left\{ P_{	heta }(f)>V_{	heta }-C ight\} .  \] Then $U_ C$ is $\mathcal{F}$-open. It follows from proposition 13.11.4 1 that for any $j>0$, \[  \mathds {1}_{U_ C}\,  	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{U_ C}\,  	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)}^ n.  \] In particular, thanks to ( 13.13.26 ), 2745CA7D012B 13.13.27  egin{equation}  \int _{U_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Note that the $P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)$'s for various $j$ are uniformly bounded from below on $U_ C$, thanks to 13.13.8 . Next we claim that $(P_{	heta }(f_ j))_ j$ is decreasing and converges to $P_{	heta }(f)$. The sequence is decreasing; let us compute its limit. In fact, $P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq f_ j$ quasi-everywhere. It follows that $\inf _ j P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and hence \[  \inf _{j>0} P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq P_{	heta }(f).  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, and our assertion follows. Since $P_{	heta }(f)
ot\equiv -\infty $, we know that the set $\{ f=-\infty \} $ is pluripolar. It follows that $P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j$ converges to the following function $g\colon Xightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ in capacity: \[  g(x)= egin{cases}  P_{	heta }(f)(x)-f(x),& 	extup{if } f(x)
eq -\infty ;\  -\infty ,&  	extup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Therefore, \[  1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j}\xlongrightarrow {\mathrm{C}} 1-\mathrm{e}^{g}.  \] Next we claim that 6BC72E6A227C 13.13.28  egin{equation}  \int _{U'_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Since $g\leq 0$ quasi-everywhere, the left-hand side of ( 13.13.28 ) is non-negative. It suffices to prove the $\leq $ direction. We wish to let $j	o \infty $ directly in ( 13.13.27 ), but since $U_ C$ is not open in general, this cannot be done directly. In the sequel, we shall slightly enlarge $U_ C$ to get an open set and then take the limit. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find an open subset $W\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$ so that B774EF560F8B 13.13.29  egin{equation}  \operatorname{Cap}_{C^{-1}	heta }(W\setminus U_ C)<\epsilon . \end{equation} For example, we can construct $W$ as follows. By example 13.12.5 , we can find an open set $A\subseteq G$ so that $\operatorname{Cap}_{C^{-1}	heta }(A)<\epsilon $ and $P_{	heta }(f)-V_{	heta }$ is continuous on $G\setminus A$. Then $U_ C\cap (G\setminus A)$ is relatively open in $G\setminus A$, so we may choose an open set $W_0\subseteq G$ such that \[  W_0\cap (G\setminus A)=U_ C\cap (G\setminus A).  \] Taking $W=W_0\cup A$, we get $U_ C\subseteq W$ and $W\setminus U_ C\subseteq A$, hence ( 13.13.29 ). Thanks to ( 13.13.29 ) and ( 13.13.27 ), we have \[  \int _ W \chi \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq C^ n\epsilon .  \] Letting $j	o \infty $ and applying theorem 13.12.8 , we find that \[  \int _{U'_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq \int _ W \chi \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq C^ n\epsilon .  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, ( 13.13.28 ) follows. Now letting $C	o \infty $ in ( 13.13.28 ), we find \[  \int _{G'}\left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0.  \] Since $G'\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$ is arbitrary, and $\operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )\subseteq X$ is a proper analytic subset, we finally conclude \[  \int _ X \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0.  \] In other words, $P_{	heta }(f)=f$ almost everywhere with respect to $	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n$. This proves ( 13.13.25 ). Step 2 . We now assume that $-C'\leq f\leq 0$ for some $C'>0$. For each $j>0$, take an open subset $V_ j\subseteq X$ so that F0D9C03CCEDA $\operatorname{Cap}_{C'^{-1}	heta }(V_ j)\leq 2^{-j-1}$, and AF1E921609BC $f|_{X\setminus V_ j}$ is continuous. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $V_ j$'s are decreasing. Take a continuous function $f_ j\colon Xightarrow [-C',0]$ extending $f|_{X\setminus V_ j}$. Note that $0 \geq \phi \geq \psi $, and $P_{	heta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Note that the interval ( 13.13.31 ) remains the same if we replace $\psi $ by $\phi $. Take $a$ in this interval, it suffices to prove the existence of $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ so that 8E31B7D70F87 13.13.36  egin{equation}  a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\phi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} Let us record the following observation for later use. Therefore, the reverse inequality follows, and ( 13.13.37 ) follows. Fix $j>k>0$. Note that 2263D1F9CA2F 13.13.39  egin{equation}  \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n, \end{equation} where we applied theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 13.11.4 1 in the second equality. eq -\infty ight\}  } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  = &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  \varphi _ j\leq \phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  = &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  \varphi \leq \phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  \leq &  a^ n\left( \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n- \int _{\left\{ \varphi >\phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n ight)& 	extup{ by (\href{../../tag/2263D1F9CA2F/}{13.13.39})}. \end{aligned}  \] Next thanks to ( 13.13.37 ), \[  \sup _{ \left\{ \phi 
eq -\infty ight\}  } \left(\eta _ j-\phi ight)=\sup _ X \eta _ j	o -\infty .  \] In particular, for a fixed $k$, if $j$ is large enough, we have \[  \left\{ \eta _ j\leq \phi -ak ight\} =X.  \] Therefore, for a fixed $k$, for any large enough $j$, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ j}^ n\leq a^ n\left( \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n- \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ night).  \] Letting $k	o \infty $, we find \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n\leq a^ n \left(\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n ight).  \] This is a contradiction with our choice of $a$. Step 2 . Next we argue that $P_{	heta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\psi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Choose \[  a'\in \left( a, \left( rac{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n}ight)^{1/n} ight).  \] It follows from ( 13.13.33 ) that 1C8D5126D276 13.13.40  egin{equation}  P_{	heta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )\geq  rac{a}{a'} P_{	heta }\Bigl (a'\varphi +(1-a')\psi \Bigr )+ rac{a'-a}{a'}\varphi . \end{equation} Therefore, by theorem 13.13.11 , we have 675086676ABE 13.13.41  egin{equation}  \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }\left(a\varphi +(1-a)\psi ight)}^ n\geq  rac{(a'-a)^ n}{a'^ n}\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0. \end{equation} We conclude the proof. $\square$ 6. ↩ This is precisely the $P$-envelope to be introduced later in definition 16.3.5 .

title: Corollary 13.13.42
text: Corollary 13.13.42 . 992A84CBAC5D Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\varphi \preceq \psi $. Assume that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n$. Then for any $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, there is $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that F009B4D18B32 $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$; 6009D3BD92A6 $\epsilon \eta +(1-\epsilon )\psi \leq \varphi $. In fact, we can take \[  \eta =P_{\theta }\left(\epsilon ^{-1}\varphi +(1-\epsilon ^{-1})\psi \right).  \] Proof. Fix $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. We define $\eta $ as in the statement of the corollary. By 13.13.30 , $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Observe that 2 is satisfied by ( 13.13.34 ). Thanks to ( 13.13.41 ), for each $a'>\epsilon ^{-1}$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\left(\frac{a'-\epsilon ^{-1}}{a'}\right)^ n\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Letting $a'\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] On the other hand, since $\eta \preceq \psi $, using the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 we find that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Hence, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, 1 holds as well. $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.43 (Domination principle)
text: Theorem 13.13.43 (Domination principle) . B798B54E6F2E Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that 92DC05470A2E 13.13.44 \begin{equation}  \exists \phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\quad \textup{s.t.} \quad \varphi \preceq \phi , \quad \psi \preceq \phi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n, \end{equation} and 99773FAEB14E 13.13.45 \begin{equation}  \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \geq \psi $. Proof. Take the common less singular potential $\phi$ in the hypotheses as the reference potential. The inequalities $\varphi\preceq\phi$, $\psi\preceq\phi$ and the two mass equalities say exactly that $\varphi,\psi\in\mathcal E(X,\theta,\phi)$. The reference mass is positive, because it equals the positive mass of $\varphi$. The second hypothesis says that the Monge--Ampère measure of $\varphi$ vanishes on $\{\varphi<\psi\}$. The relative full-mass domination principle therefore gives $\varphi\geq\psi$. This identifies every hypothesis of the earlier proof; in particular the common full-mass reference cannot be dropped.

title: Remark 13.13.46
text: Remark 13.13.46 . B80857C56A45 Using the terminologies to be introduced in section 16.1 , we can reformulate a special case of theorem 13.13.43 as follows: Suppose that $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is a model potential and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that ( 13.13.45 ) holds then $\varphi \geq \psi $. Equivalently, using the terminologies of section 16.7 , the assumption ( 13.13.44 ) can be reformulated as $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. Proof. Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] We may replace $\psi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. Without loss of generality, we may also assume that $\psi \leq 0$. Now fix $a>1$. We define \[  \eta _ a\coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl ( a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr ).  \] Note that $\eta _ a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by corollary 13.13.42 and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Furthermore, $\eta _ a\leq P_{\theta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\varphi )=\varphi $. Define \[  \gamma _ a\coloneqq a^{-1}\eta _ a+(1-a^{-1})\psi ,\quad D_ a\coloneqq \{ \gamma _ a=\varphi \} .  \] Then $\gamma _ a\leq \varphi $ with equality on $D_ a$. Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n\leq &  a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, \theta _{\psi }^ n& \\  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, \theta _{\psi }^ n &  \textup{ by theorem \href{../../tag/A60C61FA5696/}{13.13.24}}\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} \theta _{\gamma _ a}^ n & \\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} \theta _{\varphi }^ n &  \textup{ by \href{../../tag/F56651914DE1/}{13.13.14}}\\  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n &  \textup{ by (\href{../../tag/99773FAEB14E/}{13.13.45})}. \end{aligned}  \] Note that on $D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} $, we have $\eta _ a=\varphi $. We deduce that \[  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\,  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n \leq \theta _{\varphi }^ n,  \] where the inequality follows from 13.13.14 . But the two ends have the same mass, and hence \[  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\eta _ a}\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\varphi }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0.  \] Note that $\eta _ a$ is decreasing in $a$. The above equation shows that \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{a>1} \eta _ a\not\equiv -\infty .  \] On the other hand, if $x\in X$ is such that $\varphi (x)<\psi (x)$, we then have \[  \eta _ a(x)\leq a\varphi (x)-(a-1)\psi (x)= \psi (x)+a\Bigl ( \varphi (x)-\psi (x) \Bigr ).  \] Letting $a\to \infty $, we find that $\eta (x)=-\infty $. Therefore, $\{ \varphi \neq \psi \} $ is pluripolar, and hence empty by proposition 5.14.6 . Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.13.47
text: Lemma 13.13.47 . 3AA4A74713F0 For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that B1CBA0B9F2D3 $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current, and 9583FAA82351 $\psi \leq \varphi $. In particular, there is an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ converging almost everywhere to $\varphi $ such that $\theta _{\varphi _ i}$ is a Kähler current for all $i\geq 1$. Proof. Using 13.13.30 , we can find $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  \epsilon V_{\theta }+(1-\epsilon )\gamma \leq \varphi .  \] We observe that the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $ is big as a consequence of proposition 13.13.3 . Therefore, we can take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\eta }$ is a Kähler current and $\eta \leq 0$. Since $\eta \leq V_{\theta }$, we may take \[  \psi \coloneqq \epsilon \eta +(1-\epsilon )\gamma .  \] Then $\psi $ clearly satisfies 1 and 2 . For the latter claim, it suffices to take \[  \varphi _ i=\left(1-(i+1)^{-1}\right)\varphi +(i+1)^{-1}\psi  \] for each $i>0$. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.13.48
text: Lemma 13.13.48 . 72A62384B9EC Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$ with $\theta \in c_1(L)$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there exists $k_0>0$ such that for each $k\geq k_0$, we have \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\neq 0.  \] Proof. By 13.13.47 , there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\psi }$ a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. Since $\mathcal{I}(k\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$, it suffices to prove the assertion with $\psi $ in place of $\varphi $. In this case, the result follows from Hörmander's $L^2$-estimate ( [ Hor66 ] ), see [ Theorem 13.21 , Dem12 ] . $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.49 (Tosatti, Chu–Zhou)
text: Theorem 13.13.49 (Tosatti, Chu–Zhou) . FE0721C3DE01 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with a Kähler form $\omega $ and let $f\in C^{1,1}(X)$. Then \[  P_\omega (f)\in C^{1,1}(X),  \] and there is a constant $C=C(X,\omega ,\| f\| _{C^{1,1}})$ such that \[  \| P_\omega (f)\| _{C^{1,1}}\leq C.  \]

title: Proposition 13.13.50 (Darvas–Rubinstein)
text: Proposition 13.13.50 (Darvas–Rubinstein) . 4BEA034735FD Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$.

title: Lemma 13.13.51
text: Lemma 13.13.51 . 9453F71CEE8F Assume that $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$ and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then the functions $f_1$, $f_2$ and $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$ coincide up to second order at almost every point of the contact set $\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\} $. In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega _{f_1}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega _{f_2}^ n.  \] We also have for $j\in \{ 1,2\} $, 93FB8527BF9B 13.13.52 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_{P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)} = &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} \\ & - \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}\\  \geq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_ j\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Proof. Set $\varphi \coloneqq P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$. Since $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \in C^0(X)$, we have $\varphi \leq \min \{ f_1,f_2\} $. By proposition 13.13.50 , $\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. As $f_1,f_2,\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, the measures $\omega ^ n_{f_1}$, $\omega ^ n_{f_2}$ and $\omega ^ n_\varphi $ are all absolutely continuous. Step 1 : We show that at almost every contact point, $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two. For $i\in \{ 1,2,3\} $ set \[  \Psi _1\coloneqq \varphi -f_1,\quad \Psi _2\coloneqq \varphi -f_2,\quad \Psi _3\coloneqq f_1-f_2.  \] Each $\Psi _ i$ lies in $C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. We claim that for $i=1,2,3$, we have 12862DAB63AB 13.13.53 \begin{equation}  \Psi _ i\textup{ vanishes to second order at almost every point of }\{ \Psi _ i=0\} . \end{equation} To prove this, write $\{ \Psi _ i=0\} $ as the disjoint union $A_ i\sqcup B_ i\sqcup C_ i\sqcup D_ i$ of the following four sets: $A_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i\neq 0\} $; $B_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian of }\Psi _ i\textup{ does not exist}\} $; $C_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian exists and is non-zero}\} $; $D_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian exists and equals zero}\} $. It suffices to prove $A_ i$, $B_ i$, $C_ i$ are Lebesgue null sets. The set $A_ i$ is a $C^1$ real hypersurface in $X$, hence has Lebesgue measure zero. Since $\Psi _ i\in W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the classical pointwise real Hessian of $\Psi _ i$ exists almost everywhere, so $B_ i$ is Lebesgue null. Finally $C_ i$ is Lebesgue null by Stampacchia's lemma. This proves ( 13.13.53 ). Specialising ( 13.13.53 ) to $\Psi _1,\Psi _2$, the functions $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two at almost every point of the contact set $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $. Consequently $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i$ have the same matrix of coefficients almost everywhere on $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $, and therefore so do their $n$-fold wedge powers: A9866D01984D 13.13.54 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ i},\qquad i\in \{ 1,2\} . \end{equation} The analogous statement applied to $\Psi _3$ gives 6FB38BF4B16C 13.13.55 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} = \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2}. \end{equation} Step 2 . The barrier $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} $ is continuous, hence quasi-continuous, so theorem 13.13.24 yields 77FFDFF752EB 13.13.56 \begin{equation}  \int _{X\setminus \left(\{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\} \right)}\omega ^ n_\varphi = \int _{\left\{ \varphi <\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right\} }\omega ^ n_\varphi =0. \end{equation} Set $V_1\coloneqq \{ f_1<f_2\} $ and $V_2\coloneqq \{ f_1>f_2\} $, both open. We may decompose \[  \{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\}  = \bigl (V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} \bigr ) \sqcup \bigl (V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} \bigr ) \sqcup \{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} .  \] This combined with ( 13.13.56 ) and ( 13.13.54 ) yields \[  \begin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_\varphi ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi \\  ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned}  \] On the other hand, \[  \mathds {1}_{V_ j\cap \{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} - \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}.  \] Therefore, \[  \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} } \, \bigl (\omega ^ n_{f_ j}-\omega ^ n_{f_1}-\omega ^ n_{f_2}\bigr ).  \] Together with ( 13.13.55 ) we obtain ( 13.13.52 ). $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.57 (Di Nezza–Trapani)
text: Theorem 13.13.57 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . 6245F87DD88E Let $\theta _1,\dots ,\theta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing pseudo-effective cohomology classes. For each $i=1,\dots ,n$, let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ and $f_ i\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ be functions with $\varphi _ i\leq f_ i$. Then F5A7BEAB8003 13.13.58 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n} = \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,f_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,f_ n}. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $\theta _1=\cdots =\theta _ n$, $\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n$ and $f_1=\cdots =f_ n$. Assume for the moment that this special case is known. Let us handle the general case. For $\lambda =(\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n)\in (\mathbb {R}_{>0})^ n$, we set \[  \theta _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j\theta _ j,\quad \varphi _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j\varphi _ j,\quad f_\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j f_ j.  \] Then $\varphi _\lambda \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _\lambda )$, $f_\lambda \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, $\varphi _\lambda \leq f_\lambda $, and \[  \bigcap _{j=1}^ n\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} \subseteq \{ \varphi _\lambda =f_\lambda \} .  \] So \[  \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(\theta _\lambda )^ n_{\varphi _\lambda } = \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(\theta _\lambda )^ n_{f_\lambda }.  \] Both sides are polynomials in $\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n$; comparing the coefficient of $\lambda _1\cdots \lambda _ n$ gives ( 13.13.58 ). From now on, we assume \[  \theta =\theta _1=\dots =\theta _ n,\quad \varphi =\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),  \] and \[  f=f_1=\cdots =f_ n\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)  \] with \[  \varphi \leq f.  \] We wish to prove that 1FE4032CE3EE 13.13.59 \begin{equation}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{f}^ n. \end{equation} Step 2 . We first handle the special case where $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Step 2.1 . We assume that $\theta $ is a Kähler form, denoted by $\omega $ for clarity. Pick a decreasing sequence $(\phi _ j)_ j$ in $C^{\infty }(X)$ 7 with pointwise limit $\varphi $ and set \[  \psi _ j\coloneqq P_{\omega }\left(\min \{ \phi _ j,f\} \right).  \] Then $\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, and \[  \varphi \leq \psi _ j\leq \min \{ \phi _ j,f\}  \leq f,  \] and hence $\psi _ j\searrow \varphi $. Applying 13.13.51 with $f_1=\phi _ j$ and $f_2=f$ gives 88AC8C43CD82 13.13.60 \begin{equation}  \omega ^ n_{\psi _ j}\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ j=f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f \geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f. \end{equation} Fix $C>0$ with $\min _ X f>-C$ and $\epsilon >0$. Let \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq \frac{(\psi _ j+C)\lor 0}{\left((\psi _ j+C)\lor 0 \right)+\epsilon },\qquad h^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq \frac{(\varphi +C)\lor 0}{\left((\varphi +C)\lor 0\right)+\epsilon }.  \] These functions are both quasi-continuous with values in $[0,1]$. Observe that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }$ converges in capacity to $h^{C,\epsilon }$ as $j\to \infty $. Now fix $g\in C^0(X)$, $g\geq 0$. Note that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \psi _ j\leq -C\} $ and $h^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \varphi \leq -C\} $. Using locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 1 , we have \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n=h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n,\quad h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n=h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq &  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n & \\  =&  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n & \\  =&  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n &  \textup{by theorem \href{../../tag/272876B00528/}{13.12.8}}\\  =& \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n & \\  \geq &  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} } h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n &  \textup{by }(\href{../../tag/88AC8C43CD82/}{13.13.60})\\  =&  \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the last equality follows from the dominated convergence theorem. By our choice of $C$, we have $h^{C,\epsilon }>0$ on $\{ \varphi =f\} $, and hence when $\epsilon \to 0+$, $h^{C,\epsilon }\to 1$ everywhere on this set. Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, we find \[  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g \, \omega _{f}^ n  \] by the dominated convergence theorem. By the Riesz representation theorem, we conclude that \[  \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega _{f}^ n.  \] Then by 13.13.14 , the reverse inequality also holds, and ( 13.13.59 ) follows in this case. Step 2.2 . We no longer assume that $\theta $ is a Kähler form. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\theta +\omega $ is a Kähler form and $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\omega )$. Fix $g\in C^0(X)$ and consider, for $t\geq 0$, \[  Q(t)\coloneqq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n - \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ n.  \] By multilinearity of the non-pluripolar product, $Q$ is a polynomial in $t$. Step 2.1 applied to $\theta +t\omega $ for $t>1$ gives $Q(t)\equiv 0$ for $t>1$, hence $Q\equiv 0$, and in particular $Q(0)=0$. Since $g$ is arbitrary, ( 13.13.59 ) holds. Step 3 . We handle the general case. We no longer assume that $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\theta +\omega $ is a Kähler form. Then \[  \varphi \leq P_{\theta +\omega }(f)\leq f.  \] By 13.13.51 applied to $f_1=f_2=f$, we find that $f$ and $P_{\theta +\omega }(f)$ agree to the second order on the contact set $\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \} $, so \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \right\} }\, \theta _{P_{\theta +\omega }(f)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \right\} }\, \theta _{f}^ n.{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000018446}{8}} \] However, Step 2 implies that \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=\varphi \right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=\varphi \right\} }\, \theta _{P_{\theta +\omega }(f)}^ n.  \] Combining these results, we conclude ( 13.13.59 ). $\square$ 7. ↩ The functions $\phi _ j$ are not required to be $\omega $-psh. 8. ↩ This expression looks slightly unusual, as $P_{\theta +\omega }(f)$ is not $\theta $-psh in general, but it does make sense.

title: Corollary 13.13.61
text: Corollary 13.13.61 . 77CAD5891555 Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\neq \varnothing $. For any $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, we have \[  \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ V_{\theta }=0\} }\, \theta ^ n.  \] Proof. From theorem 13.13.57 , we find \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] By the concentration property theorem 13.13.24 , our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 13.13.62 (Di Nezza–Trapani)
text: Theorem 13.13.62 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . 700E44C7083B Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then \[  P_\theta (f)\in C^{1,\overline{1}}\bigl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )\bigr ).  \] In particular, $V_{\theta }\in C^{1,\overline{1}}\bigl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )\bigr )$.

title: 16.1 The envelope operators
text: This chapter develops the envelope formalism that will be used in the following constructions. There are two parallel constructions. The first is the $P$-envelope, which records the singularity type relevant to non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère mass. The second is the $\mathcal I$-envelope, which records the singularity type detected by multiplier ideal sheaves. The distinction between these two envelopes is one of the main organizing principles of the book. The starting point is the rooftop operator. Given two singular potentials, the rooftop construction produces the largest potential lying below both, and it provides a flexible way to compare singularities. From this we define the $P$-envelope $P_\theta [\varphi ]$. Its fixed points are the model potentials. Model potentials are the natural representatives of $P$-singularity types: they preserve non-pluripolar mass and satisfy strong contact-set properties. The first part of the chapter establishes the basic algebra of these envelopes, their behavior under monotone limits, and the domination and contact principles needed later. We then introduce the Monge–Ampère energy relative to a model potential. This leads to the finite-energy classes $\mathcal E^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and to stability results for rooftop envelopes. These results will be used in the metric theory of singularities and in the study of geodesic rays. The second part of the chapter develops the $\mathcal I$-envelope $P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$. This envelope is defined by imposing multiplier ideal conditions rather than ordinary singularity-type conditions. It is therefore sensitive to valuative data in a way that the ordinary $P$-envelope is not. We prove its basic functorial properties, its independence of the chosen representative of the cohomology class, its bimeromorphic behavior, and its compatibility with analytic singularities. The comparison between $P_\theta [\varphi ]$ and $P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$ is delicate. They agree in important cases, for instance for analytic singularities, but they differ in general. Later chapters use this comparison to define $\mathcal I$-good singularities, trace operators, partial Okounkov bodies and non-Archimedean potentials. Thus the technical results of this chapter should be regarded as the basic calculus of singularity types used in the sequel.

Fix a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$. Definition 16.11.5 . F80B4C1B3032 Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we define their rooftop operator as follows: 6AE4825E4C6F 16.3.1  egin{equation}  \varphi \land \psi =\sup \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi ight\} . \end{equation} For simplicity of notation, we extend the definition to the case where $\varphi $ or $\psi $ is constantly $-\infty $, in which case we simply set \[  \varphi \land \psi =-\infty .  \] When we want to be more specific, we may also write $\varphi \land _{	heta }\psi $. Note that it is possible that the set in ( 16.3.1 ) is empty, in which case $\varphi \land \psi =-\infty $. Proposition 16.3.2 . C1971A5F3DFD The operator $\land $ is a well-defined commutative, associative binary operator \[   igl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \}  igr )	imes  igl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \}  igr )ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Proof. We first show that the map is well-defined. For this purpose, take $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. When the set in ( 16.3.1 ) is empty, there is nothing to prove. So let us assume that the set is not empty. Define \[  \gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi ight\} .  \] Then by proposition 5.14.2 , we find that $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and hence $\gamma $ is a candidate for the supremum in ( 16.3.1 ). Therefore, $\gamma \leq \varphi \land \psi $. The reverse inequality follows from the definition of $\gamma $, so \[  \varphi \land \psi =\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] The commutativity and the associativity of $\land $ follow directly from the defining maximality property. $\square$ Note that from the proof, we have \[  \varphi \land \psi =P_{	heta }\Bigl ( \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \}  \Bigr ).  \] See definition 13.13.18 for the notation $P_{	heta }( ullet )$. Lemma 16.3.3 . 4CF7246E6E5A Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then E08D87E98114 16.3.4  egin{equation}  	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, $	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n$ is carried by the union $\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} \cup \{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} $. Proof. We first observe that as a consequence of 13.13.14 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying theorem 13.13.24 to $\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} $, we conclude that \[  	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n,  \] and ( 16.3.4 ) is established. $\square$ We recall that the relations $\preceq $ and $\sim $ are introduced in definition 16.7.1 . Definition 16.3.5 . 395DB7860949 Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we define its $P$-envelope as follows: 7E001B03F24A 16.3.6  egin{equation}  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0,\psi \preceq \varphi ight\} . \end{equation} Note that $\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi $ is always a candidate for the supremum. For $C>0$, we compute 35F5A4FBAC68 16.3.37  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n & \  =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  	extup{by proposition \href{../../tag/9E81D36B1290/}{13.11.4} \href{../../tag/9E81D36B1290/#sgpt-1C036AD6}{1}}\  =&  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  	extup{by theorem \href{../../tag/553335F185CE/}{16.3.12}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} In the last line we use that $\varphi $ is model, so $	heta _\varphi ^ n$ is carried by $\{ \varphi =0\} \subseteq \{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} $. We also get a similar formula for $	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n$. Therefore, taking the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 into consideration, we find BCB4335E3D6E 16.3.38  egin{equation}  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n=\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{equation} On the other hand, using 16.3.3 and ( 16.3.37 ), we find \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C\} } \, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C=0\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C=0\} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C<0 \} }\,  	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n.  \] Integrating, we find \[   egin{aligned}  \int _{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=0 \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \geq &  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n-\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n\  =&  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where on the first line we used the fact that $\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C\sim \gamma $, while on the second line, we used ( 16.3.38 ). Letting $C	o \infty $, and using corollary 13.13.16 , we conclude ( 16.3.36 ). $\square$ For later use, we also introduce a generalized envelope operator: Definition 16.3.39 . B791A3D8205D Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and a function $f\colon X	o [-\infty ,\infty ]$, we define \[  P_	heta [\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*} igl \{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \eta \leq f	extup{ quasi-everywhere},\  \eta \preceq \varphi  igr \} .  \] In general, we cannot replace $\eta \leq f$ quasi-everywhere by everywhere. Example 16.3.40 . 17FC69E7E25E When $f=0$, we have $P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. When $\varphi =V_{	heta }$, we have $P_	heta [V_{	heta }](f)=P_{	heta }(f)$. So definition 16.3.39 is a common generalization of definition 16.3.5 and definition 13.13.18 . Proposition 16.3.41 . Then \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ]} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ]=0ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n.  \] This is a vast generalization of theorem 16.3.12 . Proof. By definition, we have \[  P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_	heta [\varphi ]\Bigl (P_	heta (f)\Bigr )  \] and $\varphi \leq P_	heta (f)$. By corollary 16.3.14 and corollary 13.13.61 , \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] The reverse inequality follows immediately from theorem 13.13.57 . $\square$ Proposition 16.3.42 . 1F5A8A58FB4D Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ with $\varphi \leq f$. Then \[   egin{aligned}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_\varphi , \  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)\} }\, 	heta ^ n_\varphi . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. title: Proposition 16.3.2
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Proposition 16.3.2 . C1971A5F3DFD The operator $\land $ is a well-defined commutative, associative binary operator \[  \bigl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} \bigr )\times \bigl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} \bigr )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Proof. We first show that the map is well-defined. For this purpose, take $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. When the set in ( 16.3.1 ) is empty, there is nothing to prove. So let us assume that the set is not empty. Define \[  \gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi \right\} .  \] Then by proposition 5.14.2 , we find that $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and hence $\gamma $ is a candidate for the supremum in ( 16.3.1 ). Therefore, $\gamma \leq \varphi \land \psi $. The reverse inequality follows from the definition of $\gamma $, so \[  \varphi \land \psi =\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] The commutativity and the associativity of $\land $ follow directly from the defining maximality property. $\square$

title: Lemma 16.3.3
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Lemma 16.3.3 . 4CF7246E6E5A Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then E08D87E98114 16.3.4 \begin{equation}  \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We first observe that as a consequence of 13.13.14 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying theorem 13.13.24 to $\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} $, we conclude that \[  \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n,  \] and ( 16.3.4 ) is established. $\square$

title: Proposition 16.3.9
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Proposition 16.3.9 . EF5AC4B19C4D Let $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$ for some $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$. Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have $\varphi '\coloneqq \varphi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$ and \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\sim P_{\theta '}[\varphi '].  \] Proof. By symmetry, it suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta '}[\varphi '].  \] We may assume that $g\geq 0$ (after replacing $g$ by $g+C$ with $C\geq -\inf _ X g$, which leaves $\theta '$ unchanged and shifts $\varphi '$ by an additive constant). Then for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \preceq \varphi $ and $\psi \leq 0$, we set $\psi '\coloneqq \psi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$. Then $\psi '\preceq \varphi '$ and $\psi '\leq 0$, so $\psi '\leq P_{\theta '}[\varphi ']$. Since $\psi $ is arbitrary, it follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-\sup _ X g\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-g\leq P_{\theta '}[\varphi '],  \] which gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta '}[\varphi ']$. $\square$

title: Proposition 16.3.10
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Proposition 16.3.10 . E58386609911 Suppose that $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ are smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 0F7C5A9FEE2D 16.3.11 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{1,P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]}=\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} Proof. For each $C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  (\varphi _ i+C)\land V_{\theta _ i}\sim \varphi _ i.  \] It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,(\varphi _1+C)\land V_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(\varphi _ n+C)\land V_{\theta _ n}}=\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] So ( 16.3.11 ) follows from ( 16.3.7 ) and corollary 13.13.12 . $\square$

title: Theorem 16.3.12
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Theorem 16.3.12 . 553335F185CE Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 5CEAE61A4277 16.3.13 \begin{equation}  \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=0\} }\, \theta ^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Thanks to 16.3.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }}^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }=\varphi +C\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }=V_{\theta }\}  }\,  \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{\theta }\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=V_{\theta }\}  } \, \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C\to \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 13.13.12 give, as $C\to \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{\theta }\}  } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\rightharpoonup 0,\quad \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=V_{\theta }\} } \, \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Taking corollary 13.13.61 into consideration, we conclude ( 16.3.13 ). $\square$

title: Corollary 16.3.14
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Corollary 16.3.14 . B6EF8456606F Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land \psi .{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000019653}{1}} \] Assume that $\eta \not\equiv -\infty $ (for example when $\varphi \preceq \psi $). Then \[  \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] 1. ↩ Using the terminology to be introduced in definition 16.3.39 , we can also write $\eta =P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. Proof. Thanks to 16.3.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\varphi +C\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\psi \}  }\,  \theta _{\psi }^ n\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \}  } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C\to \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 13.13.12 give, as $C\to \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\rightharpoonup 0,\quad \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{\eta }^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Theorem 16.3.15
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Theorem 16.3.15 . 7ADF30509E4E Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 2B585EFD6781 16.3.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\sup \left\{ \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0,\varphi \preceq \psi , \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\right\} . \end{equation} In particular, in this case, 2 A43EDA3894B0 16.3.17 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation} 2. ↩ Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou [ PSWZ26 ] recently proved that, ( 16.3.17 ) continues to hold even when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. Proof. Let $\psi $ be a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 16.3.16 ). It follows from theorem 16.3.12 that \[  \int _{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} } \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \int _{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} \cap \{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=0\}  } \theta ^ n=0.  \] On the other hand, we have \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ],\quad \psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ]  \] and all these potentials have the same mass due to proposition 16.3.10 . So the domination principle theorem 13.13.43 is applicable and gives \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\geq \psi .  \] Hence we get the $\geq $ direction in ( 16.3.16 ). On the other hand, $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ itself is a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 16.3.16 ), as a consequence of proposition 16.3.10 . Therefore, ( 16.3.16 ) follows. As for ( 16.3.17 ), the $\geq $ direction is trivial. For the other direction, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential satisfying \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Then it follows from proposition 16.3.10 that \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad \varphi \preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In view of ( 16.3.16 ), we conclude the $\leq $ direction of ( 16.3.17 ). $\square$

title: Remark 16.3.19

text: Remark 16.3.19 . ED7781211B7B definition 16.3.18 is different from the common definition in the literature: We impose the extra condition $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. The author believes that this is the only case where this notion is natural. We sometimes emphasize this point by saying $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is a model potential.

title: Corollary 16.3.20
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Corollary 16.3.20 . E10CA97A11EF Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Moreover, \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 16.3.15 and proposition 16.3.10 . $\square$

title: Proposition 16.3.21
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Proposition 16.3.21 . 4C5C62135747 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Consider a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq \phi $. Then \[  \sup _{\{ \phi \neq -\infty \} } (\varphi -\phi )=\sup _ X \varphi .  \] Proof. Observe that $\phi \leq 0$, so on the set $\{ \phi \neq -\infty \} $, we have \[  \varphi -\phi \geq \varphi .  \] So the $\geq $ direction follows from corollary 5.15.21 . Conversely, by assumption, we can find a constant $C>0$ so that \[  \varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq \min \{ \phi +C,0 \} .  \] It follows that $\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Therefore, the reverse inequality follows. $\square$

title: Example 16.3.22
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Example 16.3.22 . E548BFB3BF04 We continue our favorite example example 5.20.6 . Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. We define $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ as follows: For $z\in \mathbb {C}$, we let \[  \varphi (z)= \begin{cases}  -\log \left(|z|^2+1\right)+\Bigl (-\log \left(-\log |z|^2\right)\Bigr ) \lor \Bigl (2+\log |z|^2\Bigr ),&  \textup{if }|z|<1/\sqrt{2},\\  2+\log \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^2+1},&  \textup{otherwise}, \end{cases}  \] while $\varphi (\infty )=2$. Note that $\varphi $ is $\omega $-psh on $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ by the gluing lemma 5.14.16 . The singularity of $\varphi $ only occurs at $z=0$, close to which, $\varphi $ is approximately $-\log \left(-\log |z|^2\right)$. This type of singularity is therefore called the log-log type singularity . We claim that B2DFFDD6A0F3 16.3.23 \begin{equation}  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0. \end{equation} In particular, we find that $\varphi $ and $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]$ have different singularity types. By theorem 16.3.15 , in order to verify ( 16.3.23 ), it suffices to verify that C825DA5CEC8C 16.3.24 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^1=1. \end{equation} Here $\omega _{\varphi }^1$ is taken in the non-pluripolar sense. Since $\{ 0,\infty \} \subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ is pluripolar, this reduces to showing that \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\frac{1}{4\pi }\int _{\mathbb {C}^*} (\Delta \psi )\, \mathrm{d}\mu =1,  \] where $\psi (z)=\varphi (z)+\log (|z|^2+1)$ and $\mu $ is the standard Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb {C}$. Note that the Laplacian vanishes outside $\overline{B(0,0.7)}$ since $\psi (z)=2+\log |z|^2$ there, which is harmonic. Therefore, \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\frac{1}{4\pi }\int _{|z|<1/\sqrt{2}} (\Delta \psi )(z)\, \mathrm{d}\mu .  \] It is an elementary exercise to see that the right-hand side is exactly equal to $1$. If you are familiar with toric geometry, this is more or less trivial since \[  \nabla _ r \Bigl ( \left(-\log (-r)\right)\lor (2+r) \Bigr )\bigl ((-\infty ,-\log 2)\bigr )= (0,1].  \] Otherwise, just try to evaluate the integral using Green's identities. Therefore, ( 16.3.24 ) is proved and our assertion ( 16.3.23 ) follows.

text: Proposition 16.3.25 . F7C0BACE770D Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and E6B68D406648 16.3.26 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$. For simplicity, we write \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ].  \] Note that due to our assumption ( 16.3.26 ), $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, and hence so is $\varphi \lor \psi $ thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . By corollary 16.3.20 , $\eta $ is a model potential, and $\int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n>0$. Take $C>0$ large enough, so that E47535691487 16.3.27 \begin{equation}  \int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n. \end{equation} This is possible thanks to proposition 13.11.4 4 . Fix $C'>C$. Write \[  \gamma _{C'}\coloneqq \Bigl (\varphi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr )\land \Bigl (\psi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr ).  \] Then observe that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $, and \[  \inf _{C'>C}\gamma _{C'}=\varphi \land \psi .  \] Suppose, for contradiction, that $\varphi \land \psi \equiv -\infty $. Then \[  \adjustlimits \lim _{C'\to \infty } \sup _ X\gamma _{C'}=-\infty .  \] Thanks to proposition 16.3.21 , for each $C'>C$, \[  \sup _{X} \gamma _{C'}=\sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta ),  \] since $\eta $ is a model potential. It follows that 74C044AB05CB 16.3.28 \begin{equation}  \adjustlimits \lim _{C'\to \infty } \sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta )=-\infty . \end{equation} In particular, we can take $C'$ large enough so that \[  \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C.  \] For such $C'$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n=& \int _{\{ \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C\} } \theta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n \\  \leq &  \int _{\left\{ \varphi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -C\right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n +\int _{\left\{ \psi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -C \right\} } \theta _{\psi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n\\  =&  2\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} }\theta _{\psi }^ n\\  <&  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the second line follows from 16.3.3 , the fourth line follows from ( 16.3.27 ). This contradicts the fact that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $ in view of theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$

title: Theorem 16.3.35
section: 16.3 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope
text: Theorem 16.3.35 . 5B751E9DFBC1 Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 020126C445C3 16.3.36 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, as otherwise ( 16.3.36 ) follows immediately from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Step 1 . We claim that it suffices to prove ( 16.3.36 ) with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. In fact, as $\varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty $, we also have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\land P_{\theta }[\psi ]\not\equiv -\infty $. Moreover, \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n  \] by proposition 16.3.10 . On the other hand, as $C\to \infty $, the potentials \[  \Bigl ( (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta } \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ( (\psi +C)\land V_{\theta } \Bigr )  \] converge to $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ almost everywhere. Therefore, thanks to corollary 13.13.12 and theorem 13.13.11 , \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n.  \] Finally, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\land P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n  \] as well. When the left-hand side vanishes, this follows from theorem 13.13.11 . Otherwise, it follows from 16.3.32 . In particular, ( 16.3.36 ) is equivalent to the corresponding result with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. Step 2 . We shall assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are model potentials in the sequel. We write $\gamma =\varphi \lor \psi $ for simplicity. Note that $\gamma \leq 0$. For each $C>0$, we introduce \[  \varphi _ C=\varphi \lor (\gamma -C),\quad \psi _ C=\psi \lor (\gamma -C).  \] Note that $\varphi _ C\sim \psi _ C\sim \gamma $. Observe that \[  \inf _{C>0} \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi \land \psi .  \] The $\geq $ direction is trivial, and the $\leq $ direction follows from the observation that the left-hand side is dominated by both $\varphi _ C$ and $\psi _ C$ for any $C>0$, and therefore by both $\varphi $ and $\psi $. For $C>0$, we compute 35F5A4FBAC68 16.3.37 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n & \\  =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by proposition \href{../../tag/9E81D36B1290/}{13.11.4} \href{../../tag/9E81D36B1290/#sgpt-1C036AD6}{1}}\\  =&  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by theorem \href{../../tag/553335F185CE/}{16.3.12}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} In the last line we use that $\varphi $ is model, so $\theta _\varphi ^ n$ is carried by $\{ \varphi =0\} \subseteq \{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} $. We also get a similar formula for $\theta _{\psi _ C}^ n$. Therefore, taking the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 into consideration, we find BCB4335E3D6E 16.3.38 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{equation} On the other hand, using 16.3.3 and ( 16.3.37 ), we find \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C\} } \, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n \\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C=0\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C=0\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C<0 \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n.  \] Integrating, we find \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=0 \} } \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n-\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where on the first line we used the fact that $\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C\sim \gamma $, while on the second line, we used ( 16.3.38 ). Letting $C\to \infty $, and using corollary 13.13.16 , we conclude ( 16.3.36 ). $\square$
