title: Lemma 21.12.7
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Lemma 21.12.7 . 1F4ACCC03A78 Let $F\colon N_{\mathbb {R}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function. Then the following are equivalent: AB1950E65189 $F$ is convex and takes values in $\mathbb {R}$, and AFD8C117A0B0 $\operatorname{Trop}^*F$ is plurisubharmonic on $T(\mathbb {C})$. Proof. We may choose an identification $N\cong \mathbb {Z}^ n$ so that we have an identification $T(\mathbb {C})\cong \mathbb {C}^{*n}$. Then $\operatorname{Trop}$ is identified with the map \[  \operatorname{Trop}\colon \mathbb {C}^{*n}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}^ n,\quad (z_1,\ldots ,z_ n)\mapsto \left(\log |z_1|^2,\ldots ,\log |z_ n|^2\right).  \] 1 $\implies $ 2 . By the standard convolution regularization of finite convex functions, let $F_ k\in C^{\infty }(\mathbb {R}^ n)\cap \mathrm{Conv}(\mathbb {R}^ n)$ be a decreasing sequence with limit $F$. It follows from a straightforward computation that 836C60871D35 21.12.8 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Trop}^*F_ k(z_1,\ldots ,z_ n) =& \frac{\mathrm{i}}{2\pi } \sum _{i,j=1}^ n \partial _{ij}F_ k\left(\log |z_1|^2,\ldots ,\log |z_ n|^2\right)\\ & \times z_ i^{-1}\overline{z_ j}^{-1}\mathrm{d}z_ i\wedge \mathrm{d}\overline{z_ j}. \end{split} \end{equation} So $\operatorname{Trop}^* F_ k$ is plurisubharmonic. It follows from proposition 5.14.2 that $\operatorname{Trop}^* F$ is plurisubharmonic. 2 $\implies $ 1 . It follows from 5.14.14 that $F$ is finite. Moreover, by radial regularization, we may find a decreasing sequence $\varphi _ k$ of $(S^1)^ n$-invariant smooth psh functions on $\mathbb {C}^{*n}$ with limit $\operatorname{Trop}^*F$. Write $\varphi _ k=\operatorname{Trop}^* F_ k$ for some function $F_ k\colon \mathbb {R}^ n\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$; it follows from ( 21.12.8 ) that $F_ k$ is convex for all $k$. Therefore, $F$ is convex by 21.11.13 . $\square$

text: Example 21.12.12 . CD7BA5BA48AF Let us move on with our favorite example example 21.12.4 . We continue to use the same notations. In this case, \[  G_0(m)= \begin{cases}  m\log m+(1-m)\log (1-m),&  \textup{if } m\in [0,1],\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] The Legendre transform is given by \[  F_0(n)=\log \left(1+\mathrm{e}^ n\right).  \] Composing with the tropicalization map, we find that \[  \omega |_{\mathbb {C}^*}(z)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log \left(1+|z|^2\right).  \] This is exactly the Fubini–Study metric as we have seen in example 5.20.6 . We can now explain one subtlety: in our expression ( 21.12.9 ), there is no factor $1/2$ before the sum; the absence of the factor $1/2$ matches the choice $\operatorname{Trop}(z)=\log |z|^2$ rather than $\log |z|$ in our tropicalization map ( 21.12.3 ).

title: Theorem 21.12.13
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Theorem 21.12.13 . 8B5B73657BF7 There are canonical bijections between the following three sets: 7680C9B63EAE The set of $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$, 2C49CA751C18 the set $\mathcal{P}(N_{\mathbb {R}},P)$ in definition 21.11.41 , namely, the set of convex functions $F\colon N_{\mathbb {R}}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ satisfying $F\preceq \operatorname{Supp}_ P$, and B8FE90D4F13F the set of closed proper convex functions $G\in \mathrm{Conv}(M_{\mathbb {R}})$ satisfying \[  G|_{M_{\mathbb {R}}\setminus P}\equiv \infty .  \] Proof. The bijection between 2 and 3 is the classical Legendre duality. Given $F$ as in 2 , we construct $G=F^*$ and vice versa , see proposition 21.11.38 . The map from 1 to 2 is given as follows: Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$, since $\varphi $ is $T_ c$-invariant, we can find $f\colon N_{\mathbb {R}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ such that 0CA6FBB8B2BF 21.12.14 \begin{equation}  \varphi |_{T(\mathbb {C})}=\operatorname{Trop}^*f. \end{equation} We then define $F=f+F_0$. Then $\operatorname{Trop}^* F\in \mathrm{PSH}(T(\mathbb {C}))$. By 21.12.7 , $F(n)$ is finite for any $n\in N_{\mathbb {R}}$ and $F$ is convex. Moreover, $F\preceq \operatorname{Supp}_ P$ since $\varphi $ is bounded from above on the compact space $X$ and $F_0\preceq \operatorname{Supp}_ P$. Conversely, given a map $F\in \mathcal{P}(N_{\mathbb {R}},P)$, then \[  \operatorname{Trop}^*(F-F_0)\in \mathrm{PSH}\left(T(\mathbb {C}),\omega |_{T(\mathbb {C})}\right).  \] Since $F\preceq \operatorname{Supp}_ P$ and $F_0\sim \operatorname{Supp}_ P$, the difference $F-F_0$ is bounded from above. Hence the corresponding local psh potentials are locally bounded from above near $X\setminus T(\mathbb {C})$. It follows from theorem 5.14.10 that this function can be extended uniquely to an $\omega $-psh function on $X$. The uniqueness of the extension guarantees its $T_ c$-invariance. The two maps are inverse to each other by construction. $\square$

text: Example 21.12.16 . 9BDBC1FA226A Let us take our favorite example example 21.12.12 again. We will continue to use the same notations. Recall that in example 5.20.12 and example 16.3.22 , we constructed two $S^1$-invariant functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. We begin with the function $\varphi $ in example 5.20.12 . Recall that \[  \varphi (z)=\log \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^2+1}  \] for $z\in \mathbb {C}$. The function $f\colon \mathbb {R}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ in ( 21.12.14 ) is therefore \[  f(n)=\log \frac{\mathrm{e}^{n}}{1+\mathrm{e}^{n}}.  \] Therefore, $F_{\varphi }\colon \mathbb {R}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is \[  F_{\varphi }(n)=n.  \] Correspondingly, $G_{\varphi }\colon \mathbb {R}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is \[  G_{\varphi }(m)= \begin{cases}  0,& \textup{if } m=1;\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Similarly, if $\psi $ denotes the function in example 16.3.22 , then the function $f$ in ( 21.12.14 ) is \[  f(n)= \begin{cases}  -\log \left(\mathrm{e}^ n+1 \right)+(-\log (-n))\lor (n+2),& \textup{if } n<-\log 2;\\  2+\log \frac{\mathrm{e}^{n}}{1+\mathrm{e}^{n}},& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Therefore, \[  F_{\psi }(n)= \begin{cases}  (-\log (-n))\lor (n+2),& \textup{if } n<-\log 2;\\  2+n,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] The Legendre transform is tricky to compute. Let $\lambda $ be the large solution of $\log x=x-2$. So $\lambda \approx 3.146$. The smaller solution is around $0.159<\log 2\approx 0.693$. It might be helpful to have a look at the poorly drawn picture 21.12.17 . 1AC4B1EDD9A2 21.12.17 The graphs of $\log x$ and $x-2$. It is immediate that $G_{\psi }(m)=\infty $ unless $m\in [0,1]$. Let us assume that $m\in [0,1]$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  G_{\psi }(m)=& \sup _{n\in \mathbb {R}} \left( mn-F_{\psi }(n)\right)\\  =&  \sup _{n<-\log 2} \left( mn-(-\log (-n))\lor (n+2)\right) \lor \sup _{n\geq -\log 2} (mn-n-2)\\  =&  \sup _{n>\log 2} \left( -mn+(\log n)\land (n-2)\right) \lor \left((1-m)\log 2-2\right). \end{aligned}  \] Let us focus on the first part, which can be decomposed further into \[  \begin{aligned} &  \sup _{n>\log 2} \left( -mn+(\log n)\land (n-2)\right)\\  =&  \sup _{n\in \left(\log 2,\lambda \right]} (n-2-mn) \lor \sup _{n>\lambda } (\log n-mn)\\  =&  \left( (1-m)\lambda -2 \right) \lor \sup _{n>\lambda } \left(\log n-mn\right). \end{aligned}  \] The latter part can be computed easily: \[  \sup _{n>\lambda } \left(\log n-mn\right)= \begin{cases}  -\log m-1,& \textup{if } m\in \left(0,\lambda ^{-1}\right];\\  \log \lambda -m\lambda ,&  \textup{if }m\in \left(\lambda ^{-1},1\right]. \end{cases}  \] Putting everything together, we find \[  G_{\psi }(m)= \begin{cases}  (-\log m-1)\lor \left( (1-m)\lambda -2 \right) ,& \textup{if } m\in \left(0,\lambda ^{-1}\right];\\  (\log \lambda -m\lambda )\lor \left( (1-m)\lambda -2 \right),&  \textup{if }m\in \left(\lambda ^{-1},1\right]. \end{cases}  \] This can be further simplified, the final result is \[  G_{\psi }(m)= \begin{cases}  -\log m-1 ,& \textup{if } m\in \left(0,\lambda ^{-1}\right];\\  (1-m)\lambda -2 ,&  \textup{if }m\in \left(\lambda ^{-1},1\right];\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] The graph of $G_{\psi }$ on $(0,1]$ is sketched in 21.12.18 . title: Proposition 21.12.19
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Proposition 21.12.19 . EEFA0F6B0CF6 Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$. The following are equivalent: 7C32E25C10B0 $\varphi \preceq \psi $, 94A12C520688 $F_{\varphi }\preceq F_{\psi }$, and 8A2AEA53E95B $G_{\psi }\preceq G_{\varphi }$. The same holds if we replace all $\preceq $'s by $\leq $. Proof. The equivalence between 1 and 2 follows from the definition ( 21.12.15 ). The equivalence between 2 and 3 follows from the definition of the Legendre transform. $\square$

title: Proposition 21.12.20
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Proposition 21.12.20 . D60ADA8CEE9B Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. We have \[  F_{\varphi +C}=F_{\varphi }+C,\quad G_{\varphi +C}=G_{\varphi }-C.  \] Proof. The first equality follows from ( 21.12.15 ). The second is obtained by taking the Legendre transform. $\square$

title: Proposition 21.12.21
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Proposition 21.12.21 . 419A1D9F18A9 Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ with $\varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty $, then $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ and \[  F_{\varphi \land \psi }=F_{\varphi }\land F_{\psi },\quad G_{\varphi \land \psi }=G_{\varphi }\lor G_{\psi }.  \] Proof. By proposition 16.3.2 , we have $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. Since $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are $T_ c$-invariant, the set of candidates in the definition of $\varphi \land \psi $ is preserved by the action of $T_ c$. Hence $\varphi \land \psi $ is $T_ c$-invariant as well. So $\varphi \land \psi $ is the biggest element in $\mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ which is dominated by both $\varphi $ and $\psi $. In view of theorem 21.12.13 and proposition 21.12.19 , $G_{\varphi \land \psi }$ is the smallest closed proper convex function $G$ on $M_{\mathbb {R}}$ dominating both $G_{\varphi }$ and $G_{\psi }$, which is just $G_{\varphi }\lor G_{\psi }$. For the statement about $F$, we use proposition 21.11.36 : \[  F_{\varphi \land \psi }=(G_\varphi \lor G_\psi )^*=\operatorname{cl}(F_\varphi \land F_\psi ).  \] Since $\varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty $, $F_{\varphi \land \psi }=(G_\varphi \lor G_\psi )^*$ is finite on all of $N_{\mathbb R}$. It follows that $F_\varphi \land F_\psi >-\infty $, and hence is finite on all of $N_{\mathbb R}$ as well. Being finite and convex on $N_{\mathbb R}$, it is continuous, hence closed. Therefore \[  F_{\varphi \land \psi }=F_\varphi \land F_\psi .  \] $\square$

title: Example 21.12.22
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Example 21.12.22 . 2B1E84EAAE13 Now we can give an example of $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ with $\varphi \land \psi \equiv -\infty $. We take $P=[0,1]$ so that $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ is the Fubini–Study metric. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ be such that \[  \varphi (z)=\log \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^2+1}  \] for $z\in \mathbb {C}$. We have computed that $G_{\varphi }$ in example 21.12.16 : \[  G_{\varphi }(m)= \begin{cases}  0,& \textup{if } m=1,\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Now we define $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ as the unique function such that \[  \psi (z)=\log \frac{1}{|z|^2+1}  \] for $z\in \mathbb {C}$. Then a similar computation shows that \[  G_{\psi }(m)= \begin{cases}  0,& \textup{if } m=0,\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Now we claim that $\varphi \land \psi \equiv -\infty $. Otherwise, we would have \[  G_{\varphi \land \psi }=G_{\varphi }\lor G_{\psi }\equiv \infty ,  \] which is not proper.

title: Proposition 21.12.23
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Proposition 21.12.23 . 73034E124A9A Let $\{ \varphi _ i\} _{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ uniformly bounded from above. Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ and \[  F_{\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i}=\bigvee _{i\in I}F_{\varphi _ i},\quad G_{\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i}=\operatorname{cl}\bigwedge _{i\in I} G_{\varphi _ i}.  \] Moreover, if $I$ is finite, then \[  G_{\max _{i\in I}\varphi _ i}=\bigwedge _{i\in I} G_{\varphi _ i}.  \] Similarly, if $\{ \varphi _ i\} _{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ such that $\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i\not\equiv -\infty $, then $\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ and \[  F_{\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i}=\inf _{i\in I}F_{\varphi _ i},\quad G_{\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i}=\bigvee _{i\in I}G_{\varphi _ i}.  \] Proof. Thanks to 21.11.13 and proposition 21.11.8 , in both cases, the statement for $F$ is clear. The corresponding statement for $G$ is obtained via proposition 21.11.36 . When $I$ is finite, the convex function $\bigvee _ i F_{\varphi _ i}$ is finite on all $N_{\mathbb R}$, hence closed. Therefore no additional closure is needed. $\square$

title: Definition 21.12.27
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Definition 21.12.27 . CC64AE504A19 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$. We define its Newton body as \[  \Delta (\omega ,\varphi )\coloneqq \overline{\{ G_{\varphi }<\infty \} }\subseteq P.  \] Note that $\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$ is a convex body.

title: Example 21.12.28
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Example 21.12.28 . E6289865C7A4 By ( 21.12.9 ), we have \[  \Delta (\omega ,0)=P.  \] In the case of example 21.12.16 , we have \[  \Delta (\omega ,\varphi )=\{ 1\} ,\quad \Delta (\omega ,\psi )=[0,1].  \] Observe that in the latter case, \[  \{ G_{\psi }<\infty \} \subsetneq P.  \]

title: Proposition 21.12.29
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Proposition 21.12.29 . 11748980D2DF Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$. Then $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$ and F8C4AC16B8F2 21.12.30 \begin{equation}  G_{P_{\omega }[\varphi ]}(x)= \begin{cases}  G_0(x),& \textup{if } x\in \Delta (\omega ,\varphi );\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Proof. By ( 16.3.7 ), we have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=\operatorname *{sup}_{C\in \mathbb {R}}{}\! {}^{*}\bigl ((\varphi +C)\land 0\bigr ).  \] It follows from proposition 21.12.20 , proposition 21.12.21 and proposition 21.12.23 that $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$. Moreover, by the same propositions, we have \[  G_{P_{\omega }[\varphi ]}=\operatorname{cl}\inf _{C\in \mathbb {R}} \left( G_{0}\lor (G_{\varphi }-C) \right).  \] We spell out the last closure. Set \[  K=\inf _{C\in \mathbb {R}} \left( G_{0}\lor (G_{\varphi }-C) \right).  \] If $x\in \operatorname{Dom}G_{\varphi }$, then $G_{\varphi }(x)-C\leq G_0(x)$ for $C$ large enough, hence $K(x)=G_0(x)$. If $x\notin \operatorname{Dom}G_{\varphi }$, then $K(x)=\infty $. Since $\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )=\overline{\operatorname{Dom}G_{\varphi }}$ and $G_0$ is continuous on $P$, the lower semicontinuous regularization $\operatorname{cl}K$ is equal to $G_0$ on $\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$ and equal to $\infty $ outside $\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$. This is exactly ( 21.12.30 ). $\square$

title: Corollary 21.12.35
section: 21.12 Toric pluripotential theory on ample line bundles
text: Corollary 21.12.35 . 05A4124B7E31 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\omega )$. Then \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)= n!\operatorname{vol}\Delta (\omega ,\varphi ).  \] Proof. Take $k>0$. Let $F_{0,k}$ denote the Guillemin potential associated with the polytope $kP$. On $T(\mathbb C)$, set \[  \widetilde\varphi _ k=\operatorname{Trop}^*(kF_\varphi -F_{0,k}).  \] Then $\widetilde\varphi _ k$ is the toric potential, with respect to the reference metric associated with $kP$, corresponding to the singular metric $h^ k\exp (-k\varphi )$ on $L^ k$. It differs from $k\varphi $ by the smooth toric function $\operatorname{Trop}^*(kF_0-F_{0,k})$. Hence \[  \mathcal I(\widetilde\varphi _ k)=\mathcal I(k\varphi ).  \] Moreover, the convex function associated with $\widetilde\varphi _ k$ is $kF_\varphi $, so its Legendre transform is \[  (kF_\varphi )^*(m)=kG_\varphi (m/k).  \] Thus the Newton body of $\widetilde\varphi _ k$ is $k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$. Applying theorem 21.12.31 1 to the line bundle $L^ k$ and the potential $k\varphi $, whose Newton body is $k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$, we have \[  \#  \left( k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )\cap M\right)\leq h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right).  \] Here $\# $ denotes the number of elements. Therefore, \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }k^{-n}\# \left( k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )\cap M\right)\leq \varliminf _{k\to \infty } k^{-n} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right).  \] The left-hand side is just $\operatorname{vol}\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$, as follows from theorem 19.7.20 . So we conclude that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq n!\operatorname{vol}\Delta (\omega ,\varphi ).  \] It remains to prove the reverse inequality. We choose an identification $M\cong \mathbb {Z}^ n$. In particular, there is a natural distance $\mathrm{d}$ on $M_{\mathbb {R}}\cong \mathbb {R}^ n$. Given a convex body $K$ and $\epsilon >0$, we let \[  K^{\epsilon }\coloneqq \left\{ x\in \mathbb {R}^ n: \mathrm{d}(x,K)\leq \epsilon \right\} .  \] This is again a convex body, since it can be realized as the Minkowski sum of $K$ with a closed ball of radius $\epsilon $. Applying theorem 21.12.31 2 to the polytope $kP$ and the potential $\widetilde\varphi _ k$, we can find $C>0$ uniform in $k$ such that for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, \[  \bigl \{  m\in M:\chi ^ m\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))\bigr \}  \subseteq \left(k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )\right)^ C.  \] Indeed, if a point $m\in kP\cap M$ is at distance at least $C$ from $k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )$, the separating hyperplane theorem gives a unit vector $v\in N_{\mathbb R}$ such that \[  \langle m,v\rangle -\operatorname{Supp}_{k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )}(v)\geq C.  \] Since the fan $\Sigma $ is finite and covers $N_{\mathbb R}$, there is a constant $\Lambda >0$ with the following property: every unit vector $v\in N_{\mathbb R}$ can be written in the form \[  v=-\lambda \sum _ i c_ i u_{\rho _ i},\quad 0<\lambda \leq \Lambda ,\quad c_ i>0,\quad \sum _ i c_ i=1,  \] where the rays $\rho _ i$ are contained in a single cone of $\Sigma $. Put \[  u\coloneqq \sum _ i c_ i u_{\rho _ i}.  \] Since the support function is positively homogeneous, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \langle m,-u\rangle -\operatorname{Supp}_{k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )}(-u)& =\lambda ^{-1}\left(\langle m,v\rangle -\operatorname{Supp}_{k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )}(v)\right)\\ & \geq C/\Lambda . \end{aligned}  \] Choosing $C>\Lambda $ makes ( 21.12.32 ) applicable, uniformly in $k$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. Then for large enough $k$, we have \[  \left(k\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )\right)^{C}\subseteq k\left(\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )^{\epsilon }\right).  \] It follows that \[  h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \#  \left( k\left(\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )^{\epsilon }\right) \cap M\right).  \] Applying theorem 19.7.20 again, we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq n! \operatorname{vol}\left(\Delta (\omega ,\varphi )^{\epsilon }\right).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ and applying theorem 19.7.5 , we find \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq n! \operatorname{vol}\Delta (\omega ,\varphi ).  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: 16.7 Comparison of singularities
text: A central theme of these constructions is that singularities of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be compared at several levels of precision. The preorder $\preceq $ of definition 16.7.1 compares potentials up to additive constants. It is the most concrete notion, but it is often too fine for global pluripotential theory: the $P$-envelope identifies potentials with the same model representative, while multiplier ideals identify singularities that have the same integrability behavior. This chapter makes these two coarser comparisons systematic. We first introduce the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal I$-preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. The $P$-preorder is defined by comparing $P$-envelopes, and its equivalence classes are the $P$-singularity types. The $\mathcal I$-preorder is defined by comparing multiplier ideals $\mathcal I(k\varphi )$ for all $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. These two preorders are compatible with ordinary singularity comparison, but they capture different information: the former is governed by non-pluripolar mass, while the latter is governed by valuative and multiplier-ideal data. The second main object of the chapter is the pseudometric $d_ S$. For positive-mass potentials in a fixed class, $d_ S$ is defined through the Darvas $d_1$-distance between the associated geodesic rays. Its zero locus is precisely $P$-equivalence. Thus $d_ S$ should be viewed as a convergence structure on $P$-singularity types. The chapter proves the basic properties of $d_ S$, including monotone convergence, sandwich criteria and compatibility with changing the background form. The final results establish the continuity properties that will be used in the following constructions. We prove continuity of the $\mathcal I$-envelope, continuity of non-pluripolar mass and volume, and a general equisingularity criterion. These results allow one to pass from analytic approximations to limiting singularities while controlling both $P$-types and multiplier ideals. They are used repeatedly in the theory of $\mathcal I$-good singularities, trace operators, test curves, partial Okounkov bodies and non-Archimedean potentials.

title: 16.8 The $P$ and $\mathcal{I}$-preorders
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Recall that we defined a preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ in definition 16.7.1 to compare the singularity types of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions. The problem with this preorder is that it is too fine. For our purposes, it is useful to consider rougher relations.

Note that $\psi \sim _ P \varphi $ implies that $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ by proposition 16.3.10 . We observe that \[   egin{split} & \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi ight\} \ =& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \varphi \preceq \psi , \psi \sim _ P \varphi ight\}  \end{split}  \] since for any candidate $\psi $ for the first supremum, $\psi \lor (\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi )$ is larger than $\psi $, and is a candidate for the second supremum thanks to 16.8.13 . So the first equality is a direct consequence of proposition 16.8.7 and theorem 16.3.15 . Next we prove the second equality. We only need to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. By 16.8.13 and example 16.8.6 , we know that $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \sim _ P \varphi $ and $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \leq 0$. It follows from the first equality that $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$ Similarly, we have a new characterization of the $\mathcal{I}$-envelope. Corollary 16.8.16 . 69E7C4B20FAE Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi ight\} .  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. By 16.8.13 and proposition 16.6.11 , we know that $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Therefore, $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi $ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ (cf. ( 16.6.8 )), so \[  \psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$ Proposition 16.8.17 . 2E8F613E7CBE Let $	heta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then the following are equivalent: 42227A6623F5 $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $; 6B5F8E56CB73 $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . This follows immediately from corollary 16.8.16 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . It follows from proposition 16.6.11 that \[  \varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}} \sim _{\mathcal{I}} \psi .  \] We conclude 1 . $\square$ Example 16.8.18 . C7A2AD00BFF3 Let us continue our example example 16.3.22 , where $X=\mathbb {P}^1$, $\omega $ is the Fubini–Study metric and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ has log-log singularity at $0$. We have shown that $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0$ in ( 16.3.23 ), so $\varphi \sim _{P} 0$ and hence $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$. In particular, $P$-equivalence is not equivalent to the equivalence of singularity types. On the other hand, consider a potential $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with log singularity at $0$, as in example 5.20.12 . We know that $
u (\psi ,0)=1$ from the explicit expression ( 5.20.13 ). So $\psi 
ot\sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ and hence $\psi 
ot\sim _{P} 0$. Moreover, $\psi \preceq _{P} \varphi $ and hence $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. We give an example showing that $P$-equivalence is not equivalent to $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence. Example 16.8.19 . 325A49CBCF74 Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. Let $K\subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ be a polar Cantor set carrying an atom free probability measure $\mu $ supported on $K$ (see [ Page 31 , Car83 ] ). Write $\mu =\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\omega $-subharmonic function $\varphi $. Since $\mu $ is atom free, we know that all Lelong numbers of $\varphi $ are $0$. On the other hand, $\varphi $ has $0$ non-pluripolar mass since $K$ is pluripolar. Then observe that $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ while $\varphi 
ot\sim _ P 0$. For later use, we give the following definition. Definition 16.8.20 . 33F50367BB68 Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. An elementary metric on $L$ is a psh metric $h$ on $L$ such that there is a generalized Fubini–Study metric $h'$ on $L$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\sim _{P} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h'.  \] The set of elementary metrics on $L$ is denoted by $\mathrm{Ele}(L)$. We also say $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is elementary. If we have fixed a Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$, and if we represent $h$ as $h_0\exp (-\varphi )$, we also say the quasi-psh function $\varphi $ is elementary. Recall that the generalized Fubini–Study metrics are defined in definition 5.20.15 .

title: Definition 16.8.2
text: Definition 16.8.2 . 4E959BD934C4 For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we say $\varphi $ is $P$-more singular than $\psi $ and write $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ if for some (equivalently, every, due to 16.8.4 below) closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we have D3383E5F872D 16.8.3 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]. \end{equation} If $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we write $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ and say that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ have the same $P$-singularity type .

title: Equation 16.8.3

title: Lemma 16.8.4
text: Lemma 16.8.4 . A3C93A5CDBF4 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, the following are equivalent: ED4E919B13E0 $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$; E3965942668C $P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Observe that \[  \varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ].  \] Taking the $P_{\theta +\omega }$-envelope, we find \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ],  \] where the equality follows from theorem 16.3.15 . In particular, 7E95C2DD4B7D 16.8.5 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]. \end{equation} A similar formula holds for $\psi $. So we see that 2 holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By ( 16.8.5 ), we may assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are both model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Observe that $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. It follows that $P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. The reverse inequality is trivial, so \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ].  \] From the direction we have proved, for any $C\geq 1$, \[  P_{\theta +C\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{\theta +C\omega }[\psi ].  \] So by proposition 16.3.10 , \[  \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi \lor \psi )\Bigr )^ n=\int _ X\left(\theta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \right)^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $C$, the equality extends to $C=0$, namely, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In particular, $\varphi \lor \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]=\psi $ by ( 16.3.16 ). So 1 follows. $\square$

title: Equation 16.8.5

title: Proposition 16.8.7
text: Proposition 16.8.7 . C7C64ABB4647 Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then the following are equivalent: B4083090A0B4 $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; 28D1D9DDF8EF for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, we have DF3EF73A9B89 16.8.8 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation} Assume furthermore that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then these conditions are equivalent to the following: 2A79C290D213 We have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. We first prove the equivalence between 1 and 1 when $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. 1 $\implies $ 1 . Assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. By 16.8.4 , we have \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi ].  \] So 1 follows from proposition 16.3.10 . 1 $\implies $ 1 . Since $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Moreover, proposition 16.3.10 shows that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ have the same positive mass. By theorem 16.3.15 , $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ is a candidate in the characterization of $P_{\theta }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\bigr ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. Hence $P_{\theta }[\psi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and therefore $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. So 1 follows. Let us come back to the general case with $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Fix $j\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $. We argue ( 16.8.8 ). Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By 16.8.4 , for each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]= P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ].  \] It follows from proposition 16.3.10 that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \right)^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=& \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  =& \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \\  =&  \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] Since the two extremes are both polynomials in $\epsilon $ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 , we conclude that the same holds when $\epsilon =0$, that is, ( 16.8.8 ) holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume ( 16.8.8 ) holds for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. Then the same holds with $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\psi $, thanks to proposition 16.3.10 . Therefore, for each $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n  \] by the binomial expansion. Furthermore, $t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }\preceq tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }$. By the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }\sim _ P t P_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }  \] for each $t\in (0,1)$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  \int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n= \int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $t$ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 , the same holds when $t=1$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 again, we have $\varphi \sim _ P P_{\theta }[\psi ]\sim _ P \psi $. $\square$

title: Lemma 16.8.11

title: Lemma 16.8.13
text: Lemma 16.8.13 . 005A077A0167 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then the following are equivalent: F123EB79E13C $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ (resp. $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $); 1D8449F6F20B $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P\psi $ (resp. $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $). title: Corollary 16.8.14
text: Corollary 16.8.14 . FE600747C81E Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $. Proof. Thanks to 16.8.13 , we have $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P \psi $. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. title: Corollary 16.8.15
text: Corollary 16.8.15 . 564E8A0E68F9 Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\} \\  =&  \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _ P \varphi \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. Note that $\psi \sim _ P \varphi $ implies that $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by proposition 16.3.10 . We observe that \[  \begin{split} & \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\} \\ =& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \varphi \preceq \psi , \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\}  \end{split}  \] since for any candidate $\psi $ for the first supremum, $\psi \lor (\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi )$ is larger than $\psi $, and is a candidate for the second supremum thanks to 16.8.13 . So the first equality is a direct consequence of proposition 16.8.7 and theorem 16.3.15 . Next we prove the second equality. We only need to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. By 16.8.13 and example 16.8.6 , we know that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \sim _ P \varphi $ and $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \leq 0$. It follows from the first equality that $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.8.16
text: Corollary 16.8.16 . 69E7C4B20FAE Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \right\} .  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. By 16.8.13 and proposition 16.6.11 , we know that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Therefore, $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi $ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ (cf. ( 16.6.8 )), so \[  \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$

title: Proposition 16.8.17

title: 16.8.21 Properties of the preorders
text: Now we state a more natural version of the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Proposition 16.8.22 (Monotonicity theorem) . 82DCD8E3B1BA Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for each $i$. Then \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass is a decreasing quantity with respect to the $P$-singularity types of the potentials. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, since $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P\psi _ i$, we have \[  P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]\leq P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\psi _ i]  \] for all $\epsilon >0$. Therefore, by proposition 16.3.10 and our previous monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , we have \[  \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _ n}.  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ and applying the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 , we find the desired inequality. $\square$ The $P$-preorder allows us to derive a natural generalization of 13.13.30 . Theorem 16.8.23 . 68E00C8C52A1 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then for any 3BF94E656512 16.8.24 \begin{equation}  a\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right), \end{equation} the function \[  \eta \coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )  \] lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ and 9690BB77C920 16.8.25 \begin{equation}  a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} If in addition, $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $, then $\eta \sim _ P \varphi $ as well. In ( 16.8.24 ), the fraction is understood as $\infty $ if either $\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$ or $n=0$, exactly as in 13.13.30 . Proof. By our assumption and ( 16.3.8 ), we have $\varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Due to proposition 16.3.10 , the interval ( 16.8.24 ) remains unchanged after replacing $\psi $ by $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Fix $a$ in this interval. So by 13.13.30 and the discussions afterwards, \[  \eta '\coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\Bigr )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] We first check that $\eta $ is a genuine $\theta $-psh function. Choose a closed non-pluripolar set $K\subseteq X$ on which $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are bounded. Then the obstacle $a\varphi +(1-a)\psi $ is bounded above on $K$. Every candidate in the definition of $\eta $ is therefore uniformly bounded above on $X$ by 5.17.4 , so $\eta \not\equiv \infty $ and hence $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. On the other hand, since $\psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$, we can find $C>0$ such that $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]+C$. Then \[  \eta '-(a-1)C\leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere, hence $\eta \geq \eta '-(a-1)C$. Thus $\eta '\preceq \eta $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 gives $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. By ( 13.13.20 ), \[  \eta \leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere. Equivalently, ( 16.8.25 ) holds quasi-everywhere. Since both sides of ( 16.8.25 ) are $\theta $-psh, proposition 5.14.6 upgrades the inequality to an everywhere inequality. It remains to prove the assertion about the $P$-order. Using proposition 16.4.2 , we get \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]+\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ] \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By the assumption $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we also have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Therefore, \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\leq a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]  \] quasi-everywhere and hence everywhere by proposition 5.14.6 . It follows that $P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, namely $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $. Finally assume that $\varphi \sim _ P\psi $. Then $\int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ by proposition 16.3.10 . Applying corollary 13.13.42 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta '}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Since $\eta '\preceq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] The reverse inequality follows from $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $ and proposition 16.8.22 . Hence $\eta \sim _ P\varphi $ by proposition 16.8.7 . $\square$ Next we show that the $P$ and $\mathcal{I}$-preorders are preserved by some natural operations. Lemma 16.8.26 . FB1663F2B6E1 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Given two quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi ,\psi $ on $X$, then the following are equivalent: 8ED2C9D6D32D $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $; 754FFF454EEB $\pi ^*\varphi \preceq _{P} \pi ^*\psi $. The same holds with $\mathcal{I}$ in place of $P$. Proof. In the $P$-case, this follows from proposition 16.4.1 , while in the $\mathcal{I}$-case, this follows from proposition 16.6.10 . $\square$ Proposition 16.8.27 . C42706880DED Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that \[  \varphi \preceq _ P \psi ,\quad \varphi '\preceq _ P \psi '.  \] Then \[  \varphi +\varphi '\preceq _ P \psi +\psi '.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of proposition 5.16.8 . We only need to handle the case of $\preceq _{P}$. Step 1 . We first show that \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\sim _ P \varphi +\varphi '.  \] In fact, we clearly have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\succeq \varphi +\varphi '.  \] So by proposition 16.8.7 , it suffices to show that they have the same mass. We compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \Bigl (2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^ n\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr )^ j\wedge \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^{n-j}\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \omega _{\varphi '}^{n-j}\\  =&  \int _ X \left(2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi '\right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where we applied proposition 16.3.10 to the mixed products on the third line. Step 2 . By Step 1, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '$ are all model potentials, after replacing them by their $P_{\omega }$-envelopes. So $\varphi \leq \psi $ and $\varphi '\leq \psi '$. Our assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 16.8.28 . 1C6DED516857 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$, $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be uniformly bounded from above non-empty families in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i\preceq _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\psi _ i.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. By adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of corollary 5.16.9 , we only have to consider the statement for $\preceq _ P$. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $I$ is a directed set and $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ and $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ are increasing nets. In this case, our assertion follows simply from proposition 16.4.9 . Step 2 . We handle the case where $I$ is finite. We may assume that $I=\{ 0,1\} $. It suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi _0]\lor P_{\theta }[\varphi _1]\sim _ P \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1,  \] which follows from 16.8.11 . Step 3 . The general case can be reduced to the two cases handled in Step 1 and Step 2. More precisely, by applying proposition 5.14.3 to the two families and taking the union of the resulting countable subsets, we can find a countable subset $J\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i,\quad \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ i.  \] We may replace $I$ by $J$ and assume that $I$ is countable. If $I$ is finite, Step 2 applies directly. Otherwise, write $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and set \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ m=\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ m,\quad \tilde{\psi }_ m=\psi _1\lor \cdots \lor \psi _ m.  \] By Step 2, $\tilde{\varphi }_ m\preceq _ P\tilde{\psi }_ m$ for every $m$. The two new sequences are increasing and have the same upper envelopes as the original families, so Step 1 applies. $\square$ We now refine 16.3.32 using the $P$-equivalence relation. Proposition 16.8.29 . 8C181599D520 Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that \[  \varphi \sim _ P \varphi ',\quad \psi \sim _ P\psi ',\quad \varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Then \[  \varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \varphi \land \psi \sim _ P \varphi '\land \psi '.  \] Proof. We first observe that $\varphi ,\varphi ',\psi ,\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by assumption. Let \[  \phi \coloneqq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi '],\quad \gamma =P_{\theta }[\psi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi '].  \] Since $\varphi '\preceq \phi $ and $\psi '\preceq \gamma $, after adding a common constant to $\varphi '$ and $\psi '$, we may assume that $\varphi '\leq \phi $ and $\psi '\leq \gamma $. Then $\varphi '\land \psi '\leq \phi \land \gamma $, so the assumption $\varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ implies $\phi \land \gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by monotonicity. It follows from 16.3.32 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n.  \] Next, we apply 16.3.32 again to conclude that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n>0.  \] Since $\varphi \land \psi \preceq \phi \land \gamma $ and the two potentials have the same positive mass, theorem 16.3.15 gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\phi \land \gamma $. The same argument gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi '\land \psi ']=\phi \land \gamma $, hence $\varphi \land \psi \sim _ P\varphi '\land \psi '$. $\square$ We can formulate a generalization of proposition 16.5.54 using the $P$-partial order. Corollary 16.8.30 . 21CC5153F56F Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $. Then for any $C>0$, $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 42D232E5CD85 16.8.31 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation} We refer to definition 16.3.39 for the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. Proof. Since $\psi \preceq _ P\varphi $, by proposition 16.8.29 , we get \[  \psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}  \] and $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\sim _ P\psi $ for every $C>0$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*}\psi \land (\varphi +C).  \] Then $\eta \sim _ P \psi $. By corollary 16.3.14 , we have \[  \theta _\eta ^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _\psi ^ n.  \] The domination principle theorem 13.13.43 gives $\eta \geq \psi $. The reverse inequality is trivial, so $\eta =\psi $. $\square$ The $P$-equivalence relation characterizes when a subgeodesic exists. See definition 17.10.2 for the notion of subgeodesics. Theorem 16.8.32 . 1CA975F04423 Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: 8E345DA2D98A There is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$; 5498C9F0BF2D $\varphi _0\sim _ P\varphi _1$. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This follows from proposition 17.10.24 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Step 1 . We assume that $\varphi _0\geq \varphi _1$. We first replace the given subgeodesic by the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Note that the geodesic is necessarily a subgeodesic as well by 17.10.22 . Observe that $t\mapsto \varphi _ t$ is decreasing due to 17.10.28 . Let $\varphi _ t=\varphi _1$ for all $t>1$. Then by the gluing lemma 17.10.16 , we find that $(\varphi _ t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a subgeodesic ray. Next, we consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{t\geq 0}(\varphi _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] It follows from Kiselman's principle proposition 5.14.15 that $\Gamma _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. Note that for $\tau >0$, we clearly have $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $. On the other hand, for $\tau \leq 0$, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t\in [0,1]}(\varphi _ t-t\tau )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] By Legendre inversion (cf. corollary 21.11.26 ), for $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left(\Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau \right).  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It follows from proposition 16.8.28 that for each $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }].  \] The right-hand side is independent of $t$. Here by adding $\omega $, we no longer have to worry about the possibility where $\Gamma _{\tau }$ has vanishing mass. Write \[  \varphi _0=\operatorname *{sup}_{t\in (0,1)}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ t.  \] By proposition 16.8.28 again, we find that \[  \varphi _0\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }]  \] as well. So $\varphi _0\sim _ P \varphi _1$. Step 2 . We prove the general case. Observe that $(\varphi _ t\lor \varphi _1)_{t\in (0,1)}$ is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0\lor \varphi _1$ to $\varphi _1$. By Step 1, \[  \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1\sim _ P \varphi _1.  \] Hence $\varphi _0\preceq _ P \varphi _1$ by 16.8.13 . The converse is proved similarly. Hence 2 follows. $\square$ Restating the 1 $\implies $ 2 direction in the theorem in terms of the complexification, we find the following interesting result. Let $S=\{ z\in \mathbb {C}:0< \operatorname{Re}z <1\} $. We write $p_1\colon X\times S\rightarrow X$ for the natural projection. Corollary 16.8.33 . 4EE47D80CC25 Let $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*\theta )$. Assume that for any $c\in \mathbb {R}$, $x\in X$ and $z\in S$, we have \[  \Phi (x,z)=\Phi (x,z+\mathrm{i}c).  \] Then $\int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ z)^ n$ is independent of $z\in S$, where $\Phi _ z \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is given by $\Phi _ z(x)=\Phi (x,z)$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We may regard $\Phi $ as an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*(\theta +\omega ))$. For any $0<a<b<1$, the restriction $(\Phi _ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is then a subgeodesic from $\Phi _ a$ to $\Phi _ b$ in the class $\theta +\omega $. The slices have positive mass in this class, so theorem 16.8.32 gives $\Phi _ a\sim _ P\Phi _ b$. By proposition 16.8.22 , this directly implies \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ b}^ n.  \] Since $\Phi $ is invariant under imaginary translations, $\Phi _ z$ depends only on $\operatorname{Re}z$, so the mass is independent of $z\in S$. $\square$

title: Proposition 16.8.22 (Monotonicity theorem)
