title: Proposition 16.8.28
text: Proposition 16.8.28 . 1C6DED516857 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$, $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be uniformly bounded from above non-empty families in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i\preceq _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\psi _ i.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. By adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of corollary 5.16.9 , we only have to consider the statement for $\preceq _ P$. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $I$ is a directed set and $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ and $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ are increasing nets. In this case, our assertion follows simply from proposition 16.4.9 . Step 2 . We handle the case where $I$ is finite. We may assume that $I=\{ 0,1\} $. It suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi _0]\lor P_{\theta }[\varphi _1]\sim _ P \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1,  \] which follows from 16.8.11 . Step 3 . The general case can be reduced to the two cases handled in Step 1 and Step 2. More precisely, by applying proposition 5.14.3 to the two families and taking the union of the resulting countable subsets, we can find a countable subset $J\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i,\quad \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ i.  \] We may replace $I$ by $J$ and assume that $I$ is countable. If $I$ is finite, Step 2 applies directly. Otherwise, write $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and set \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ m=\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ m,\quad \tilde{\psi }_ m=\psi _1\lor \cdots \lor \psi _ m.  \] By Step 2, $\tilde{\varphi }_ m\preceq _ P\tilde{\psi }_ m$ for every $m$. The two new sequences are increasing and have the same upper envelopes as the original families, so Step 1 applies. $\square$

title: Proposition 16.8.29
text: Proposition 16.8.29 . 8C181599D520 Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that \[  \varphi \sim _ P \varphi ',\quad \psi \sim _ P\psi ',\quad \varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Then \[  \varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \varphi \land \psi \sim _ P \varphi '\land \psi '.  \] Proof. We first observe that $\varphi ,\varphi ',\psi ,\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by assumption. Let \[  \phi \coloneqq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi '],\quad \gamma =P_{\theta }[\psi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi '].  \] Since $\varphi '\preceq \phi $ and $\psi '\preceq \gamma $, after adding a common constant to $\varphi '$ and $\psi '$, we may assume that $\varphi '\leq \phi $ and $\psi '\leq \gamma $. Then $\varphi '\land \psi '\leq \phi \land \gamma $, so the assumption $\varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ implies $\phi \land \gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by monotonicity. It follows from 16.3.32 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n.  \] Next, we apply 16.3.32 again to conclude that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n>0.  \] Since $\varphi \land \psi \preceq \phi \land \gamma $ and the two potentials have the same positive mass, theorem 16.3.15 gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\phi \land \gamma $. The same argument gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi '\land \psi ']=\phi \land \gamma $, hence $\varphi \land \psi \sim _ P\varphi '\land \psi '$. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.8.30
text: Corollary 16.8.30 . 21CC5153F56F Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $. Then for any $C>0$, $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 42D232E5CD85 16.8.31 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation} Proof. Since $\psi \preceq _ P\varphi $, by proposition 16.8.29 , we get \[  \psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}  \] and $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\sim _ P\psi $ for every $C>0$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*}\psi \land (\varphi +C).  \] Then $\eta \sim _ P \psi $. By corollary 16.3.14 , we have \[  \theta _\eta ^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _\psi ^ n.  \] The domination principle theorem 13.13.43 gives $\eta \geq \psi $. The reverse inequality is trivial, so $\eta =\psi $. $\square$

title: Equation 16.8.31
text: 42D232E5CD85 16.8.31 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation}

title: Theorem 16.8.32
text: Theorem 16.8.32 . 1CA975F04423 Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: 8E345DA2D98A There is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$; 5498C9F0BF2D $\varphi _0\sim _ P\varphi _1$. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This follows from proposition 17.10.24 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Step 1 . We assume that $\varphi _0\geq \varphi _1$. We first replace the given subgeodesic by the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Note that the geodesic is necessarily a subgeodesic as well by 17.10.22 . Observe that $t\mapsto \varphi _ t$ is decreasing due to 17.10.28 . Let $\varphi _ t=\varphi _1$ for all $t>1$. Then by the gluing lemma 17.10.16 , we find that $(\varphi _ t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a subgeodesic ray. Next, we consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{t\geq 0}(\varphi _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] It follows from Kiselman's principle proposition 5.14.15 that $\Gamma _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. Note that for $\tau >0$, we clearly have $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $. On the other hand, for $\tau \leq 0$, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t\in [0,1]}(\varphi _ t-t\tau )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] By Legendre inversion (cf. corollary 21.11.26 ), for $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left(\Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau \right).  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It follows from proposition 16.8.28 that for each $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }].  \] The right-hand side is independent of $t$. Here by adding $\omega $, we no longer have to worry about the possibility where $\Gamma _{\tau }$ has vanishing mass. Write \[  \varphi _0=\operatorname *{sup}_{t\in (0,1)}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ t.  \] By proposition 16.8.28 again, we find that \[  \varphi _0\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }]  \] as well. So $\varphi _0\sim _ P \varphi _1$. Step 2 . We prove the general case. Observe that $(\varphi _ t\lor \varphi _1)_{t\in (0,1)}$ is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0\lor \varphi _1$ to $\varphi _1$. By Step 1, \[  \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1\sim _ P \varphi _1.  \] Hence $\varphi _0\preceq _ P \varphi _1$ by 16.8.13 . The converse is proved similarly. Hence 2 follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.8.33
text: Corollary 16.8.33 . 4EE47D80CC25 Let $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*\theta )$. Assume that for any $c\in \mathbb {R}$, $x\in X$ and $z\in S$, we have \[  \Phi (x,z)=\Phi (x,z+\mathrm{i}c).  \] Then $\int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ z)^ n$ is independent of $z\in S$, where $\Phi _ z \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is given by $\Phi _ z(x)=\Phi (x,z)$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We may regard $\Phi $ as an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*(\theta +\omega ))$. For any $0<a<b<1$, the restriction $(\Phi _ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is then a subgeodesic from $\Phi _ a$ to $\Phi _ b$ in the class $\theta +\omega $. The slices have positive mass in this class, so theorem 16.8.32 gives $\Phi _ a\sim _ P\Phi _ b$. By proposition 16.8.22 , this directly implies \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ b}^ n.  \] Since $\Phi $ is invariant under imaginary translations, $\Phi _ z$ depends only on $\operatorname{Re}z$, so the mass is independent of $z\in S$. $\square$

title: 16.9 The $d_ S$-pseudometric
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. The goal of this section is to study a pseudometric on the space $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$.

title: 16.9.1 The definition of the $d_ S$-pseudometric
text: Recall that for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, the geodesic ray $\ell ^{\varphi }\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta )$ is defined in example 17.10.92 . Definition 16.9.2 . 240B1899916C For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\coloneqq d_1(\ell ^{\varphi },\ell ^{\psi }).  \] When we want to be more specific, we write $d_{S,\theta }$ instead of $d_ S$. The $d_1$ distance of geodesic rays is defined in definition 17.10.80 . Proposition 16.9.3 . 1ABAE06071CD The function $d_ S$ defined in definition 16.9.2 is a pseudometric on $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 17.10.81 . $\square$ When studying a pseudometric, the first thing is to understand when the distance between two elements vanishes. We first prove a preparation: Lemma 16.9.4 . 2490CFA511EC Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )+d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi ) \leq C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. We shall use the notations introduced in example 17.10.92 . Proof. We claim that FE54EE184B7A 16.9.5 \begin{equation}  \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }. \end{equation} Recall that $\lor $ is defined in definition 17.10.85 . Note that this assertion implies our desired inequality by 17.10.90 . In proving this assertion, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$ since \[  \ell ^{\varphi +C}=\ell ^{\varphi },\quad \ell ^{\psi +C}=\ell ^{\psi },\quad \ell ^{(\varphi +C)\lor (\psi +C)}=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }  \] for any $C\in \mathbb {R}$. In fact, it is clear that \[  \ell ^{\varphi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },\quad \ell ^{\psi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },  \] so the $\leq $ direction in ( 16.9.5 ) holds. Conversely, if $\ell '\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta )$ and $\ell '\geq \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }$, then for each $t\geq 0$, \[  \ell '_ t\geq \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \varphi \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \psi \Bigr )=(V_{\theta }-t)\lor (\varphi \lor \psi ).  \] See ( 17.10.96 ) for the first inequality. Therefore, thanks to the definition of the Perron envelopes (cf. ( 17.10.21 )), we have \[  \ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi ,t}_ s  \] for any $0\leq s\leq t$. It follows from ( 17.10.96 ) that $\ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }_ s$ for any $s\geq 0$. $\square$ Proposition 16.9.6 . C1D8A9BD3B3B Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: CCA0DECFB7E5 $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; A3A85D64324F $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$. In particular, $d_ S(\varphi ,P_{\theta }[\varphi ])=0$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proof. By 16.8.13 , we have $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ if and only if $\varphi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $ and $\psi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $. By 16.9.4 , $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$ if and only if $d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$ and $d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$. So it suffices to prove the assertion when $\varphi \leq \psi $. Assuming this, by proposition 17.10.83 , 2 holds if and only if \[  \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\varphi }\right)= \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\psi }\right),  \] where $\mathbf{E}$ is introduced in definition 17.10.82 . But by ( 17.10.94 ), this holds if and only if \[  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , this holds if and only if for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j},  \] which is equivalent to 1 by proposition 16.8.7 . $\square$ Lemma 16.9.7 . 03FCA1AB2751 Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Proof. Set $\chi \coloneqq \varphi \lor \psi $. By 16.8.13 , we have $\chi \sim _ P\psi $. Hence proposition 16.9.6 gives $d_ S(\chi ,\psi )=0$, and the pseudometric property gives \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=d_ S(\varphi ,\chi ).  \] Since $\varphi \leq \chi $, ( 17.10.94 ) and proposition 17.10.83 give \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\chi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Finally, proposition 16.8.7 applied to $\psi \leq \chi $ gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. $\square$ Corollary 16.9.8 . 255A623EA393 Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi ,\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi \preceq _ P \eta $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),\quad d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\psi ,\eta ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of 16.9.7 and the monotonicity theorem proposition 16.8.22 . $\square$ Corollary 16.9.9 . B29DCA70A9E6 For any $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have 0AC35440957F 16.9.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left( 2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \right) \\  \leq &  C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{split} \end{equation} where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. In particular, if $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $d_ S$-limit $\varphi $, then for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Proof. The estimates ( 16.9.10 ) follow from the combination of 16.9.7 and 16.9.4 . Suppose that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 16.9.4 . Therefore, theorem 13.13.11 and 16.9.7 imply that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for any $j=0,\ldots ,n$. The last assertion now follows from ( 16.9.10 ) and theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$ Corollary 16.9.11 . 94B2CC4C30BB Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold. Given a net $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, the following are equivalent: $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Proof. It suffices to observe that the middle term in ( 16.9.10 ) is invariant under $\pi ^*$. $\square$ Corollary 16.9.12 . 77738CEC8071 Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, uniformly bounded from above. Then \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i.  \] If the $\varphi _ i$'s are all model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then so is $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i$, as we have seen in proposition 16.4.9 . Proof. Write $\varphi =\operatorname *{sup}_{j\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ j$. Recall that by proposition 5.14.2 , $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By 16.9.7 , it suffices to show that for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}.  \] The latter follows from corollary 13.13.12 . $\square$ Corollary 16.9.13 . D47345F0C3C8 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  \left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n \right|\leq D_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $D_ n=3(n+1)C_ n$ with $C_ n$ being the same constant as in 16.9.4 . In other words, the non-pluripolar mass is uniformly continuous with respect to the $d_ S$-pseudometric. Proof. We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n \right|\leq &  \left|2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\right| + 2\left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\right|\\  \leq &  (n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )+2(n+1) d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )\\  \leq &  (n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )+2(n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{aligned}  \] where the first line is just the triangle inequality, the second line follows from corollary 16.9.9 and the third line follows from 16.9.4 . $\square$ By contrast to the increasing case, for nets decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder, the situation is different: Corollary 16.9.14 . F84D53FDA599 Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  \varphi _ j\preceq _ P\varphi _ i  \] whenever $j\geq i$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that $\varphi \preceq _ P\varphi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then the following are equivalent: 3D1A7D703ADF We have \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi ;  \] 919198E0409A for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have E95AEF6203E2 16.9.15 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}. \end{equation} If we assume furthermore that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$, then the above conditions are equivalent to the following: 8DEC59327E72 We have \[  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] When $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$ and these equivalent conditions are met, we also have FC1B825A9516 16.9.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\inf _{j\in I}P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]. \end{equation} Proof. 1 $\iff $ 2 . This follows immediately from 16.9.7 . Assume that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This is the case $k=n$ in ( 16.9.15 ). 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume (3). If for some $i\in I$, $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$, then for all $j\geq i$ we have \[  \varphi \preceq _ P\varphi _ j\preceq _ P\varphi _ i.  \] Hence $\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ by proposition 16.8.22 . It follows from proposition 16.8.7 that $\varphi _ j\sim _ P\varphi $, and (2) follows from proposition 16.3.10 . So in the sequel, we shall assume that for all $i\in I$, we have $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$. In particular, each $\varphi _ i$ has positive mass. Let $(b_ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net converging to $\infty $ such that \[  b_ j\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right).  \] This can be achieved for example by taking $b_ j$ as the midpoint of this interval. By theorem 16.8.23 , for each $j\in I$, we can find $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  b_ j^{-1}\eta _ j +\left(1-b_ j^{-1}\right)\varphi _ j \leq \varphi .  \] It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that for any $k=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}\geq \left(1-b_ j^{-1}\right)^ k\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}.  \] Taking the limit, we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 16.9.15 ). The $\geq $ direction follows from proposition 16.8.22 . Finally, we argue ( 16.9.16 ). Let $\psi _ j=P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]$. It follows from corollary 16.3.20 that $\psi _ j$ is a model potential. Since the net $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder, $(\psi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is decreasing pointwise. Let \[  \psi =\inf _{j\in I}\psi _ j\geq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By proposition 16.4.3 , $\psi $ is a model potential. Since $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq \psi \leq \psi _ j$ for all $j\in I$, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 16.3.10 give \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\psi _ j}^ n=\lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Hence $\psi $ has the same mass as $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. As $\psi $ is model and $\psi \geq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, theorem 16.3.15 gives $\psi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$ Having understood the increasing and decreasing cases, we shall handle general convergent sequences. In fact, since $d_ S$ is a pseudometric, the topology is completely determined by convergent sequences, so we do not need to consider nets in general. Proposition 16.9.17 . 1DEED63B61B0 Let $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ ($j\geq 1$), $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Assume that there is $\delta >0$ such that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] for all $j$ and the $\varphi _ j$'s are all model potentials. Then up to replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there is a decreasing sequence $(\psi _ j)_ j$ and an increasing sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that 36F21B225E6D $\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; 1EE77849B2C2 $\psi _ j\geq \varphi _ j\geq \eta _ j$ for all $j$. In fact, for any $j\geq 1$, we will take \[  \eta _ j=\inf _{k\in \mathbb {N}}\varphi _ j\land \varphi _{j+1}\land \cdots \land \varphi _{j+k},\quad \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ k.  \] Proof. First note that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq \delta $ as well, due to the $d_ S$-continuity of non-pluripolar masses as proved in corollary 16.9.13 . Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, we may then assume that $\varphi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We are free to replace $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence. So we may assume that 2902F1B6C4A6 16.9.18 \begin{equation}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-4}}{D_ n C_ n^{j+1}},\quad d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi _ j)\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-4}}{D_ n}, \end{equation} where $C_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.9 , $D_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.13 . In particular, by corollary 16.9.13 , 67C255B50420 16.9.19 \begin{equation}  \left|\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\right|\leq \delta 2^{-j-4}. \end{equation} Step 1 . We handle the $\psi _ j$'s. For each $j\geq 1$ and $k\geq 1$, by 16.9.4 we have \[  \begin{aligned}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}) & \leq C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k})\\ & \leq C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\\ & \quad + C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _{j+1},\varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}). \end{aligned}  \] By iteration, we find \[  \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k})\leq \sum _{a=j}^{j+k-1}C_ n^{a+1-j}d_ S(\varphi _ a,\varphi _{a+1})\\  \leq \frac{C_ n^{-j}}{D_ n}\sum _{a=j}^{j+k-1}\delta 2^{-a-4}\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-3}}{D_ n}. \end{split}  \] Using corollary 16.9.12 , we have \[  \varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ j  \] as $k\to \infty $. Hence 3B96A5372D55 16.9.20 \begin{equation}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\psi _ j)\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-3}}{D_ n}. \end{equation} We conclude that $\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Moreover, we observe that 79C50CD3AC3E 16.9.21 \begin{equation}  \varphi =\inf _{j\geq 1} P_{\theta }[\psi _ j] \end{equation} Indeed, set $\tilde{\psi }_ j=P_{\theta }[\psi _ j]$. Then $(\tilde{\psi }_ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials, and $d_ S(\tilde{\psi }_ j,\psi _ j)=0$ by proposition 16.9.6 . Hence $\tilde{\psi }_ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. If $\chi =\inf _ j\tilde{\psi }_ j$, then proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 give $\tilde{\psi }_ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\chi $. Thus $d_ S(\chi ,\varphi )=0$. Since both $\chi $ and $\varphi $ are model potentials, proposition 16.9.6 gives $P_{\theta }[\chi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, hence $\chi =\varphi $, proving ( 16.9.21 ). Step 2 . We consider the $\eta _ j$'s. For each $j\geq 1$ and $k\geq 0$, we let \[  \eta _ j^ k\coloneqq \varphi _ j\land \cdots \land \varphi _{j+k}.  \] Using ( 16.9.18 ), ( 16.9.20 ) and corollary 16.9.13 , we have \[  \left|\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n \right|\leq \delta 2^{-j-2}  \] for all $j\geq 1$. Taking ( 16.9.19 ) into account, we have 9F803C97D29B 16.9.22 \begin{equation}  \left|\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j-1}}^ n \right|\leq \delta 2^{-j} \end{equation} for $j>1$. Step 2.1 . We claim that for a fixed $j\geq 1$, for any $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we have $\eta _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and A82EF3572727 16.9.23 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k} \delta 2^{-j-a}. \end{equation} We argue by induction on $k\geq 0$. The case $k=0$ is trivial. When $k>0$, assume that the case $k-1$ is known. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^{k-1}}^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{j+k}}^ n \geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k-1}\delta 2^{-j-a}+\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n-\delta 2^{-j-k}\\  \geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\delta 2^{-j}+\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the first inequality follows from the inductive hypothesis and ( 16.9.22 ). Observe that \[  \eta _ j^{k-1}\lor \varphi _{j+k}\leq \psi _{j+k-1},  \] it follows from proposition 16.3.25 that $\eta _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By theorem 16.3.35 , we deduce that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n\geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{j+k}}^ n+ \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^{k-1}}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k} \delta 2^{-j-a}, \end{aligned}  \] where the second inequality follows from the inductive hypothesis and ( 16.9.22 ). Therefore, ( 16.9.23 ) follows. Step 2.2 . It follows by induction from proposition 16.3.29 that for any $j\geq 1$, $k\geq 0$, \[  P_{\theta }\left[\eta _ j^ k\right]=\eta _ j^ k.  \] By proposition 16.4.4 , we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n  \] for any $j\geq 1$. Letting $k\to \infty $ in ( 16.9.23 ), we find that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\delta 2^{-j}>0  \] for $j\geq 1$. Observe that we also have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n \leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi _ j}^ n  \] for $j\geq 1$ by theorem 13.13.11 . It follows from these inequalities and ( 16.9.19 ) that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\eta _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] For $k\geq 1$, we have \[  \eta _ j^ k=\varphi _ j\land \eta _{j+1}^{k-1}\leq \eta _{j+1}^{k-1}.  \] Letting $k\to \infty $ gives $\eta _ j\leq \eta _{j+1}$. Hence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is increasing. Hence corollary 13.13.12 gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n,  \] where $\eta =\operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} \eta _ j$. For fixed $m$, if $j\geq m$, then $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j\leq \psi _ m$, whereas if $j<m$, then $\eta _ j\leq \eta _ m\leq \psi _ m$. Thus $\eta _ j$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\psi _ m]$ for all $j,m$, and ( 16.9.21 ) gives $\eta \leq \varphi $. It follows from proposition 16.8.7 that $\eta \sim _ P \varphi $. By corollary 16.9.12 and proposition 16.9.6 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. $\square$ Corollary 16.9.24 . 56D1BC5A2B85 Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a Cauchy net (with respect to $d_ S$) in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that there is $\delta >0$ such that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ for all $j\in I$. Then $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ converges with respect to $d_ S$. In particular, if $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is a decreasing net such that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta >0$ for all $j\in I$, then $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ converges with respect to $d_ S$. We can obviously relax the decreasing condition to the following: the $P$-singularity types of $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ are decreasing. Proof. In a pseudometric space, sequential completeness implies completeness for Cauchy nets. So for the first assertion, we may assume that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a Cauchy sequence. We first treat the case of a decreasing sequence $(\gamma _ j)_ j$ with $\int _ X\theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ for all $j$. Put $\tilde\gamma _ j=P_\theta [\gamma _ j]$. Then $(\tilde\gamma _ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials, $d_ S(\gamma _ j,\tilde\gamma _ j)=0$, and \[  \int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] by proposition 16.3.10 . By proposition 16.4.4 , the decreasing limit $\tilde\gamma =\inf _ j\tilde\gamma _ j$ is model and \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma }^ n\geq \delta .  \] Hence $\tilde\gamma _ j\to \tilde\gamma $ in $d_ S$ by corollary 16.9.14 , and therefore $\gamma _ j$ also converges in $d_ S$. Next let $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$ be a $d_ S$-Cauchy sequence with masses bounded from below by $\delta $. Put \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ j=P_\theta [\varphi _ j].  \] By corollary 16.3.20 , example 16.8.6 , proposition 16.9.6 , the $\tilde{\varphi }_ j$'s are model potentials, $d_ S(\varphi _ j,\tilde{\varphi }_ j)=0$, and \[  \int _ X\theta _{\tilde{\varphi }_ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] by proposition 16.3.10 . Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $\tilde{\varphi }_ j$, we may therefore assume that the $\varphi _ j$'s are model potentials. Passing to a subsequence, we may also assume that \[  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\leq C_ n^{-2j},  \] where $C_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.9 . Define \[  \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ k  \] for each $j>0$. As in the proof of proposition 16.9.17 Step 1, especially ( 16.9.20 ), we know that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } d_ S(\varphi _ j,\psi _ j)=0.  \] The sequence $(\psi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing and satisfies $\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ by theorem 13.13.11 . By the first paragraph, $(\psi _ j)_ j$ converges in $d_ S$. Hence the chosen subsequence of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ converges, and the original Cauchy sequence converges as well. Finally, suppose that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is a decreasing net with masses bounded from below by $\delta $. For each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, the net \[  \int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_\theta }^{n-k}  \] is decreasing and bounded from below, hence Cauchy as a real-valued net. If $j'\geq j$, then $\varphi _{j'}\leq \varphi _ j$, and 16.9.7 expresses $d_ S(\varphi _{j'},\varphi _ j)$ as a finite sum of the corresponding differences of these mixed masses. For two sufficiently large indices, we choose a common upper bound in $I$ and use the triangle inequality. It follows that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is $d_ S$-Cauchy. The first assertion gives its convergence. $\square$ Lemma 16.9.25 . 7F9EDAFF39F9 There is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X$ and $\theta $ such that for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, we have \[  d_{S,\theta }\Bigl ((1-\epsilon )\varphi ,\varphi \Bigr )\leq C \epsilon  \] for small enough $\epsilon >0$ such that $(1-\epsilon )\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. After adding a constant, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Since $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, $(1-\epsilon )\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all small enough $\epsilon >0$. Fix such an $\epsilon $. Take any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\omega -\theta $ is still a Kähler form. Note that the choice of $\omega $ depends only on $X$ and $\theta $. Since $\varphi \preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi $, by 16.9.7 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 3 , we can compute \[  \begin{aligned}  d_{S,\theta }\Bigl ((1-\epsilon )\varphi ,\varphi \Bigr )=&  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{(1-\epsilon )\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right)\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \left((1-\epsilon )\theta _{\varphi }+\epsilon \omega \right)^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right)\\  =& \sum _{m=1}^ n c_ m(\varphi )\epsilon ^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where, for $1\leq m\leq n$, \[  c_ m(\varphi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m (-1)^{m-\ell }\binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j-\ell }\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Note that \[  \begin{aligned}  \left|c_ m(\varphi )\right| \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m \binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j-\ell }\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m \binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-\ell } \end{aligned}  \] where we used the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Hence the whole expression is of the order of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon )$, and our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Definition 16.9.2
text: Definition 16.9.2 . 240B1899916C For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\coloneqq d_1(\ell ^{\varphi },\ell ^{\psi }).  \] When we want to be more specific, we write $d_{S,\theta }$ instead of $d_ S$.

title: Proposition 16.9.3
text: Proposition 16.9.3 . 1ABAE06071CD The function $d_ S$ defined in definition 16.9.2 is a pseudometric on $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 17.10.81 . $\square$

title: Lemma 16.9.4
text: Lemma 16.9.4 . 2490CFA511EC Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )+d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi ) \leq C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. Proof. We claim that FE54EE184B7A 16.9.5 \begin{equation}  \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }. \end{equation} Recall that $\lor $ is defined in definition 17.10.85 . Note that this assertion implies our desired inequality by 17.10.90 . In proving this assertion, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$ since \[  \ell ^{\varphi +C}=\ell ^{\varphi },\quad \ell ^{\psi +C}=\ell ^{\psi },\quad \ell ^{(\varphi +C)\lor (\psi +C)}=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }  \] for any $C\in \mathbb {R}$. In fact, it is clear that \[  \ell ^{\varphi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },\quad \ell ^{\psi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },  \] so the $\leq $ direction in ( 16.9.5 ) holds. Conversely, if $\ell '\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta )$ and $\ell '\geq \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }$, then for each $t\geq 0$, \[  \ell '_ t\geq \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \varphi \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \psi \Bigr )=(V_{\theta }-t)\lor (\varphi \lor \psi ).  \] See ( 17.10.96 ) for the first inequality. Therefore, thanks to the definition of the Perron envelopes (cf. ( 17.10.21 )), we have \[  \ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi ,t}_ s  \] for any $0\leq s\leq t$. It follows from ( 17.10.96 ) that $\ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }_ s$ for any $s\geq 0$. $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.5
text: FE54EE184B7A 16.9.5 \begin{equation}  \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 16.9.6
text: Proposition 16.9.6 . C1D8A9BD3B3B Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: CCA0DECFB7E5 $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; A3A85D64324F $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$. In particular, $d_ S(\varphi ,P_{\theta }[\varphi ])=0$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proof. By 16.8.13 , we have $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ if and only if $\varphi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $ and $\psi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $. By 16.9.4 , $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$ if and only if $d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$ and $d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$. So it suffices to prove the assertion when $\varphi \leq \psi $. Assuming this, by proposition 17.10.83 , 2 holds if and only if \[  \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\varphi }\right)= \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\psi }\right),  \] where $\mathbf{E}$ is introduced in definition 17.10.82 . But by ( 17.10.94 ), this holds if and only if \[  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , this holds if and only if for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j},  \] which is equivalent to 1 by proposition 16.8.7 . $\square$

title: Lemma 16.9.7
text: Lemma 16.9.7 . 03FCA1AB2751 Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Proof. Set $\chi \coloneqq \varphi \lor \psi $. By 16.8.13 , we have $\chi \sim _ P\psi $. Hence proposition 16.9.6 gives $d_ S(\chi ,\psi )=0$, and the pseudometric property gives \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=d_ S(\varphi ,\chi ).  \] Since $\varphi \leq \chi $, ( 17.10.94 ) and proposition 17.10.83 give \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\chi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Finally, proposition 16.8.7 applied to $\psi \leq \chi $ gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.8
text: Corollary 16.9.8 . 255A623EA393 Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi ,\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi \preceq _ P \eta $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),\quad d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\psi ,\eta ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of 16.9.7 and the monotonicity theorem proposition 16.8.22 . $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.9
text: Corollary 16.9.9 . B29DCA70A9E6 For any $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have 0AC35440957F 16.9.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left( 2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \right) \\  \leq &  C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{split} \end{equation} where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. In particular, if $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $d_ S$-limit $\varphi $, then for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Proof. The estimates ( 16.9.10 ) follow from the combination of 16.9.7 and 16.9.4 . Suppose that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 16.9.4 . Therefore, theorem 13.13.11 and 16.9.7 imply that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for any $j=0,\ldots ,n$. The last assertion now follows from ( 16.9.10 ) and theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.10
text: 0AC35440957F 16.9.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left( 2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \right) \\  \leq &  C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{split} \end{equation}

title: Corollary 16.9.11
text: Corollary 16.9.11 . 94B2CC4C30BB Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold. Given a net $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, the following are equivalent: $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Proof. It suffices to observe that the middle term in ( 16.9.10 ) is invariant under $\pi ^*$. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.12
text: Corollary 16.9.12 . 77738CEC8071 Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, uniformly bounded from above. Then \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i.  \] Proof. Write $\varphi =\operatorname *{sup}_{j\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ j$. Recall that by proposition 5.14.2 , $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By 16.9.7 , it suffices to show that for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}.  \] The latter follows from corollary 13.13.12 . $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.13
text: Corollary 16.9.13 . D47345F0C3C8 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  \left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n \right|\leq D_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $D_ n=3(n+1)C_ n$ with $C_ n$ being the same constant as in 16.9.4 . Proof. We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n \right|\leq &  \left|2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\right| + 2\left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\right|\\  \leq &  (n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )+2(n+1) d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )\\  \leq &  (n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )+2(n+1)C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{aligned}  \] where the first line is just the triangle inequality, the second line follows from corollary 16.9.9 and the third line follows from 16.9.4 . $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.14
text: Corollary 16.9.14 . F84D53FDA599 Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  \varphi _ j\preceq _ P\varphi _ i  \] whenever $j\geq i$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that $\varphi \preceq _ P\varphi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then the following are equivalent: 3D1A7D703ADF We have \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi ;  \] 919198E0409A for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have E95AEF6203E2 16.9.15 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}. \end{equation} If we assume furthermore that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$, then the above conditions are equivalent to the following: 8DEC59327E72 We have \[  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] When $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$ and these equivalent conditions are met, we also have FC1B825A9516 16.9.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\inf _{j\in I}P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]. \end{equation} Proof. 1 $\iff $ 2 . This follows immediately from 16.9.7 . Assume that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This is the case $k=n$ in ( 16.9.15 ). 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume (3). If for some $i\in I$, $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$, then for all $j\geq i$ we have \[  \varphi \preceq _ P\varphi _ j\preceq _ P\varphi _ i.  \] Hence $\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ by proposition 16.8.22 . It follows from proposition 16.8.7 that $\varphi _ j\sim _ P\varphi $, and (2) follows from proposition 16.3.10 . So in the sequel, we shall assume that for all $i\in I$, we have $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$. In particular, each $\varphi _ i$ has positive mass. Let $(b_ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net converging to $\infty $ such that \[  b_ j\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right).  \] This can be achieved for example by taking $b_ j$ as the midpoint of this interval. By theorem 16.8.23 , for each $j\in I$, we can find $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  b_ j^{-1}\eta _ j +\left(1-b_ j^{-1}\right)\varphi _ j \leq \varphi .  \] It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that for any $k=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}\geq \left(1-b_ j^{-1}\right)^ k\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}.  \] Taking the limit, we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 16.9.15 ). The $\geq $ direction follows from proposition 16.8.22 . Finally, we argue ( 16.9.16 ). Let $\psi _ j=P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]$. It follows from corollary 16.3.20 that $\psi _ j$ is a model potential. Since the net $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder, $(\psi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is decreasing pointwise. Let \[  \psi =\inf _{j\in I}\psi _ j\geq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By proposition 16.4.3 , $\psi $ is a model potential. Since $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq \psi \leq \psi _ j$ for all $j\in I$, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 16.3.10 give \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\psi _ j}^ n=\lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Hence $\psi $ has the same mass as $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. As $\psi $ is model and $\psi \geq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, theorem 16.3.15 gives $\psi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.15
text: E95AEF6203E2 16.9.15 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}. \end{equation}

title: Equation 16.9.16
text: FC1B825A9516 16.9.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\inf _{j\in I}P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 16.9.17
text: Proposition 16.9.17 . 1DEED63B61B0 Let $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ ($j\geq 1$), $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Assume that there is $\delta >0$ such that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] for all $j$ and the $\varphi _ j$'s are all model potentials. Then up to replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there is a decreasing sequence $(\psi _ j)_ j$ and an increasing sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that 36F21B225E6D $\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; 1EE77849B2C2 $\psi _ j\geq \varphi _ j\geq \eta _ j$ for all $j$. In fact, for any $j\geq 1$, we will take \[  \eta _ j=\inf _{k\in \mathbb {N}}\varphi _ j\land \varphi _{j+1}\land \cdots \land \varphi _{j+k},\quad \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ k.  \] Proof. First note that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq \delta $ as well, due to the $d_ S$-continuity of non-pluripolar masses as proved in corollary 16.9.13 . Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, we may then assume that $\varphi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We are free to replace $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence. So we may assume that 2902F1B6C4A6 16.9.18 \begin{equation}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-4}}{D_ n C_ n^{j+1}},\quad d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi _ j)\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-4}}{D_ n}, \end{equation} where $C_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.9 , $D_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.13 . In particular, by corollary 16.9.13 , 67C255B50420 16.9.19 \begin{equation}  \left|\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\right|\leq \delta 2^{-j-4}. \end{equation} Step 1 . We handle the $\psi _ j$'s. For each $j\geq 1$ and $k\geq 1$, by 16.9.4 we have \[  \begin{aligned}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}) & \leq C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k})\\ & \leq C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\\ & \quad + C_ n\, d_ S(\varphi _{j+1},\varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}). \end{aligned}  \] By iteration, we find \[  \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k})\leq \sum _{a=j}^{j+k-1}C_ n^{a+1-j}d_ S(\varphi _ a,\varphi _{a+1})\\  \leq \frac{C_ n^{-j}}{D_ n}\sum _{a=j}^{j+k-1}\delta 2^{-a-4}\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-3}}{D_ n}. \end{split}  \] Using corollary 16.9.12 , we have \[  \varphi _ j\lor \varphi _{j+1}\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _{j+k}\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ j  \] as $k\to \infty $. Hence 3B96A5372D55 16.9.20 \begin{equation}  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\psi _ j)\leq \frac{\delta 2^{-j-3}}{D_ n}. \end{equation} We conclude that $\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Moreover, we observe that 79C50CD3AC3E 16.9.21 \begin{equation}  \varphi =\inf _{j\geq 1} P_{\theta }[\psi _ j] \end{equation} Indeed, set $\tilde{\psi }_ j=P_{\theta }[\psi _ j]$. Then $(\tilde{\psi }_ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials, and $d_ S(\tilde{\psi }_ j,\psi _ j)=0$ by proposition 16.9.6 . Hence $\tilde{\psi }_ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. If $\chi =\inf _ j\tilde{\psi }_ j$, then proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 give $\tilde{\psi }_ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\chi $. Thus $d_ S(\chi ,\varphi )=0$. Since both $\chi $ and $\varphi $ are model potentials, proposition 16.9.6 gives $P_{\theta }[\chi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, hence $\chi =\varphi $, proving ( 16.9.21 ). Step 2 . We consider the $\eta _ j$'s. For each $j\geq 1$ and $k\geq 0$, we let \[  \eta _ j^ k\coloneqq \varphi _ j\land \cdots \land \varphi _{j+k}.  \] Using ( 16.9.18 ), ( 16.9.20 ) and corollary 16.9.13 , we have \[  \left|\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n \right|\leq \delta 2^{-j-2}  \] for all $j\geq 1$. Taking ( 16.9.19 ) into account, we have 9F803C97D29B 16.9.22 \begin{equation}  \left|\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j-1}}^ n \right|\leq \delta 2^{-j} \end{equation} for $j>1$. Step 2.1 . We claim that for a fixed $j\geq 1$, for any $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we have $\eta _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and A82EF3572727 16.9.23 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k} \delta 2^{-j-a}. \end{equation} We argue by induction on $k\geq 0$. The case $k=0$ is trivial. When $k>0$, assume that the case $k-1$ is known. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^{k-1}}^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{j+k}}^ n \geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k-1}\delta 2^{-j-a}+\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n-\delta 2^{-j-k}\\  \geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\delta 2^{-j}+\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the first inequality follows from the inductive hypothesis and ( 16.9.22 ). Observe that \[  \eta _ j^{k-1}\lor \varphi _{j+k}\leq \psi _{j+k-1},  \] it follows from proposition 16.3.25 that $\eta _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By theorem 16.3.35 , we deduce that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n\geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{j+k}}^ n+ \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^{k-1}}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi _{j+k-1}}^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\sum _{a=1}^{k} \delta 2^{-j-a}, \end{aligned}  \] where the second inequality follows from the inductive hypothesis and ( 16.9.22 ). Therefore, ( 16.9.23 ) follows. Step 2.2 . It follows by induction from proposition 16.3.29 that for any $j\geq 1$, $k\geq 0$, \[  P_{\theta }\left[\eta _ j^ k\right]=\eta _ j^ k.  \] By proposition 16.4.4 , we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j^ k}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n  \] for any $j\geq 1$. Letting $k\to \infty $ in ( 16.9.23 ), we find that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\delta 2^{-j}>0  \] for $j\geq 1$. Observe that we also have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n \leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi _ j}^ n  \] for $j\geq 1$ by theorem 13.13.11 . It follows from these inequalities and ( 16.9.19 ) that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\eta _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] For $k\geq 1$, we have \[  \eta _ j^ k=\varphi _ j\land \eta _{j+1}^{k-1}\leq \eta _{j+1}^{k-1}.  \] Letting $k\to \infty $ gives $\eta _ j\leq \eta _{j+1}$. Hence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is increasing. Hence corollary 13.13.12 gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\eta _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n,  \] where $\eta =\operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} \eta _ j$. For fixed $m$, if $j\geq m$, then $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j\leq \psi _ m$, whereas if $j<m$, then $\eta _ j\leq \eta _ m\leq \psi _ m$. Thus $\eta _ j$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\psi _ m]$ for all $j,m$, and ( 16.9.21 ) gives $\eta \leq \varphi $. It follows from proposition 16.8.7 that $\eta \sim _ P \varphi $. By corollary 16.9.12 and proposition 16.9.6 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.24
text: Corollary 16.9.24 . 56D1BC5A2B85 Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a Cauchy net (with respect to $d_ S$) in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that there is $\delta >0$ such that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ for all $j\in I$. Then $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ converges with respect to $d_ S$. In particular, if $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is a decreasing net such that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta >0$ for all $j\in I$, then $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ converges with respect to $d_ S$. Proof. In a pseudometric space, sequential completeness implies completeness for Cauchy nets. So for the first assertion, we may assume that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a Cauchy sequence. We first treat the case of a decreasing sequence $(\gamma _ j)_ j$ with $\int _ X\theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ for all $j$. Put $\tilde\gamma _ j=P_\theta [\gamma _ j]$. Then $(\tilde\gamma _ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials, $d_ S(\gamma _ j,\tilde\gamma _ j)=0$, and \[  \int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] by proposition 16.3.10 . By proposition 16.4.4 , the decreasing limit $\tilde\gamma =\inf _ j\tilde\gamma _ j$ is model and \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma _ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\tilde\gamma }^ n\geq \delta .  \] Hence $\tilde\gamma _ j\to \tilde\gamma $ in $d_ S$ by corollary 16.9.14 , and therefore $\gamma _ j$ also converges in $d_ S$. Next let $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$ be a $d_ S$-Cauchy sequence with masses bounded from below by $\delta $. Put \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ j=P_\theta [\varphi _ j].  \] By corollary 16.3.20 , example 16.8.6 , proposition 16.9.6 , the $\tilde{\varphi }_ j$'s are model potentials, $d_ S(\varphi _ j,\tilde{\varphi }_ j)=0$, and \[  \int _ X\theta _{\tilde{\varphi }_ j}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq \delta  \] by proposition 16.3.10 . Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $\tilde{\varphi }_ j$, we may therefore assume that the $\varphi _ j$'s are model potentials. Passing to a subsequence, we may also assume that \[  d_ S(\varphi _ j,\varphi _{j+1})\leq C_ n^{-2j},  \] where $C_ n$ is the constant in corollary 16.9.9 . Define \[  \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ k  \] for each $j>0$. As in the proof of proposition 16.9.17 Step 1, especially ( 16.9.20 ), we know that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } d_ S(\varphi _ j,\psi _ j)=0.  \] The sequence $(\psi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing and satisfies $\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ j}^ n\geq \delta $ by theorem 13.13.11 . By the first paragraph, $(\psi _ j)_ j$ converges in $d_ S$. Hence the chosen subsequence of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ converges, and the original Cauchy sequence converges as well. Finally, suppose that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is a decreasing net with masses bounded from below by $\delta $. For each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, the net \[  \int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_\theta }^{n-k}  \] is decreasing and bounded from below, hence Cauchy as a real-valued net. If $j'\geq j$, then $\varphi _{j'}\leq \varphi _ j$, and 16.9.7 expresses $d_ S(\varphi _{j'},\varphi _ j)$ as a finite sum of the corresponding differences of these mixed masses. For two sufficiently large indices, we choose a common upper bound in $I$ and use the triangle inequality. It follows that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ is $d_ S$-Cauchy. The first assertion gives its convergence. $\square$

title: Lemma 16.9.25
text: Lemma 16.9.25 . 7F9EDAFF39F9 There is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X$ and $\theta $ such that for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, we have \[  d_{S,\theta }\Bigl ((1-\epsilon )\varphi ,\varphi \Bigr )\leq C \epsilon  \] for small enough $\epsilon >0$ such that $(1-\epsilon )\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. After adding a constant, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Since $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, $(1-\epsilon )\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all small enough $\epsilon >0$. Fix such an $\epsilon $. Take any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\omega -\theta $ is still a Kähler form. Note that the choice of $\omega $ depends only on $X$ and $\theta $. Since $\varphi \preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi $, by 16.9.7 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 3 , we can compute \[  \begin{aligned}  d_{S,\theta }\Bigl ((1-\epsilon )\varphi ,\varphi \Bigr )=&  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{(1-\epsilon )\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right)\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \left((1-\epsilon )\theta _{\varphi }+\epsilon \omega \right)^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right)\\  =& \sum _{m=1}^ n c_ m(\varphi )\epsilon ^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where, for $1\leq m\leq n$, \[  c_ m(\varphi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m (-1)^{m-\ell }\binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j-\ell }\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Note that \[  \begin{aligned}  \left|c_ m(\varphi )\right| \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m \binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j-\ell }\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=m}^ n \binom {j}{m} \sum _{\ell =0}^ m \binom {m}{\ell } \int _ X \omega ^\ell \wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-\ell } \end{aligned}  \] where we used the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Hence the whole expression is of the order of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon )$, and our assertion follows. $\square$

title: 16.9.26 Convergence theorems
text: Next we establish some important convergence theorems, allowing us to effectively manipulate the $d_ S$-convergence. Lemma 16.9.27 . 51EA136E15FA Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then for any $t\in (0,1]$, \[  (1-t)\varphi _ i+ tV_{\theta }\xrightarrow {d_ S}(1-t)\varphi + tV_{\theta }.  \] When $t=1$, the sum is understood as in 13.13.6 . Proof. Fix $t\in (0,1]$. We write \[  \varphi _{i,t}=(1-t)\varphi _ i+ tV_{\theta },\quad \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi + tV_{\theta }  \] for any $i\in I$. By corollary 16.9.9 , it suffices to show that for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, D81A5AAFDA65 16.9.28 \begin{equation}  2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}\lor \varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\to 0. \end{equation} Observe that \[  \varphi _{i,t}\lor \varphi _ t=(1-t)(\varphi \lor \varphi _ i)+t V_{\theta }.  \] So after binomial expansion, ( 16.9.28 ) follows from corollary 16.9.9 . $\square$ Lemma 16.9.29 . 2E78B4FEFFF9 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. For each $t\in (0,1)$, let $\varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t V_{\theta }$. Then \[  \varphi _ t\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi  \] as $t\to 0+$. Proof. Since $\varphi \preceq \varphi _ t$, by 16.9.7 , we need to show that for each $j=1,\dots ,n$, we have \[  \lim _{t\to 0+} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] For this purpose, we compute \[  \begin{aligned} &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}- \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  =& \left((1-t)^ j-1\right)\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\ & +\sum _{i=0}^{j-1} \binom {j}{i}(1-t)^ i t^{j-i}\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ i\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-i}. \end{aligned}  \] As $t\to 0+$, the right-hand side clearly tends to $0$. $\square$ The following convergence theorem lies at the heart of the whole theory. Theorem 16.9.30 . 713B9E26113B Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 3F8CB8C5B9A5 16.9.31 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\in I}\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}=\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} Proof. Since $d_ S$ is a pseudometric, in order to establish the continuity of mixed masses, it suffices to consider sequences instead of nets. So we may assume that $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as ordered sets. Step 1 . We reduce to the case where $\varphi _ j^ k,\varphi _ j$ all have positive masses and there is a constant $\delta >0$ such that for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$ and $k\in I$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{j,\varphi _ j^ k}^ n>\delta .  \] Assuming in this case, the theorem has been proved, let us handle the general case. Take $t\in (0,1)$. By 16.9.27 , we have \[  (1-t)\varphi _ j^ k+tV_{\theta _ j}\xrightarrow {d_ S}(1-t)\varphi _ j+tV_{\theta _ j}  \] as $k\to \infty $ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Note that for all $k\in I$, \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{j,(1-t)\varphi _ j^ k+tV_{\theta _ j}}\geq t^ n\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta _ j}}^ n>0.  \] Assume that we have proved the special case of the theorem, we have \[  \begin{split} & \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{1,(1-t)\varphi _1^ k+tV_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(1-t)\varphi _ n^ k+tV_{\theta _ n}}\\  =& \int _ X\theta _{1,(1-t)\varphi _1+tV_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(1-t)\varphi _ n+tV_{\theta _ n}}. \end{split}  \] More explicitly, for fixed $k$ the left-hand side is the value at $t$ of a polynomial $Q_ k(t)$ of degree at most $n$, and the right-hand side is the value of a polynomial $Q(t)$ of degree at most $n$. Choose $n+1$ distinct numbers $t_0,\ldots ,t_ n\in (0,1)$. Lagrange interpolation expresses $Q_ k(0)-Q(0)$ as a fixed linear combination of the numbers $Q_ k(t_ a)-Q(t_ a)$, which tend to $0$. Hence the same formula holds at $t=0$. From this, ( 16.9.31 ) follows. Step 2 . We now assume that the assumptions mentioned at the beginning of Step 1 are met. Note that we may assume that $\varphi _ j^ k$, $\varphi _ j$ are model potentials for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$, $k>0$ by proposition 16.9.6 and corollary 16.3.20 . We first handle the following monotone situation. Assume that, for each fixed $i$, the sequence $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$ is either increasing or decreasing. Let $\tilde{\varphi }_ i$ denote its pointwise limit, namely \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ i=\inf _{k>0}\varphi _ i^ k  \] in the decreasing case and \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{k>0}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i^ k  \] in the increasing case. We assume moreover that $\tilde{\varphi }_ i\sim _ P\varphi _ i$ for every $i$. Since mixed non-pluripolar masses are invariant under replacing each entry by a $P$-equivalent potential, it suffices in this monotone situation to prove convergence to the mixed mass of the $\tilde{\varphi }_ i$'s. After reordering the indices, we may assume that there is $i_0\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $ such that $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$ is decreasing for $i\leq i_0$ and increasing for $i>i_0$.
