As $\epsilon \to 0$ (from both sides), we have 11D8415D35F8 16.9.51 \begin{equation}  V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }\xlongrightarrow {d_ S}V_{\theta }. \end{equation} Proof. There are two assertions to prove, as detailed in the two steps. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\epsilon \to 0+$. In this case ( 16.9.51 ) means \[  V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }\xlongrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}V_{\theta }  \] as $\epsilon \to 0+$. So thanks to corollary 16.9.14 and proposition 16.4.4 , it suffices to prove the following: E3D4ADBA54B9 16.9.52 \begin{equation}  \inf _{\epsilon >0} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta } \right]. \end{equation} First observe that \[  V_{\theta }=\inf _{\epsilon >0} V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }.  \] In fact, the $\leq $ direction is trivial. As for the reverse inequality, it suffices to observe that the right-hand side lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Therefore, due to proposition 16.4.4 , \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ X \left( \theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Therefore, for all $\epsilon >0$ small enough, we can find $\eta _{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon \omega )$ and $a_{\epsilon }>0$ decreasing to $0$ so that \[  (1-a_\epsilon )V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } + a_\epsilon \eta _\epsilon \leq V_{\theta }.  \] Therefore, thanks to proposition 16.4.2 , \[  (1-a_\epsilon )P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right] + a_\epsilon P_{\theta +\omega }\left[\eta _\epsilon \right] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\left[V_{\theta }\right].  \] Since the envelopes $P_{\theta +\omega }[\eta _\epsilon ]$ have supremum $0$, they are uniformly bounded in $L^1$ by proposition 5.17.3 ; hence $a_\epsilon P_{\theta +\omega }[\eta _\epsilon ]\to 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $\epsilon \to 0$ and using proposition 5.14.6 , we conclude ( 16.9.52 ). Step 2 . We then handle the case where $\epsilon \to 0-$. In this case, ( 16.9.51 ) simply means \[  V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}V_{\theta }  \] as $\epsilon \to 0+$. But this follows from corollary 16.9.12 if we can prove 4D05EB795FC2 16.9.53 \begin{equation}  \operatorname *{sup}_{\epsilon >0}{}\! {}^{*} V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }=V_{\theta }, \end{equation} where we understand that $\epsilon $ is small enough so that $\theta -\epsilon \omega $ represents a big cohomology class. Since $\{ \theta \} $ is big, we can find $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ so that \[  \varphi \leq 0,\quad \theta _{\varphi }\geq \delta \omega  \] for some $\delta >0$. For a small $\epsilon >0$, we then have \[  \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \left(1-\frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\right)V_{\theta }+ \frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\varphi \right)\geq \epsilon \omega .  \] Therefore, \[  \left(1-\frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\right)V_{\theta }+ \frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\varphi \leq V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }.  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, we then find \[  V_{\theta }\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{\epsilon >0}{}\! {}^{*} V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }.  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, hence ( 16.9.53 ) is established. $\square$

title: Lemma 16.9.27
text: Lemma 16.9.27 . 51EA136E15FA Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then for any $t\in (0,1]$, \[  (1-t)\varphi _ i+ tV_{\theta }\xrightarrow {d_ S}(1-t)\varphi + tV_{\theta }.  \] Proof. Fix $t\in (0,1]$. We write \[  \varphi _{i,t}=(1-t)\varphi _ i+ tV_{\theta },\quad \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi + tV_{\theta }  \] for any $i\in I$. By corollary 16.9.9 , it suffices to show that for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, D81A5AAFDA65 16.9.28 \begin{equation}  2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}\lor \varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\to 0. \end{equation} Observe that \[  \varphi _{i,t}\lor \varphi _ t=(1-t)(\varphi \lor \varphi _ i)+t V_{\theta }.  \] So after binomial expansion, ( 16.9.28 ) follows from corollary 16.9.9 . $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.28
text: D81A5AAFDA65 16.9.28 \begin{equation}  2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}\lor \varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _{i,t}}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\to 0. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 16.9.29
text: Lemma 16.9.29 . 2E78B4FEFFF9 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. For each $t\in (0,1)$, let $\varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t V_{\theta }$. Then \[  \varphi _ t\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi  \] as $t\to 0+$. Proof. Since $\varphi \preceq \varphi _ t$, by 16.9.7 , we need to show that for each $j=1,\dots ,n$, we have \[  \lim _{t\to 0+} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] For this purpose, we compute \[  \begin{aligned} &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}- \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  =& \left((1-t)^ j-1\right)\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\ & +\sum _{i=0}^{j-1} \binom {j}{i}(1-t)^ i t^{j-i}\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ i\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-i}. \end{aligned}  \] As $t\to 0+$, the right-hand side clearly tends to $0$. $\square$

title: Theorem 16.9.30
text: Theorem 16.9.30 . 713B9E26113B Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 3F8CB8C5B9A5 16.9.31 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\in I}\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}=\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} Proof. Since $d_ S$ is a pseudometric, in order to establish the continuity of mixed masses, it suffices to consider sequences instead of nets. So we may assume that $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as ordered sets. Step 1 . We reduce to the case where $\varphi _ j^ k,\varphi _ j$ all have positive masses and there is a constant $\delta >0$ such that for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$ and $k\in I$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{j,\varphi _ j^ k}^ n>\delta .  \] Assuming in this case, the theorem has been proved, let us handle the general case. Take $t\in (0,1)$. By 16.9.27 , we have \[  (1-t)\varphi _ j^ k+tV_{\theta _ j}\xrightarrow {d_ S}(1-t)\varphi _ j+tV_{\theta _ j}  \] as $k\to \infty $ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Note that for all $k\in I$, \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{j,(1-t)\varphi _ j^ k+tV_{\theta _ j}}\geq t^ n\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta _ j}}^ n>0.  \] Assume that we have proved the special case of the theorem, we have \[  \begin{split} & \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{1,(1-t)\varphi _1^ k+tV_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(1-t)\varphi _ n^ k+tV_{\theta _ n}}\\  =& \int _ X\theta _{1,(1-t)\varphi _1+tV_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(1-t)\varphi _ n+tV_{\theta _ n}}. \end{split}  \] More explicitly, for fixed $k$ the left-hand side is the value at $t$ of a polynomial $Q_ k(t)$ of degree at most $n$, and the right-hand side is the value of a polynomial $Q(t)$ of degree at most $n$. Choose $n+1$ distinct numbers $t_0,\ldots ,t_ n\in (0,1)$. Lagrange interpolation expresses $Q_ k(0)-Q(0)$ as a fixed linear combination of the numbers $Q_ k(t_ a)-Q(t_ a)$, which tend to $0$. Hence the same formula holds at $t=0$. From this, ( 16.9.31 ) follows. Step 2 . We now assume that the assumptions mentioned at the beginning of Step 1 are met. Note that we may assume that $\varphi _ j^ k$, $\varphi _ j$ are model potentials for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$, $k>0$ by proposition 16.9.6 and corollary 16.3.20 . We first handle the following monotone situation. Assume that, for each fixed $i$, the sequence $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$ is either increasing or decreasing. Let $\tilde{\varphi }_ i$ denote its pointwise limit, namely \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ i=\inf _{k>0}\varphi _ i^ k  \] in the decreasing case and \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{k>0}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i^ k  \] in the increasing case. We assume moreover that $\tilde{\varphi }_ i\sim _ P\varphi _ i$ for every $i$. Since mixed non-pluripolar masses are invariant under replacing each entry by a $P$-equivalent potential, it suffices in this monotone situation to prove convergence to the mixed mass of the $\tilde{\varphi }_ i$'s. After reordering the indices, we may assume that there is $i_0\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $ such that $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$ is decreasing for $i\leq i_0$ and increasing for $i>i_0$. Therefore, for each $k>0$, using theorem 13.13.11 , we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\geq \int _ X \theta _{1,\tilde{\varphi }_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{i_0,\tilde{\varphi }_{i_0}}\wedge \theta _{i_0+1,\varphi ^ k_{i_0+1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}.  \] Using corollary 13.13.12 , we therefore conclude that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\geq \int _ X \theta _{1,\tilde{\varphi }_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\tilde{\varphi }_ n}.  \] It remains to prove DDD39F87B553 16.9.32 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\tilde{\varphi }_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\tilde{\varphi }_ n}. \end{equation} By theorem 13.13.11 , for each $k>0$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{i_0,\varphi _{i_0}^ k}\wedge \theta _{i_0+1,\tilde{\varphi }_{i_0+1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\tilde{\varphi }_{n}}.  \] When proving ( 16.9.32 ), we may replace $\varphi _ j^ k$ by $\tilde{\varphi }_ j$ whenever $j>i_0$, $k>0$. Thus, we are reduced to the case where for all $i$, $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$ is decreasing. By proposition 16.4.4 , the masses $\int _ X\theta _{i,\varphi _ i^ k}^ n$ decrease to $\int _ X\theta _{i,\tilde{\varphi }_ i}^ n$. Hence, thanks to 13.13.30 , for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we may take an increasing sequence $(b^ k_ i)_ k$ tending to $\infty $ satisfying \[  b_ i^ k\in \left(1, \left( \frac{\int _ X \theta _{i,\varphi _ i^ k}^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{i,\varphi _ i^ k}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{i,\tilde{\varphi }_ i}^ n} \right)^{1/n} \right)  \] where the upper endpoint is understood as $\infty $ if the denominator is $0$. For each such $b_ i^ k$, 13.13.30 gives $\rho _ i^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ with \[  (b^ k_ i)^{-1}\rho _ i^ k+\left(1-(b^ k_ i)^{-1}\right)\varphi _ i^ k\leq \tilde{\varphi }_ i.  \] Then by theorem 13.13.11 again, \[  \prod _{i=1}^ n\left(1-(b^ k_ i)^{-1}\right)\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\tilde{\varphi }_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\tilde{\varphi }_ n}.  \] Letting $k\to \infty $, we conclude ( 16.9.32 ). This proves the monotone situation. We now return to the general case. It suffices to prove that any subsequence of \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}  \] has a further subsequence converging to the desired limit. Starting with an arbitrary subsequence, we pass to a further subsequence, still indexed by $k$, so that the construction in proposition 16.9.17 applies simultaneously to the finitely many sequences $(\varphi _ i^ k)_ k$, $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Thus, after discarding finitely many terms and relabeling, for each $i$ there are model potentials $\eta _ i^ k,\psi _ i^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ such that $(\eta _ i^ k)_ k$ is increasing, $(\psi _ i^ k)_ k$ is decreasing, and \[  \eta _ i^ k\leq \varphi _ i^ k\leq \psi _ i^ k,\quad \eta _ i^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ i,\quad \psi _ i^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ i.  \] For the upper sequence, we take $\psi _ i^ k=P_{\theta _ i}[\operatorname *{sup}_{\ell \geq k}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i^\ell ]$; as in ( 16.9.21 ), this gives $\inf _ k\psi _ i^ k=\varphi _ i$. For the lower sequence, the construction in proposition 16.9.17 together with proposition 16.4.3 shows that the $\eta _ i^ k$'s are model after discarding finitely many terms, and the proof of proposition 16.9.17 shows that their increasing limit is $P$-equivalent to $\varphi _ i$. By theorem 13.13.11 , for every $k$, \[  \int _ X\theta _{1,\eta _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\eta _ n^ k} \leq \int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \leq \int _ X\theta _{1,\psi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n^ k}.  \] The monotone situation just proved applies to both the lower and upper sequences, and both limiting mixed masses are equal to \[  \int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] The squeeze theorem therefore gives the desired convergence along this further subsequence. This concludes the proof. $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.31
text: 3F8CB8C5B9A5 16.9.31 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\in I}\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}=\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Equation 16.9.32
text: DDD39F87B553 16.9.32 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\tilde{\varphi }_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\tilde{\varphi }_ n}. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 16.9.33
text: Corollary 16.9.33 . 6C532715D3CD Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: 28F7794ED0EE $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; CE229E338F57 $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ and F98DF8D2E20D 16.9.34 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \end{equation} for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$; 90CB70DBE452 for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, ( 16.9.34 ) holds and 217CFC062068 16.9.35 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation} Proof. The equivalence between 2 and 3 follows directly from 16.9.7 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . That $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ follows from corollary 16.9.9 . While ( 16.9.34 ) follows from theorem 16.9.30 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . By ( 16.9.10 ), we need to show that for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\to 0.  \] This follows from theorem 16.9.30 and ( 16.9.34 ). $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.34
text: F98DF8D2E20D 16.9.34 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \end{equation}

title: Equation 16.9.35
text: 217CFC062068 16.9.35 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 16.9.36
text: Corollary 16.9.36 . 3EB846B21817 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: 9F20E828AA4A $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}\varphi $; 952942BD613A $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}\varphi $. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . It suffices to show that for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \begin{split}  2\int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}-\int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}\\  -\int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{\varphi }^ j\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}\to 0. \end{split}  \] Note that this quantity is a linear combination of terms of the following form: \[  \begin{split}  2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ r\wedge \omega ^{j-r}\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ r\wedge \omega ^{j-r}\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}\\  -\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ r\wedge \omega ^{j-r}\wedge (\theta +\omega )_{V_{\theta +\omega }}^{n-j}, \end{split}  \] where $r=0,\ldots ,j$. By theorem 16.9.30 , it suffices to show that $\varphi \lor \varphi _ i \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. But this follows from corollary 16.9.33 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . From the direction we already proved, for each $C\geq 1$, we have \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +C\omega }}\varphi .  \] By theorem 16.9.30 , it follows that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X (\theta +C\omega )_{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X (\theta +C\omega )_{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. It follows that B509AA3C2576 16.9.37 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation} By corollary 16.9.33 , it remains to show that $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}\varphi $. By corollary 16.9.33 again, we know that $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}\varphi $. So it suffices to apply ( 16.9.37 ) to $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi $ instead of $\varphi _ i$, and we conclude by 16.9.7 . $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.37
text: B509AA3C2576 16.9.37 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 16.9.38
text: Corollary 16.9.38 . B1559025EC82 Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Define $\varphi _ t=t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0$ for $t\in (0,1)$. Then \[  \varphi _ t\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _0  \] as $t\to 0+$. Proof. First note that for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _0}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] So thanks to corollary 16.9.33 , it remains to argue that for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ t\lor \varphi _0}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _0}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Observe that for $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \varphi _ t\lor \varphi _0=t(\varphi _1\lor \varphi _0)+(1-t)\varphi _0,  \] so the desired limit follows by the same binomial expansion. $\square$

title: Corollary 16.9.39
text: Corollary 16.9.39 . 300ED38851D0 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}, (\psi _ i)_{i\in I}, (\eta _ i)_{i\in I}$ be three nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that FB107A3F1389 $\psi _ i\preceq _ P \varphi _ i\preceq _ P \eta _ i$ for each $i\in I$; C027488E50E6 $\eta _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi $, $\psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi $. Then $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 , we may replace $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega $, where $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$. In particular, we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i,\eta _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$. By proposition 16.9.6 , we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i,\eta _ i$ are model potentials for all $i\in I$ and hence $\psi _ i \leq \varphi _ i\leq \eta _ i$ for all $i\in I$. It follows from theorem 13.13.11 that for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi _ i}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}\leq \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ i}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}  \] for all $i\in I$. By theorem 16.9.30 , the limits, with respect to $i\in I$, of the two outer terms are $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}$. It follows that EDB32DFBA6A5 16.9.40 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}. \end{equation} By corollary 16.9.33 , it remains to prove that $\varphi _ i \lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. By corollary 16.9.33 and proposition 16.8.28 , up to replacing $\psi _ i$ (resp. $\varphi _ i$, $\eta _ i$) by $\psi _ i\lor \varphi $ (resp. $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi $, $\eta _ i\lor \varphi $), we may assume from the beginning that $\psi _ i,\varphi _ i,\eta _ i\geq \varphi $. Now $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by ( 16.9.40 ) and 16.9.7 . $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.40
text: EDB32DFBA6A5 16.9.40 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 16.9.41
text: Lemma 16.9.41 . F0C01F4F75EB Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Fix $\lambda >0$. Then the following are equivalent: 9CF34F7033CA $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}\varphi $; 1FA7990ED285 $\lambda \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S,\lambda \theta }}\lambda \varphi $. Proof. We have $V_{\lambda \theta }=\lambda V_{\theta }$. The middle expression in ( 16.9.10 ) for the pair $(\lambda \varphi _ i,\lambda \varphi )$ in the class $\lambda \theta $ is therefore $\lambda ^ n$ times the corresponding expression for $(\varphi _ i,\varphi )$ in the class $\theta $. The equivalence follows from corollary 16.9.9 . $\square$

title: Proposition 16.9.42
text: Proposition 16.9.42 . FDEBDB1E8A22 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ (resp. $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$) be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ i \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ (resp. $\psi _ i \xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$). Then \[  \varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \lor \psi .  \] Proof. Since $d_ S$ is a pseudometric, we may assume that both nets are actually sequences and $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. By corollary 16.9.36 , we may assume that the masses $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$, $\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n>0$. By proposition 16.9.6 and proposition 16.8.28 , replacing all potentials by their $P$-envelopes changes neither the hypotheses nor the conclusion. Thus we may assume that the $\varphi _ j$'s, the $\psi _ j$'s, $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are all model. After discarding finitely many terms, the masses of the two sequences are bounded below by a positive constant. Applying proposition 16.9.17 to both sequences and using the sandwich criterion corollary 16.9.39 , it is enough to treat the case where each of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ and $(\psi _ j)_ j$ is monotone. In this reduced situation, $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ (resp. $(\psi _ j)_ j$) converges to $\varphi $ (resp. $\psi $) almost everywhere due to proposition 16.9.47 , corollary 16.9.12 and proposition 16.4.9 . We handle three cases separately. Step 1 . Assume that both sequences are increasing. In this case, we have $\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j\nearrow \varphi \lor \psi $ almost everywhere. Therefore, $\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi \lor \psi $ by corollary 16.9.12 . Step 2 . Assume that one sequence, say $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is increasing while the other is decreasing. Then we have \[  \varphi _ j \lor \psi \leq \varphi _ j \lor \psi _ j \leq \varphi \lor \psi _ j.  \] Thanks to corollary 16.9.39 , it suffices to show that both sides converge to $\varphi \lor \psi $ with respect to $d_ S$. So we reduce to the case where both sequences are decreasing. Step 3 . Assume that both sequences are decreasing. In this case, due to corollary 16.9.14 , it suffices to show that 76B405D47467 16.9.43 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n. \end{equation} The $\geq $ direction follows from theorem 13.13.11 ; it remains to argue the $\leq $ direction. Thanks to 13.13.30 , we may find a sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $(0,1)$ with limit $0$ and a sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  (1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j+\epsilon _ j \eta _ j \leq \varphi ,\quad \eta _ j \leq \varphi _ j.  \] It follows that for each $j\geq 1$, we have \[  (1-\epsilon _ j)(\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j)+\epsilon _ j \eta _ j \leq \varphi \lor \psi _ j.  \] Therefore by theorem 13.13.11 , \[  (1-\epsilon _ j)^ n \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j}^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi _ j}^ n.  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, we find that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j}^ n\leq \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi _ j}^ n.  \] Therefore, in order to prove ( 16.9.43 ), we may assume that one of the sequences is constant; let us say $\psi _ j=\psi $ for all $j$. Repeating the same argument as before and constructing $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$, $(\eta _ j)_ j$ as above, we get \[  (1-\epsilon _ j)^ n \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j\lor \psi }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n.  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude ( 16.9.43 ). $\square$

title: Proposition 16.9.44
text: Proposition 16.9.44 . 362688C3DDC9 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$, $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Proof. It follows from proposition 16.9.42 that \[  \varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \lor \psi .  \] By 16.8.13 , we have $\varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i\sim _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. In particular, by proposition 16.9.6 , \[  \varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi .  \] By proposition 16.9.6 again, $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P\psi $ and hence $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ by 16.8.13 . $\square$

title: Theorem 16.9.45
text: Theorem 16.9.45 . 666CDCEAA1BE Let $\theta _1$, $\theta _2$ be smooth real closed $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ (resp. $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$) be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _1)$ (resp. $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _2)$) and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _1)$ (resp. $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _2)$). Consider the following three conditions: 4422A6DE22A7 $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S}}\varphi $; 1FADA39F0DD6 $\psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S}}\psi $; 8A620957BCAE $\varphi _ i+\psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S}}\varphi +\psi $. Then any two of these conditions imply the third. Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 , we may assume that $\theta _1,\theta _2$ are both Kähler forms. We denote them by $\omega _1,\omega _2$ instead. Let $\omega =\omega _1+\omega _2$. 1 + 2 $\implies $ 3 . It suffices to show that for each $r=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  2\int _ X \omega _{(\varphi _ i+\psi _ i)\lor (\varphi +\psi )}^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{\varphi _ i+\psi _ i}^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{\varphi +\psi }^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}\to 0.  \] Observe that for each $i\in I$, \[  (\varphi _ i+\psi _ i)\lor (\varphi +\psi )\leq (\varphi _ i\lor \varphi )+(\psi _ i \lor \psi ).  \] The expression with the actual rooftop is non-negative and is bounded above by the same expression with this larger potential in place of $(\varphi _ i+\psi _ i)\lor (\varphi +\psi )$. Thus, it suffices to show that \[  2\int _ X \omega _{(\varphi _ i\lor \varphi )+(\psi _ i\lor \psi )}^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{\varphi _ i+\psi _ i}^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{\varphi +\psi }^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r}\to 0.  \] The left-hand side is a linear combination of \[  2\int _ X \omega _{1,\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ a\wedge \omega _{2,\psi _ i\lor \psi }^{r-a}\wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{1,\varphi _ i}^ a\wedge \omega _{2,\psi _ i}^{r-a} \wedge \omega ^{n-r}-\int _ X \omega _{1,\varphi }^ a\wedge \omega _{2,\psi }^{r-a} \wedge \omega ^{n-r}  \] with $a=0,\ldots ,r$. Observe that $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ and $\psi _ i\lor \psi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi $ by corollary 16.9.9 , each term tends to $0$ by theorem 16.9.30 . 1 + 3 $\implies $ 2 . For each $C\geq 1$, from the direction we already proved together with 16.9.41 , \[  C\varphi _ i+\psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_{S}} C\varphi +\psi .  \] By theorem 16.9.30 , for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \begin{split} & \lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \Bigl (C\omega _1+\omega _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(C\varphi _ i+\psi _ i)\Bigr )^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}\\  = & \int _ X \Bigl (C\omega _1+\omega _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(C\varphi +\psi )\Bigr )^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}. \end{split}  \] Both sides are polynomials in $C$. Comparing the constant terms gives FF05887CF686 16.9.46 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \omega _{2,\psi _ i}^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}=\int _ X \omega _{2,\psi }^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}. \end{equation} Therefore, 2 follows if $\psi _ i\geq \psi $ for each $i$ by 16.9.7 . Next we prove the general case. By the direction that we already proved, we know that $\varphi _ i+\psi \xrightarrow {d_{S}} \varphi +\psi $. By proposition 16.9.42 , we have \[  \varphi _ i+(\psi _ i\lor \psi )\xrightarrow {d_{S}} \varphi +\psi .  \] It follows from the special case above that $\psi _ i\lor \psi \xrightarrow {d_{S}}\psi $. It follows from ( 16.9.46 ) and corollary 16.9.33 that 2 holds. 2 + 3 $\implies $ 1 . This is similar. $\square$

title: Equation 16.9.46
text: FF05887CF686 16.9.46 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \omega _{2,\psi _ i}^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}=\int _ X \omega _{2,\psi }^ j\wedge \omega _2^{n-j}. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 16.9.47
text: Proposition 16.9.47 . A2F662346EB5 Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, decreasing with respect to the $P$-partial order. Assume that there is $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 17876C1905F0 16.9.48 \begin{equation}  \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by our assumption, $(P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i])_{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net. By the continuity of non-pluripolar masses corollary 16.9.13 , we have \[  \lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]}^ n=\lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Replacing $I$ by a tail, we may therefore assume that $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for each $i\in I$. Since $\varphi _ i\sim _ P P_\theta [\varphi _ i]$, replacing $\varphi _ i$ by $P_\theta [\varphi _ i]$ does not change its $d_ S$-class by proposition 16.9.6 . We may assume that each $\varphi _ i$ is model and $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is decreasing. In this case, by proposition 16.4.4 , the potential \[  \psi \coloneqq \inf _{i\in I} \varphi _ i  \] is model in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\lim _{i\in I} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, by corollary 16.9.14 , we find $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi $. In particular, $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ by proposition 16.9.6 . Therefore, \[  \psi =P_{\theta }[\psi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] Therefore, ( 16.9.48 ) follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 16.9.49
text: Theorem 16.9.49 . 88D575A3C46A The map \[  P_{\theta }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}  \] is continuous with respect to $d_ S$. Proof. Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}$ be a sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We want to show that 6.73 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} We may assume that the $\varphi _ i$'s and $\varphi $ are all model potentials by proposition 16.9.6 . By proposition 16.9.17 and corollary 16.9.39 , we may assume that $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is either increasing or decreasing. In the increasing case, we apply proposition 16.6.30 and corollary 16.9.12 , while in the decreasing case, we apply proposition 16.6.29 , proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 . $\square$

title: Lemma 16.9.50
text: Lemma 16.9.50 . CC25BA40D9FE Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. As $\epsilon \to 0$ (from both sides), we have 11D8415D35F8 16.9.51 \begin{equation}  V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }\xlongrightarrow {d_ S}V_{\theta }. \end{equation} Proof. There are two assertions to prove, as detailed in the two steps. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\epsilon \to 0+$. In this case ( 16.9.51 ) means \[  V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }\xlongrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}V_{\theta }  \] as $\epsilon \to 0+$. So thanks to corollary 16.9.14 and proposition 16.4.4 , it suffices to prove the following: E3D4ADBA54B9 16.9.52 \begin{equation}  \inf _{\epsilon >0} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta } \right]. \end{equation} First observe that \[  V_{\theta }=\inf _{\epsilon >0} V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }.  \] In fact, the $\leq $ direction is trivial. As for the reverse inequality, it suffices to observe that the right-hand side lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Therefore, due to proposition 16.4.4 , \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ X \left( \theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Therefore, for all $\epsilon >0$ small enough, we can find $\eta _{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon \omega )$ and $a_{\epsilon }>0$ decreasing to $0$ so that \[  (1-a_\epsilon )V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } + a_\epsilon \eta _\epsilon \leq V_{\theta }.  \] Therefore, thanks to proposition 16.4.2 , \[  (1-a_\epsilon )P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ V_{\theta +\epsilon \omega } \right] + a_\epsilon P_{\theta +\omega }\left[\eta _\epsilon \right] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\left[V_{\theta }\right].  \] Since the envelopes $P_{\theta +\omega }[\eta _\epsilon ]$ have supremum $0$, they are uniformly bounded in $L^1$ by proposition 5.17.3 ; hence $a_\epsilon P_{\theta +\omega }[\eta _\epsilon ]\to 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $\epsilon \to 0$ and using proposition 5.14.6 , we conclude ( 16.9.52 ). Step 2 . We then handle the case where $\epsilon \to 0-$. In this case, ( 16.9.51 ) simply means \[  V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}V_{\theta }  \] as $\epsilon \to 0+$. But this follows from corollary 16.9.12 if we can prove 4D05EB795FC2 16.9.53 \begin{equation}  \operatorname *{sup}_{\epsilon >0}{}\! {}^{*} V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }=V_{\theta }, \end{equation} where we understand that $\epsilon $ is small enough so that $\theta -\epsilon \omega $ represents a big cohomology class. Since $\{ \theta \} $ is big, we can find $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ so that \[  \varphi \leq 0,\quad \theta _{\varphi }\geq \delta \omega  \] for some $\delta >0$. For a small $\epsilon >0$, we then have \[  \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \left(1-\frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\right)V_{\theta }+ \frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\varphi \right)\geq \epsilon \omega .  \] Therefore, \[  \left(1-\frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\right)V_{\theta }+ \frac{\epsilon }{\delta }\varphi \leq V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }.  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, we then find \[  V_{\theta }\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{\epsilon >0}{}\! {}^{*} V_{\theta -\epsilon \omega }.  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, hence ( 16.9.53 ) is established. $\square$

title: 18.1 $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities
text: The class of $\mathcal I$-good singularities is the central object of this part of the book. These are the singularities for which the pluripotential-theoretic and multiplier-ideal notions of singularity type agree. Equivalently, they are the positive-mass potentials for which the ordinary model envelope and the $\mathcal I$-model envelope coincide, or for which the non-pluripolar mass equals the volume defined through multiplier ideals. The starting point is the characterization theorem theorem 18.1.2 . For $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, it shows that the following three conditions are equivalent: $\varphi $ lies in the $d_ S$-closure of potentials with analytic singularities; the mass-volume identity \[  \int _ X\theta _\varphi ^ n=\operatorname{vol}\theta _\varphi  \] holds; and \[  P_\theta [\varphi ]=P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] After establishing this characterization, the chapter develops the basic calculus of $\mathcal I$-good singularities. We prove stability under natural operations, including linear combinations and suprema, and record the main examples: analytic singularities, $\mathcal I$-model potentials, elementary metrics, and toric potentials. These closure properties are used repeatedly in later chapters, especially for traces, test curves and non-Archimedean potentials. The next part of the chapter introduces mixed volumes for singular currents. The definition is first made in positive-volume classes by replacing each current with its $\mathcal I$-model envelope, and is then extended by Kähler perturbation. We prove symmetry, multilinearity, monotonicity, birational invariance, log-concavity and continuity with respect to $d_ S$-convergence. The final section proves the asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula theorem 18.1.46 . For a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L,h)$ on a connected compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, the theorem identifies \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(h^ k)\right)  \] with the volume of the Chern current of $h$. This result is the main algebraic manifestation of $\mathcal I$-goodness. It will be used later in the construction of partial Okounkov bodies and in the study of partial Bergman kernels.

title: 18.1.1 The notion of $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Theorem 18.1.2 . F9085BB700B0 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: 9DB4D39DE89B There exists a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; 08242C3CBB6E we have 6F6AB284E081 18.1.3 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }; \end{equation} 0129149C02C9 we have 4730AA1B3287 18.1.4 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} In 1 , we can in addition require that each $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current. Moreover, if $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, one may take the sequence in 1 to be any quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Since $(\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),d_ S)$ is a pseudometric space, in 1 we can also replace the word sequence by net . Recall that according to corollary 16.6.21 and proposition 16.6.18 , one direction of ( 18.1.3 ) and ( 18.1.4 ) always holds: \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi },\quad P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . By theorem 16.9.30 , we have \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0.  \] We may therefore assume that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n>0$ for all $j \geq 1$. It follows from proposition 16.6.22 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}  \] for any $j\geq 1$. Using theorem 16.9.57 , we conclude ( 18.1.3 ). 2 $\iff $ 3 . By definition, \[  \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }= \int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}}^ n.  \] Moreover, $\varphi -\sup _ X\varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$. Thus, if 2 holds, theorem 16.3.15 gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$; the reverse inequality follows from proposition 16.6.18 . Conversely, if 3 holds, then 2 follows from proposition 16.3.10 . 3 $\implies $ 1 . Note that the condition in 1 characterizes the closure of analytic singularities in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Step 1 . We first assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. We will prove the following more general result in this case: Without assuming 3 , $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ always lies in the closure of analytic singularities. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We will show that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Let \[  \psi =\inf _{j\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j].  \] Since $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j$ for all $j>0$, we have \[  \varphi -\sup _ X\varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]  \] for all $j$, and hence \[  \varphi -\sup _ X\varphi \leq \psi .  \] In particular, $\int _ X\theta _\psi ^ n>0$. Now proposition 16.9.6 , proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 give \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi .  \] Moreover, observe that $\psi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model by proposition 16.6.29 and proposition 16.6.22 . Hence, if $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal I}\psi $, then \[  P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}=P_\theta [\psi ]_{\mathcal I}=\psi .  \] So it suffices to show that $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal I}\psi $. It only remains to argue that $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi $. For this purpose, take $\lambda >0$. We need to show that \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ).  \] By the strong openness theorem 5.16.21 , we may take $\lambda '>\lambda $ such that $\mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )=\mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \psi )$. It follows from the definition of the quasi-equisingular approximation that \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi )  \] for large enough $j$, where the first inclusion uses $\psi \leq P_\theta [\varphi _ j]$ and $P_\theta [\varphi _ j]\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi _ j$. Our assertion follows. It follows from the proof that we may take $\varphi _ j$ so that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for all $j\geq 1$. Step 2 . We handle the general case. Assume 3 holds. By 13.13.47 , we can find $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ so that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. We let \[  \psi _ j=(1-j^{-1})\varphi +j^{-1}\psi  \] for each $j\in \mathbb {Z}_{>1}$. Then $(\psi _ j)_ j$ is an increasing sequence converging almost everywhere to $\varphi $. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\psi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]  \] by proposition 16.6.30 , corollary 16.9.12 . From Step 1, we know that each $P_{\theta }[\psi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}$ lies in the closure of analytic singularities, hence so is $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\sim _ P \varphi $. Therefore, 1 follows. $\square$ Definition 18.1.5 . AE67290569F6 We say a potential $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good if for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we have A9EABC721827 18.1.6 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} Remark 18.1.7 . 11FBD440944D In view of theorem 18.1.2 and corollary 16.6.21 , the failure of $\mathcal{I}$-goodness of a given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ can be characterized using the difference between the volume and the mass. We therefore introduce \[  \mathrm{Defect}(\theta _{\varphi })\coloneqq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] An immediate question is to verify that definition 18.1.5 is independent of the choice of $\theta $. Lemma 18.1.8 . 22BB587E13F8 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: 9755050D9C5E $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$; D166FB4A811A $P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . By theorem 18.1.2 , we can find a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta }}\varphi $. By corollary 16.9.36 , we have $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}\varphi $. Therefore, by theorem 18.1.2 again, 2 holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . It follows that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n =&  \sum _{i=0}^ n\binom {n}{i}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}\\  <&  \sum _{i=0}^ n\binom {n}{i}\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}\\  =&  \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n \\  \leq & \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n. \end{aligned}  \] So 2 fails as well. $\square$ Corollary 18.1.9 . 4662D2032EC0 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Then $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. This is proved in proposition 16.6.22 . In particular, the potential in example 5.20.12 is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Example 18.1.11 . E3DE8BCA0BA1 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ 1 be an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Example 18.1.12 . 4C522F2A65F0 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class, and let $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta )$. F1CD22EF1353 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathbb {R}_{\geq 0}$ with limit $0$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Assume that $\varphi =\inf _ j \varphi _ j$. The choice of $\epsilon $ is irrelevant due to corollary 16.9.36 . Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 and example 18.1.11 , we may replace $\theta $ by $\theta +C\omega $ for some large constant $C>0$ and assume that $\varphi ,\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta -\omega )$ for all $j\geq 1$. This implies \[  P_{\theta +C\omega }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\bigr ]=P_{\theta +C\omega }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\bigr ]_{\mathcal I}=P_{\theta +C\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Thus the old and new targets are $P$-equivalent in the enlarged class, and proposition 16.9.6 , corollary 16.9.36 shows that condition 1 is unchanged. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This is already proved in the proof of theorem 18.1.2 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . This follows from theorem 16.9.59 . $\square$ Corollary 18.1.15 . 36E768E33AFB Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $. Then $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of the $\pi ^*\theta $-psh function $\pi ^*\varphi $. This result is by no means obvious from the definition of quasi-equisingular approximations. Proof. Let $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ and $\omega $ be as in definition 6.17.5 , so that $\epsilon _ j\searrow 0$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$ for all $j$. Choose a Kähler form $\tilde\omega $ on $Y$ and a constant $C>0$ such that $\pi ^*\omega \leq C\tilde\omega $. Then \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\pi ^*\theta +C\epsilon _ j\tilde\omega ).  \] Moreover, the sequence $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing, has analytic singularities, and decreases to $\pi ^*\varphi $. It remains to verify the quasi-equisingular condition definition 6.17.5 4 . Fix a constant $A>0$. Then $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is also a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ with respect to $\theta +A\omega $. Since $\theta _{\varphi }+A\omega $ is a Kähler current, corollary 18.1.14 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta +A\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Viewing the convergence in a fixed enlarged background class, pulling back and using corollary 16.9.11 , proposition 16.6.10 , we get \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*P_{\theta +A\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I} =P_{\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )}[\pi ^*\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The domination $\pi ^*\omega \leq C\tilde\omega $ also gives \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}\bigl (Y,\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )+C\epsilon _ j\tilde\omega \bigr ),  \] so the preceding convergence is in the setting of corollary 18.1.14 on $Y$. The potential $\pi ^*\varphi $ has positive mass with respect to $\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )$ by the bimeromorphic invariance of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.13.4 . Applying corollary 18.1.14 again on $Y$ shows that $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ satisfies the quasi-equisingular condition definition 6.17.5 4 for $\pi ^*\varphi $. Combining this with the first paragraph proves the assertion with respect to $\pi ^*\theta $. $\square$

By corollary 16.9.36 , we have $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\omega }}\varphi $. Therefore, by theorem 18.1.2 again, 2 holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Suppose that 1 fails, so that \[  \int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n< \int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n.  \] Since $\varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}\leq \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}}^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}  \] for all $i=0,\ldots ,n$, and the inequality is strict for $i=n$. It follows that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n =&  \sum _{i=0}^ n\binom {n}{i}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}\\  <&  \sum _{i=0}^ n\binom {n}{i}\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ i\wedge \omega ^{n-i}\\  =&  \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n \\  \leq & \int _ X (\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n. \end{aligned}  \] So 2 fails as well. $\square$

title: Corollary 18.1.9
text: Corollary 18.1.9 . 4662D2032EC0 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net of $\mathcal{I}$-good potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. By adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, and using 18.1.8 , corollary 16.9.36 , we may assume that $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $j\in I$. It follows from theorem 18.1.2 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}  \] for all $j\in I$. Taking limit with respect to $j$ with the help of theorem 16.9.57 , we conclude that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] Therefore, by theorem 18.1.2 again, we find that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. $\square$

title: Example 18.1.10
text: Example 18.1.10 . 12795171A873 Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ has analytic singularities. Then $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. This is proved in proposition 16.6.22 . In particular, the potential in example 5.20.12 is $\mathcal{I}$-good.

title: Example 18.1.11
text: Example 18.1.11 . E3DE8BCA0BA1 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ 1 be an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Then $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. In particular, $V_{\theta }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. 1. ↩ It is not known to us whether the same holds when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass.

title: Example 18.1.12
text: Example 18.1.12 . 4C522F2A65F0 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class, and let $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta )$. Then $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. In fact, since $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=V_{\theta }$, we deduce that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=V_{\theta }$ as well. In particular, the potential in example 16.3.22 is $\mathcal{I}$-good.

title: Example 18.1.13
text: Example 18.1.13 . 6212EEC14B63 The potential in example 16.8.19 is not $\mathcal{I}$-good. In fact, since all Lelong numbers of $\varphi $ vanish, we know that $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}0$, hence \[  P_{2\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=0.  \] On the other hand, \[  \int _ X (2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1=\int _ X \omega <\int _ X (2\omega ),  \] where $(2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^1$ is understood in the non-pluripolar sense.

title: Corollary 18.1.14
text: Corollary 18.1.14 . F1CD22EF1353 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathbb {R}_{\geq 0}$ with limit $0$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Consider a decreasing sequence $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$, where each $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$ is a potential with analytic singularities. Assume that $\varphi =\inf _ j \varphi _ j$. Then the following are equivalent: 610A978F4B80 $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ 2 , and DCDEC3669C76 $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $. 2. ↩ Just to be sure, this means $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_{S,\theta +\epsilon \omega }}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ for any $\epsilon >0$. The choice of $\epsilon $ is irrelevant due to corollary 16.9.36 . Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 and example 18.1.11 , we may replace $\theta $ by $\theta +C\omega $ for some large constant $C>0$ and assume that $\varphi ,\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta -\omega )$ for all $j\geq 1$. Here the limit in 1 is unchanged by this replacement. Indeed, $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$ is $\mathcal I$-model, hence $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.11 . This implies \[  P_{\theta +C\omega }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\bigr ]=P_{\theta +C\omega }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\bigr ]_{\mathcal I}=P_{\theta +C\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Thus the old and new targets are $P$-equivalent in the enlarged class, and proposition 16.9.6 , corollary 16.9.36 shows that condition 1 is unchanged. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This is already proved in the proof of theorem 18.1.2 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . This follows from theorem 16.9.59 . $\square$

title: Corollary 18.1.15
text: Corollary 18.1.15 . 36E768E33AFB Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $. Then $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of the $\pi ^*\theta $-psh function $\pi ^*\varphi $. Proof. Let $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ and $\omega $ be as in definition 6.17.5 , so that $\epsilon _ j\searrow 0$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$ for all $j$. Choose a Kähler form $\tilde\omega $ on $Y$ and a constant $C>0$ such that $\pi ^*\omega \leq C\tilde\omega $. Then \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\pi ^*\theta +C\epsilon _ j\tilde\omega ).  \] Moreover, the sequence $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing, has analytic singularities, and decreases to $\pi ^*\varphi $. It remains to verify the quasi-equisingular condition definition 6.17.5 4 . Fix a constant $A>0$. Then $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is also a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ with respect to $\theta +A\omega $. Since $\theta _{\varphi }+A\omega $ is a Kähler current, corollary 18.1.14 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta +A\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Viewing the convergence in a fixed enlarged background class, pulling back and using corollary 16.9.11 , proposition 16.6.10 , we get \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*P_{\theta +A\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I} =P_{\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )}[\pi ^*\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The domination $\pi ^*\omega \leq C\tilde\omega $ also gives \[  \pi ^*\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}\bigl (Y,\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )+C\epsilon _ j\tilde\omega \bigr ),  \] so the preceding convergence is in the setting of corollary 18.1.14 on $Y$. The potential $\pi ^*\varphi $ has positive mass with respect to $\pi ^*(\theta +A\omega )$ by the bimeromorphic invariance of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.13.4 . Applying corollary 18.1.14 again on $Y$ shows that $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ satisfies the quasi-equisingular condition definition 6.17.5 4 for $\pi ^*\varphi $. Combining this with the first paragraph proves the assertion with respect to $\pi ^*\theta $. $\square$

title: 18.1.16 Properties of $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. We show that $\mathcal{I}$-goodness is preserved by a number of natural operations. Proposition 18.1.17 . AC437613D2C1 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be $\mathcal{I}$-good and $\lambda >0$. Then the following potentials are all $\mathcal{I}$-good: DF6905DB50A6 $\varphi +\psi $; 0771DD6805B8 $\varphi \lor \psi $; 51229C9B0C0E $\lambda \varphi $. Proof. Take a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. It follows from theorem 18.1.2 that there are sequences $(\varphi _ j)_ j,(\psi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ and $\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi $. By theorem 16.9.45 , proposition 16.9.42 , we have \[  \varphi _ j+\psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi +\psi ,\quad \varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \lor \psi .  \] By proposition 5.18.2 , the potentials $\varphi _ j+\psi _ j$ and $\varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j$ have analytic singularities. So $\varphi +\psi $ and $\varphi \lor \psi $ are $\mathcal{I}$-good by theorem 18.1.2 . On the other hand, 16.9.41 gives \[  \lambda \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\lambda \varphi .  \] Here the convergence is understood in the scaled class. So by theorem 18.1.2 , in order to show that $\lambda \varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, it suffices to show that $\lambda \varphi _ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. In other words, we may assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. We may further assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. In this case, take a decreasing sequence of rational numbers $\lambda _ j\searrow \lambda $. Take a sufficiently large Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\lambda _ j\varphi ,\lambda \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$ for any $j$. Then observe that \[  \lambda \varphi =\operatorname *{sup}_{j>0}{}\! {}^{*} \lambda _ j \varphi .  \] Therefore, $\lambda _ j\varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S} \lambda \varphi $ by corollary 16.9.12 . Each $\lambda _ j \varphi $ has analytic singularities, and hence is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 18.1.10 . Therefore, $\lambda \varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by theorem 18.1.2 . $\square$ Example 18.1.18 . 3689F6A0A9EC Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Elementary metrics on $L$ are defined in definition 16.8.20 . Let $h$ be an elementary metric on $L$. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. This is a direct consequence of proposition 18.1.17 and example 18.1.10 , and the fact that $\mathcal{I}$-goodness depends only on the $P$-singularity type. Proposition 18.1.19 . FD679E0ECD3D Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a non-empty family of $\mathcal{I}$-good potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that this family is locally uniformly bounded from above. Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{j\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. After adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $j\in I$. When $I$ is finite, this result follows from proposition 18.1.17 . When $I$ is infinite, by Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 , we may assume that $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ j$ and using proposition 18.1.17 , we may assume that the sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is increasing. In this case, as shown in corollary 16.9.12 , \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\operatorname *{sup}_{ i\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i.  \] Therefore, $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by corollary 18.1.9 . $\square$

title: Example 18.1.18
text: Example 18.1.18 . 3689F6A0A9EC Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Elementary metrics on $L$ are defined in definition 16.8.20 . Let $h$ be an elementary metric on $L$. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. This is a direct consequence of proposition 18.1.17 and example 18.1.10 , and the fact that $\mathcal{I}$-goodness depends only on the $P$-singularity type.

title: Proposition 18.1.19
text: Proposition 18.1.19 . FD679E0ECD3D Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a non-empty family of $\mathcal{I}$-good potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that this family is locally uniformly bounded from above. Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{j\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. After adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $j\in I$. When $I$ is finite, this result follows from proposition 18.1.17 . When $I$ is infinite, by Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 , we may assume that $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ j$ and using proposition 18.1.17 , we may assume that the sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is increasing. In this case, as shown in corollary 16.9.12 , \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\operatorname *{sup}_{ i\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i.  \] Therefore, $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by corollary 18.1.9 . $\square$
